rr.setPlaneState

The engine's `_planeState`, memoised on the list and the selection; a selected frame's natives are found by their home.

planeAccepts()At a drag's start: aims the drag plane at the selection and posts what it lacks; false sends the drag down the per-step render path.§9
rr.planeAccepts

Ends a plane still landing from the last drop first. False with no store, a view that is neither plates nor a settle, no selected ink on screen, or `forcePerStepDrag` set; a large or interleaved selection is not refused, the plane merges runs or cuts coarser instead (`MovePlane._cut`). The refusal is kept in `_noPlaneDrag`, which stops `_planeIdle` aiming a plane under that drag.

  • Called from the engine's `_beginHold`; on false the engine takes no hold.
_planeViewOk(v)Whether a view can carry a drag plane: plates mode, or a settled view.§9
rr._planeViewOk

Whether a view can carry a drag plane: plates mode, or a settled view.

dragLight()Whether a drag step may skip the list build: the plane has layers, the view carries it, and it is not landing.§9
rr.dragLight

`selection.js` asks it on each drag step while the engine holds the move; true means the step is a camera frame only (the list build it skips is 120–240 ms on the Magnum Opus, per the caller's comment).

planeCap (getter)The most plates a drag plane may pin, both its levels together: 40 on a desktop, 24 on a phone, or a test's override.§9
rr.planeCap

The most plates a drag plane may pin, both its levels together: 40 on a desktop, 24 on a phone, or a test's override.

_aimPlane(v)Keeps the drag plane aimed at the current selection and view, re-pins its plates in the store and posts what they lack; false when the plane is refused.§9
rr._aimPlane

Under the `forcePerStepDrag` test hook it ends any plane and returns false. Otherwise it pulls the selection through `_planeFn` and calls `MovePlane.aim`; every old tag the plane no longer carries — all of them after a reset or a refusal, a renamed layer after a re-cut — is dropped from the queue and the store. Pins the plane's keys with `setPlanePins`, or clears them on a refusal. After a post it calls `onPlaneAimed` (the engine's ladder check), because the new pins can push the ladder's plates out.

_planeStep(v)Each camera step: follows a live drag with the plane, ends a landing that is done, or keeps an idle plane ready; then picks the level to draw and tells the layer.§9
rr._planeStep

Under a drag, a plane with no layers, at another frame, or in a view that cannot carry it is lost (`_losePlane`); otherwise it moves by the pointer's displacement from the drag's start and re-posts any plane plate staled mid-drag.

  • The drawn level is `MovePlane.pick`'s: the main level whole, else the quick one whole, else the selected layers of either alone (partial). Under a drag with none of those and no stopgap yet, `_planeStopgap` rasters a small selection here. Only a whole level sets `_dragOmit`, which makes every other pack leave the selection out; while partial the plates still show the ink where it was. Counts the steps drawn not ready, partial and from the quick level.
_losePlane()Ends the plane under a live drag and tells the engine, which releases its hold so the drag renders each step.§9
rr._losePlane

Counted in `planeStats.lost`; sets `_noPlaneDrag` so no new plane is aimed under that drag.

_planeIdle()With nothing dragged, aims the plane at the view once the published view has stayed unchanged for 150 ms and the layer is not holding a zoom.§9
rr._planeIdle

Unchanged means the same frame, quantum, zoom and view revision, a pan included, with no settle about to publish and no quantum hold; the code records 938 plates posted over a 60-step pan in Kobin's Chrome when each pan step re-cut the layers. A plane aimed at another frame or quantum is ended at once, and so is any plane while the layer holds a zoom, whose hold pins its own set. Otherwise one timer re-checks after `PLANE_QUIET_MS`.

  • Does nothing under `forcePerStepDrag`, after a refused drag, or during a drag. Also called from `_deliver`, since a settle's publish arrives without a camera step.
_planeLanded(v)Whether a landing plane can go: every cell it covers has a fresh plate again, the camera left its frame or quantum, or `MOVE_HOLD_MS` passed.§9
rr._planeLanded

A timeout is counted in `planeStats.landTimeouts`.

_endPlane()Takes the plane down: records the landing's length, clears its timer, drops its plates and pins, resets it and tells the layer.§9
rr._endPlane

The next camera step or `_planeIdle` aims a new one.

endMove(why)The engine's end of a drag: a drop lands the plane until the plates under it are fresh; any other end takes it down.§9
rr.endMove

Clears `_noPlaneDrag` and `_dragOmit` first, so the drop's render packs the moved ink. A drop lands the plane only when it was drawing the drag from a whole level (`cur` set and not partial, the quick level included); a timer ends the landing at `MOVE_HOLD_MS` + 20 ms and recomposes. A drop drawn partial or from the stopgap, a cancel, a delete or a deselect ends it at once.

  • Called from the engine's `_dropHold`.
_abandon(why)Reports every in-flight job as dropped so the store frees its keys; used at teardown only.§9
rr._abandon

It frees no worker capacity: an abandoned job holds its slot until its own answer arrives (`rasterWorkerReport().heldSlots`). Not on the render path, because a quantum change already bumps the dead keys' epochs, and freeing them there would re-post plates the camera has just left.

destroy()Tears down the raster path: abandons in-flight jobs, empties the queue, clears the timers, stops the pool and listeners, destroys the layers, then the SVG base.§9
rr.destroy

The abandon comes first: a job never reported leaves its keys in the store's in-flight map and `want` reads them as in flight rather than missing, a permanent hole.

endLive()Pen-up: releases the live stroke's model now and keeps its SVG path on screen until the plates under it are fresh.§9
rr.endLive

On the plates or settle path, with a store, a live path and points, it records the stroke's box (half its width added), its frame and a limit of `LIVE_HOLD_MS` (3,000 ms, extended while its plates are on the way) in `_liveHeld`, and arms the timer; every later pack paints the stroke. Anywhere else the base `endLive` removes the path at once: the sync path rasters the stroke in the pen-up frame itself.

_armLiveTimer()Arms one timer for all held live paths, at the earliest limit; it releases what it can and re-arms while any path is held.§9
rr._armLiveTimer

A release is followed by `update()`, so Two redraws without the path.

addLive(o)Starts the live stroke's SVG path, first re-centring the overlay origin on the view and re-syncing the world transform if it moved.§9
rr.addLive

The origin is one object with one writer, this method, and a new choice is a new object, because `_selDecide` caches on the origin's identity. Re-syncing here is what puts a stroke begun after a pan or zoom under the pen instead of offset by the origin's move until pen-up.

_syncWorldTransform(view)Sets the SVG world group's scale and translation from the published view, with the overlay origin folded in, so the live stroke sits on the composed ink.§9
rr._syncWorldTransform

The view maps a frame point to `p·k + tx` in device px and the SVG is in CSS px, so both are divided by the view's dpr. Without a view (or its dpr) it falls back to the base's camera transform.

syncWorld(view)The base world sync and overlay tail, timed into the `ovl.tail` slot.§9
rr.syncWorld

Both `render` and `syncCameraOnly` reach the tail here, so one bracket times both and neither counts twice.

`render` finds the row open and does not open a second; a caller that skips this gets the row opened in `render`.

rr.noteList

Charges the engine's own list-build time to the `eng.list` slot.

render(list, frame)A full frame on the raster path: records the list, runs the camera step (mapping, plates, compose, posts) and syncs the SVG world and overlays.§9
rr.render

The document-event drain is the engine's and runs just before this call, because `_buildList` itself emits events the drain must see. Records the widest unfitted fat stroke for the idle fitter and sets `_hasFat`. Returns false: there are no ink groups to reorder.

rr.syncCameraOnly

The drain is called here rather than at the engine's call sites because `selection.js` calls this method too, and a compose there would otherwise use plates a queued event has invalidated. No list build and no overlay rebuild.

Ends a job id in the store, freeing its in-flight keys.

_frameStep(list)One camera step: culls for the chord estimate, gets the published view, drops dead quanta's strips, then either rasters in sync mode or wants, composes and posts plates.§9
rr._frameStep

Plates path, in order: `store.want(view)` (the visible pins, after `frameFor` has added its own), the plane step, `compose(hits)`, the held-live release, and a post of the misses. The sync path ends or loses the plane, rasters on this thread, releases held paths and gives the layer the measured core time.

  • `frameFor` can post inside itself; that time is subtracted from `eng.view` because it is already counted in `eng.pack` and `xfer.out`. Returns the published view, which the overlays are handed.
_postPlane(pl)Posts the plates each plane layer lacks, one post per layer, skipping cells already fresh or in flight.§9
rr._postPlane

A layer's cells are a list, not a range, so each missing cell is asked of the store as a one-cell unpinned `want`. Fresh and in-flight cells are checked directly and never reach `want`, which evicts: this runs on every drag step. Returns the strips posted.

_dropPlaneTags(tags)Removes a plane's layer tags from the queue and the store.§9

Each tag is a pseudo-quantum (`z<n>_<quantum>_<members hash>`) no other request reads, so its queued strips go through `dropQueued` and its plates through `dropQuantum`.

snapshotJob(o)Rasters one plate of any frame and rect off camera, for the Scenes panel, and resolves with its bitmap; the plate cache is never touched.§14
rr.snapshotJob

Each call has its own quantum string (`t1`, `t2`, …), so no cached plate is reused at a zoom it was not rastered at, and snapshots never drop each other's queued strips. The rect lands on plate (0, 0) through an `offset` folded into each item at pack time; an offset at or past the coordinate bound is rejected before any work.

  • Priority 4. Resolves null for an empty plate and the raw pixels where there is no `createImageBitmap`; rejects on a drop or an abort, and an abort also drops the queued strip. Called by `sceneOps.snapshotView`.

raster/PicturePyramid.js 1,715 lines

The ink canvas composed from the picture pyramid (DESIGN.md §9, A3): each camera step publishes one view, plans every screen cell from one freshness-first rule list, and draws the plan directly or through one surface; it runs the rest render and the partial re-renders, holds a pen-up's results for one group commit, and keeps the paper, blur and older integrals. It posts nothing: requests leave through `onRequest`.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§

raster/PyramidStore.js 476 lines

The pyramid's plate cache (DESIGN.md §9): level, rest and plane records under `level.js`'s keys, each with the G its job was packed at. A result lands iff its G is newer (rule 1); a plate is exact iff its G is at least its cell's `dirtySince` (rule 2). LRU by bytes with the drawn set, the plane and the protected classes evicted last; the in-flight map; the hidden-tab release.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§

raster/level.js 168 lines

The pyramid's level arithmetic: a level ℓ is the integer zoom Z(ℓ) = 2^(ℓS), the view draws from the level whose stretch lies in its band, and a plate of one frame's level is a plate of another frame's by integer arithmetic on the cell digits, never a float affine. The keys of level, rest and plane plates.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§

raster/jobQueue.js 299 lines

The one queue in front of the worker pool (DESIGN.md §9): typed jobs by priority — rest and patches, the view, the plane, cuts, the prefetch, thumbnails — cut into strips dealt round-robin from the attention point; a strip whose purpose moved on or whose cells are exact is dropped; one worker kept for cuts; a pack budget per frame or per task.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§

raster/prefetch.js 139 lines

What the pyramid fetches before the view needs it, as priority-4 jobs: the near coarser levels from the live table, the far levels and a crossing's target through budgeted snapshots, the ring at rest — no more than the cache can hold beside what is pinned. Nothing while a report sends.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§

raster/plate.js 31 lines

The plate grid: 512-device-pixel squares measured in pixels, the quarter-octave zoom quanta, and the plate cache key. No state and no imports.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
plateRange(win, Zq)The inclusive range of plates a frame-unit window touches at zoom `Zq`.§9
plt.plateRange

The grid is anchored at the frame origin, so a screen W device px wide touches floor(W/512) + 1 or + 2 columns.

raster/rasterPack.js 1,324 lines

The main thread's half of the raster path: turns the render list into jobs for strips of plates, from memoised item entries (the box without `res`, the copied geometry, stroke bands per zoom quantum), families in the SVG renderer's paint order, the cull, each family's union routing and sign, colour and quantised fade. It also gives the visible chord estimate the main-thread-or-worker switch reads (DESIGN.md §9).

Zeroes the packer's counters, keeping the memo's live byte and entry counts.

Warns on the console once per distinct fault a session, counting every occurrence in `packStats.logs`.

rpk.setPackBudget

The default is 10 MiB; only the tests change it.

packMemoBytes()The bytes the pack memo holds now.§15
rpk.packMemoBytes

The bytes the pack memo holds now.

clearPackCaches()Drops every memoised entry, parsed colour and pre-pass, and the logged-once set, so the next pack starts cold.
rpk.clearPackCaches

Each entry is marked dropped, so a family still holding one refills. The tests and the bench probes call it between runs.

touch(item, e)Moves an entry to the young end of the memo's least-recently-used order.
rpk.touch

Moves an entry to the young end of the memo's least-recently-used order.

evict()Drops the least recently used memo entries until the memo is within its byte budget, keeping at least one.
rpk.evict

An evicted entry is marked `dropped`, so the families holding it refill and `charge` stops counting it. The memo is a Map, not a WeakMap, because it has to be walked to be capped.

charge(e, bytes)Adds bytes to a live entry and to the memo's total, then evicts; an entry already evicted is not charged.
rpk.charge

An entry evicted mid-pack is still used by the job being packed, and charging it would add bytes nothing could subtract.

rpk.geomRef

The array an item's geometry lives in, a shape's loops, a fill's polys or a stroke's points: part of a memo entry's identity.

build(item, cfg)Builds an item's pack entry by walking its geometry once: its box, each sub-chain's box and signed area, and whether its own rings need the union pass.§9
rpk.build

Hands the item to `buildShape`, `buildFill` or `buildStroke`; a shape or fill not refused then gets `e.union` from `ringsNeedUnion` and `e.area`, the sum of its rings' signed areas, which `unionSignOf` weighs the family's sign with. No coordinate is copied here; that is `flattenGeom`, on the first plate that keeps the item. The entry records `_ver`, the geometry array and `_outline` as its identity.

scanNums(nums, e)Checks that an item's own numbers are all finite and records their largest magnitude, copying none.
rpk.scanNums

Checks that an item's own numbers are all finite and records their largest magnitude, copying none.

buildShape(item, e)Fills a shape's entry: each loop's box (arc bulges included) and signed area, its numbers checked finite, the whole box and the geometry length.§9
rpk.buildShape

Refused (`e.bad`) when it has no loops, a loop has no box, or a number is not finite. The box must carry each arc's bulge and not only its endpoints, or the family's row range misses rows the arc reaches and the bounded clear leaves them for the next family; `loopBBox` and `loopsBBox` are exact about bulges.

numbersOf(loop)A shape loop's numbers: a `Loop`'s own Float64Array, or the loop itself when it is one; anything else, a plain piece array included, throws.§9
rpk.numbersOf

A shape loop's numbers: a `Loop`'s own Float64Array, or the loop itself when it is one; anything else, a plain piece array included, throws.

buildFill(item, e)Fills a legacy fill's entry: each ring's box and signed area, every point checked finite, the whole box and the geometry length.§9
rpk.buildFill

Refused when it has no rings or a non-finite point.

buildStroke(item, e, cfg)Fills a stroke's entry: a cull box that contains any band it can ship, its points checked finite, and an empty band map; every stroke is a union item.§9
rpk.buildStroke

The box takes in the samples and, for a stroke drawn as a curve (`strokeCurved`), each sample's two spline control points (`controlsFor`), since the curve lies inside them. It is padded by half the pen plus the outline fit's tolerance in frame units, then joined with the control-point box of `_outline` once the fitter has set one: a fitted outline reaches past half the pen, and a cubic lies inside its control points. The band itself is built per zoom quantum by `bandFor`, never here.

  • A non-finite pad or point refuses the item rather than leaving a NaN box, which would be neither culled nor drawn. `e.area` stays 0; a stroke's area is its band's.
finishEntry(e)The shared tail of the shape and fill builders: refuses a non-finite box, records its magnitude and charges the entry's bytes.
rpk.finishEntry

The shared tail of the shape and fill builders: refuses a non-finite box, records its magnitude and charges the entry's bytes.

flattenGeom(e, item)Copies an item's own coordinates into its entry, once, on the first plate that keeps it: loop numbers or ring points, with one ascending offset per sub-chain.§9
rpk.flattenGeom

`subs` counts numbers for the loop grammar and points for flat rings, the layout the core and `validateJob` read. An item the cull rejects is never copied; `packStats.coordsCopied` counts what is.

ringsNeedUnion(boxes, signs, n)Decides whether one item's own rings need the exact-winding union pass: some pair of them overlaps where accumulation would miscount.§9
rpk.ringsNeedUnion

Tests every pair with `pairNeedsUnion`; past 20,000 tests it answers yes and counts `overlapCapped`. The one implementation of the per-item rule: `build` and the oracle test both call it.

boxesOverlap(a, i, b, j)Whether box i of one flat box array and box j of another overlap, touching edges included.
rpk.boxesOverlap

Whether box i of one flat box array and box j of another overlap, touching edges included.

boxContains(a, i, b, j)Whether box i of one flat box array contains box j of another, edges included.
rpk.boxContains

Whether box i of one flat box array contains box j of another, edges included.

pairNeedsUnion(ba, i, sa, bb, j, sb)Whether two rings need the union pass: their boxes overlap and they are wound alike, or wound oppositely without one box nesting inside the other.§9
rpk.pairNeedsUnion

Accumulation is exact for a hole nested in its body (the winding stays 0 or 1), which is most of what the boolean emits; sending those to the union pass was measured at 61 % of a screen's raster time at the phone camera. A zero-area ring has no winding to read and counts as wound alike.

entryFor(item, cfg)An item's memoised pack entry, rebuilt when its `_ver`, its geometry array or its `_outline` has changed.§9
rpk.entryFor

The render list carries the Document's own natives, which an edit mutates in place with a `_ver` bump, while the idle fitter sets `_outline` with none, so all three make the identity. A move must not rebuild: `_buildList` writes `o.res` without a bump (OPEN-FLAGS F55), which is why the box is memoised without `res`. A replaced entry is marked dropped and its bytes subtracted; a hit moves to the young end of the LRU order.

itemBox(item, cfg)An item's box in frame units without `res`, or null when it has no drawable geometry.§9
rpk.itemBox

Read by the tests.

arcChords(ax, ay, bx, by, sweep, tol)Estimates how many chords one arc piece would flatten into at a tolerance, by the core's own radius-free count.§9
rpk.arcChords

1 for a zero or non-finite sweep or a sagitta already within tolerance; otherwise 2 to the power ⌈log2 n⌉, never below the quarter-turn forced splits and capped at depth 24. It takes the whole arc's count where the core takes the worst forced sub-arc's, so it can be one bisection off: it feeds a budget decision, not the tolerance.

itemChords(item, Z, cfg, e)One item's estimated chords at zoom Z, memoised on its entry per zoom quantum.§9
rpk.itemChords

A banded stroke is priced without building its band: a raw native stroke that `strokeCurved` accepts at 8 chords a point of its flattened curve (`CURVE_CHORD_MULT`, `flattenCurve` at the zoom's tolerance), any other at 12 a centreline point (`STROKE_CHORD_MULT`, near the top of the 6.75–14.74 measured); a shape sums its pieces, a line as one and an arc through `arcChords`; a fill counts its ring points. A refused entry is 0.

visibleChords(list, win, Z, cfg, cap, live)The chords the items in the viewport would cost at the exact zoom, stopping at `cap + 1`: what decides between rastering on the main thread and in the workers.§9
rpk.visibleChords

Skips the live stroke and refused items, tests each box with `res` against the viewport in frame units, and sums `itemChords`. The early exit keeps a dense screen to a few dozen items: walking all 77,317 pieces of one measured screen was 8–15 ms against a 4 ms budget. The caller's `cap` must be above `PictureLayer`'s own switch threshold (twice its sync budget), or the exit value reads as a light screen.

bandFor(item, q, Zq, cfg)A stroke's fillable rings at one zoom quantum, flat and wound positive, memoised on its entry by the quantum of `Zq`.§9
rpk.bandFor

Flattened at 1/16 device px: from `_outline` through `flattenLoops` when the stroke has been fitted, else as `strokeStripNear`'s round-joined band along the line the SVG renderer strokes, which is the curve through the samples flattened by `flattenCurve` for a stroke `strokeCurved` accepts and the points themselves for a derived piece. Every ring is wound positive, so two bands of one family never cancel. Returns the geometry, offsets, box and the rings' own area, which the family sign sums; null for a refused entry, a non-stroke or an empty band.

  • The key comes from `Zq`, never from `q` (the parameter is unused): sync and settle requests carry the camera's exact zoom under one `q`, and a band keyed on `q` was measured 1.0 device px off at a 4× sync zoom (OPEN-FLAGS F77). A cached finer band serves a coarser request, never the reverse; at most two quanta are kept per stroke, the older dropped first.
strokeCurved(item)Whether a stroke is drawn as the curve through its samples: a native stroke with more than two, as the SVG renderer strokes it.§9
rpk.strokeCurved

`buildStroke` then takes the spline's control points into the cull box, and `bandFor` bands the flattened curve instead of the sample polyline. A derived piece's points are already flat and are banded as they stand.

flatten(polys)`flattenLoops`'s nested rings as the flat geometry and offset pair, every ring rewritten positive, with the box and the summed area.§9
rpk.flatten

A negative ring is written in reverse. A family accumulates as one nonzero path, so two of its items wound against each other would cancel to a hole that no sign can repair.

fromWriter(r)The round-joined stroke writer's output trimmed to its own length, with its box and the writer's own area, which is never negative.§9
rpk.fromWriter

The round-joined stroke writer's output trimmed to its own length, with its box and the writer's own area, which is never negative.

parseColour(css)Parses a CSS colour string once into 8-bit sRGB [r, g, b]; an unparseable one is black and logged once.§9
rpk.parseColour

Reads #rgb, #rgba, #rrggbb and #rrggbbaa (alpha ignored), `rgb()`/`rgba()` with channels clamped, and six names (`transparent` reads as black). Memoised per string, and the returned array is shared, so a caller must not change it. `RasterRenderer` parses the paper colour with it too.

clamp255(v)Rounds a colour channel and clamps it to 0–255.
rpk.clamp255

Rounds a colour channel and clamps it to 0–255.

fadeQ(item, Zq, dpr, cfg)An item's fade at the plate's quantised zoom, ramped as the SVG renderer's `_fade` ramps it.§9
rpk.fadeQ

1 without a `fadeTag`; otherwise the tag read as px, `fadeTag · (Zq / dpr) / cfg.enter`, ramped from 0 at `cfg.fadeLoPx` (0.15) to 1 at `cfg.cullPx` (0.3). A non-finite reading returns 1, since a NaN alpha would paint nothing. Taken at the quantum, so the fade cannot change inside one.

renderIdOf(item, fade)The family key an item paints under: its edit group's id at full presence, else its own id, the SVG renderer's rule.§9
rpk.renderIdOf

The family key an item paints under: its edit group's id at full presence, else its own id, the SVG renderer's rule.

PlateBinnerA grid of per-plate item lists over one strip's plates; filing an item's box answers whether it touches any plate of the strip.§9
rpk.PlateBinner

`packJob` uses `add`'s answer as its cull; `itemsFor` reads one plate's list, which the tests do.

PlateBinner.constructor(plates, Zq)Creates an empty list for each plate of the strip and records the strip's index extent.
rpk.PlateBinner.constructor

Creates an empty list for each plate of the strip and records the strip's index extent.

add(index, box)Files an item index into every plate of the strip its box touches; returns whether it touched any.§9
rpk.add

The box is in frame units with `res` added, and scaling it by `Zq / 512` gives plate indices. A plate inside the strip's extent but not in it is skipped.

itemsFor(i, j)The item indices filed into one plate, in the order they were added.
rpk.itemsFor

The item indices filed into one plate, in the order they were added.

alloc(pool, ctor, len)A typed array from the buffer pool when there is one, else a fresh one.
rpk.alloc

A typed array from the buffer pool when there is one, else a fresh one.

idOf(x)A small per-object number for the pre-pass key, 0 for null.
rpk.idOf

Held in a WeakMap, so the key names the cfg, the live stroke and the `only`/`omit` sets by identity.

prepassFor(list, q, Zq, dpr, cfg, live, only, omit, offset)The strip-independent half of a pack for one render list and zoom: its families in paint order, each item with its fade, entry and box.§9
rpk.prepassFor

Skips the live stroke, applies `only`/`omit`, drops fully faded items (counted), groups the rest by `renderIdOf`, sorts the families by (z, render id) as the SVG renderer stacks them, and fills each with `famFill`. Memoised in a WeakMap per list, at most four keys a list (zoom, dpr, cfg, live, only, omit, offset), so the strips of one request walk the families once; before it a strip cost 25 ms before its first plate on the Magnum Opus's 15,192 pieces (jsdom).

famFill(f, cfg, offset)Fills a family's drawable items, each with its entry and its box with `res` (plus any pack offset), and resets its union rule and sign.§9
rpk.famFill

A refused entry is counted in `f.rejected` and logged; one whose coordinates pass `COORD_BOUND` is counted and logged but still drawn. The union rule and sign are left for `packJob` to take on the first strip that draws the family.

paintFamilies(list, q, Zq, dpr, cfg, live)The render list's families in the pack's own paint order at one zoom, each with its items' boxes, for a caller that splits a picture by z.§9
rpk.paintFamilies

The pre-pass `packJob` uses, with stale families refilled. `MovePlane` cuts the drag plane's layers on it, so the layers split exactly where the pack paints.

famStale(f)Whether any item of a family has been edited, fitted, evicted from the memo or given a new `res` since `famFill`.§9
rpk.famStale

Whether any item of a family has been edited, fitted, evicted from the memo or given a new `res` since `famFill`.

packJob(list, opts)Packs one strip of plates into the typed-array job the core paints: the families that touch the strip, with their items' geometry, boxes, colour, alpha, flags and union sign.§9
rpk.packJob

From the pre-pass, each family is refilled if stale, its items culled by the binner (no coordinate copied for one that misses), and, for a family with anything on the strip, its union rule (`familyUnion`) and sign (`unionSignOf`) taken once over all its items. Then each kept item's geometry is found (`geomOf`: the band for a stroke, the copied loops or rings otherwise), the arrays are allocated once from the pool, and each item is written: family index, spans, flags (covers, erase, union), box with `res`, `res`, pen width, alpha, and in `attr[8]` the family's union sign on a union item.

  • A family paints with its first drawn item's colour and alpha; an item that disagrees is counted and logged. Every array is the job's own copy, because `wireJob` transfers and so detaches them. `opts.offset` shifts every item's `res` to put an arbitrary rectangle on one plate (the Scenes pictures) without touching a memo. A strip nothing reaches gets an empty job.
emptyJob(opts, plates, paper, pool)A job with the strip's plates and paper and no items, for a strip nothing reaches.§9
rpk.emptyJob

A job with the strip's plates and paper and no items, for a strip nothing reaches.

alphaOf(o, f, fade)An item's paint alpha: its opacity, times its fade unless its family is an edit group painted at full presence.§9
rpk.alphaOf

An item's paint alpha: its opacity, times its fade unless its family is an edit group painted at full presence.

boxWithRes(b, res)A box shifted by an item's `res`, as a new array, or the same box when there is none.
rpk.boxWithRes

A box shifted by an item's `res`, as a new array, or the same box when there is none.

familyUnion(drawn)Whether a family's items together need the union pass: a ring of one item and an oppositely wound ring of another whose boxes overlap without nesting.§9
rpk.familyUnion

Gathers every shape and fill ring with `res` applied (a stroke has no rings in its entry and is a union item anyway), splits them by winding with zero-area rings in both lists, and tests only opposite-wound pairs of different items with `pairNeedsUnion`, capped at 20,000 tests (then yes, counted). Alike-wound overlaps between items stay on the fast path, because the 48-unit seam pad keeps the accumulated value at least 1 inside them. An item that needs the pass by its own rings does not make its siblings union items.

unionSignOf(all, f, q, Zq, cfg)A family's union orientation, +1 or −1, from the summed signed area of all its union items drawn or not, plus a count of its items wound against its total.§9
rpk.unionSignOf

The union pass deposits with this sign, and it must be the same on every plate or one plate paints ink where its neighbour cuts a hole. An empty or zero sum gives −1. The items wound against the family's total are counted into `f.mixed` and logged once: where two such items overlap the ink cancels to a hole no sign repairs, and the bake builds such a family today (OPEN-FLAGS F76).

unionAreaOf(d, q, Zq, cfg)The signed area an item weighs its family's sign with: its entry's ring area, or for a stroke the area of the band it ships.§9
rpk.unionAreaOf

A stroke culled from the strip in a drawn family is banded here for that number alone; `bandFor` memoises it per quantum. A stroke that ships no band weighs 0.

geomOf(d, q, Zq, cfg)The flat geometry one kept item ships, with the band's own box for a stroke; null when it ships nothing.§9
rpk.geomOf

For a shape or a fill it copies the coordinates into the entry on first use (`flattenGeom`).

raster/rasterJob.js 273 lines

The wire between the main thread and a raster worker: the job's and the result's typed-array layouts with their name tables, the validation that stops a malformed job painting a wrong picture, the transfer lists, the buffer pool the job's arrays come from, and the epoch rule that marks an arrived plate stale.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
BYTES(a)A typed array's byte length, 0 for a missing one.

A typed array's byte length, 0 for a missing one.

BufferPoolA free list of ArrayBuffers by power-of-two size class, so the jobs of a zoom reuse the buffers the worker hands back instead of allocating new ones.§9
rjb.BufferPool

`take` returns a view of exactly the length asked for, over a pooled buffer of its class when one is free; `give` files a returned buffer by its byte length, up to the pool's byte cap. `rasterWorkerClient` holds one of 8 MiB and passes it through the renderer to `packJob`; the worker hands the job's arrays back in the result's `recycled`.

BufferPool.constructor(maxBytes)Starts an empty pool with its byte cap, 8 MiB by default, and its take, hit and allocation counters.

Starts an empty pool with its byte cap, 8 MiB by default, and its take, hit and allocation counters.

take(ctor, len)A typed-array view of `len` elements over a pooled buffer of the right size class, or over a new buffer of that class.
rjb.take

Counts every take, the hits and the bytes allocated for misses; `rasterWorkerClient` reports them.

give(b)Returns a buffer, or a view's buffer, to the free list; a detached or empty one is ignored, and one that would pass the cap is dropped.
rjb.give

Returns a buffer, or a view's buffer, to the free list; a detached or empty one is ignored, and one that would pass the cap is dropped.

clear()Forgets every pooled buffer; the counters are left for the caller to reset.
rjb.clear

Forgets every pooled buffer; the counters are left for the caller to reset.

classOf(n)The size class a request falls in: the smallest power of two from 4 KiB up that holds `n` bytes.

wireJob(job)Validates a packed job and returns it as the message to post with its transfer list, every typed array's buffer in it.§9
rjb.wireJob

The message carries `kind: "raster-job"`, the id and zoom scalars and the nine arrays; each buffer is listed once, so nothing is copied and the main thread keeps no live view of a buffer the worker now owns. That is why `packJob` gives every job its own copies of the plate list, epochs and paper.

unwireJob(msg)Rebuilds the job a worker reads from its message, the arrays being the transferred bytes, and validates it.§9
rjb.unwireJob

Rebuilds the job a worker reads from its message, the arrays being the transferred bytes, and validates it.

validateJob(job)Throws on a job whose layout would paint a wrong picture silently: short arrays, a bad kind, spans past the data, families out of paint order, sub-chains not ascending.§9
rjb.validateJob

Checks the item count, each array's length against it, one epoch per plate, and per item its kind, its geometry and `subs` spans, at least one sub-chain, family indices ascending, and every sub-chain offset ascending and inside the item's span. The core reads a sub-chain's end from the next entry, so a short or unordered table reads a length as an offset and the ink disappears with no error. O(items + sub-chains); no geometry is read.

wireResult(res)Packs a worker's result as the message to post with its transfer list: plate bitmaps or pixels, the id sets, timings, counts, guards and the job's buffers handed back.§9
rjb.wireResult

Nulls, an empty plate's bitmap, are skipped, and each buffer is listed once. An ImageBitmap is serialisable as well as transferable, so one left out of the list is copied, 1.05 MB a plate, instead of moved.

unwireResult(msg)The result the main thread reads from a worker's message, with defaults for the recycled list and the serialisation time.§9
rjb.unwireResult

The result the main thread reads from a worker's message, with defaults for the recycled list and the serialisation time.

copyPlate(rgba)Copies one plate's pixels out of the worker's RGBA scratch, for the path without ImageBitmap.§9
rjb.copyPlate

It has to be a copy: the scratch is reused by the next plate, `new ImageData` aliases rather than copies, and a transferred buffer is detached. 1.05 MB a plate.

The bytes of a job's typed arrays, the size of what one post transfers; the worker client records it per job.

raster/rasterCore.js 1,302 lines

The coverage rasteriser that paints one 512-device-pixel plate of a packed job: signed-area accumulation in float64 into one buffer, a family at a time over its own rows, arcs flattened here and nowhere else to 1/16 device px without a centre, and a family whose rings may overlap filled as one nonzero union by exact-winding sub-scanlines (DESIGN.md §9). Pure; it runs in the raster worker and on the main thread's sync path.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
setDebugChecks(on)Turns the core's debug checks on or off: an edge outside its family's declared rows throws, and so does an arc sweep past a whole turn.§15
rco.setDebugChecks

Off in the shipped path. With it on, `addEdge` throws when an edge reaches rows outside the ones `beginFamily` declared (the bounded clear would miss them), and `emitArc` throws on an over-turn sweep instead of drawing its chord.

useAccumPrecision(kind)Swaps the accumulation buffer between Float32 and Float64, for the bench and the precision test only.
rco.useAccumPrecision

Reallocates only when the kind changes. The shipped path allocates the buffer once as `ACC_F32` says (Float32: half the memory traffic, worst error recorded as 6e-5 of coverage at 1,000 edges in a row) and never calls this.

accumPrecision()Which precision the accumulation buffer holds now, `f32` or `f64`.
rco.accumPrecision

Which precision the accumulation buffer holds now, `f32` or `f64`.

readAcc(x, y)One accumulation cell, for the tests and the bench; the running sum along a row is the coverage.
rco.readAcc

One accumulation cell, for the tests and the bench; the running sum along a row is the coverage.

rowRange(y)A row's touched-column range, [first, last], which the resolve and the bounded clear walk.
rco.rowRange

The last column is never above TW − 1: a deposit clamped at the plate's right edge sets it there, and that is what paints a clamped row out to the edge.

depositRun(y, xs, xe, d)Deposits one step of an edge inside one pixel row into the accumulation buffer, font-rs's `draw_line` arithmetic in float64, and widens the row's touched range.§9
rco.depositRun

`xs` and `xe` are already inside [0, TW]. A step within one column splits `d` between two cells by its mean x; a longer one spreads it over the columns it spans by their trapezoid areas. The deposit is signed area, so the running sum along the row is the coverage.

  • The touched range's top is capped at TW − 1; the buffer's two spill columns take the writes past it, and `clearFamily` clears them.
addStep(y, xs, xe, d)Clamps one row step of an edge to the plate's columns as a clamp of x(y), then deposits it.§9
rco.addStep

The step is split where x crosses 0 and TW, and each part outside becomes a vertical deposit on that bound carrying its share of `d`. Clamping the two endpoints instead is wrong: an edge from x = −3 to 0.5 across one row covers 0.964 of pixel 0, and the endpoint clamp reports 0.750.

addEdge(x0, y0, x1, y1)Deposits one straight edge, in plate-local device pixels, row by row; returns 1 if it deposited anything, else 0.§9
rco.addEdge

Orients the edge top to bottom with a direction sign, clips it to the plate's rows and hands each row it crosses to `addStep`. A horizontal edge or one off the plate in y returns 0.

  • A non-finite coordinate is dropped, counted in `coreStats.nonFinite`, and forces a whole-buffer clear at the end of the family: NaN defeats the comparisons that keep the touched ranges, so the bounded clear could not find its deposits.
beginFamily(y0, y1)Starts a family over rows [y0, y1): resets those rows' touched-column ranges and records the rows for the debug check.§9
rco.beginFamily

Starts a family over rows [y0, y1): resets those rows' touched-column ranges and records the rows for the debug check.

resolveFamily(out, r, g, b, alpha, y0, y1)Turns a family's accumulation into coverage and blends its colour onto the plate; returns the pixels it painted.§9
rco.resolveFamily

Per touched row, a running sum over the touched columns gives coverage min(|sum|, 1). Times the family's alpha, a pixel that reaches 1 is written outright and one below it is blended source-over on the 8-bit bytes (the alpha byte too on a transparent plate). A row whose sum is still past `TAIL_EPS` after its range is painted on to the plate's right edge.

  • `TAIL_EPS` (1/2048) sits above the Float32 residue of a closed loop; at 1e-9 that residue painted the rest of every row of a thin shape and added 15 % to its coverage. A row clamped at the right edge is painted to it by its touched range reaching TW − 1, not by this tail.
clearFamily(y0, y1)Zeroes exactly what the family touched, each row's touched columns plus the two spill columns, or the whole buffer after a non-finite coordinate.§9
rco.clearFamily

The bounded clear is what makes a family cost its ink rather than its area: a whole-buffer clear per family was 100–200 ms a plate at 800 families. A forced full clear is counted in `coreStats.fullClears`.

rowsTouched(y0, y1)Counts the family's rows that received a deposit, for the plate's `rowsTouched` count.§15
rco.rowsTouched

Counts the family's rows that received a deposit, for the plate's `rowsTouched` count.

pushUnionEdge(ax, ay, bx, by, yb0, yb1)Loads one edge, clipped to the row band [yb0, yb1), into the union pass's edge buffer; false when the buffer is full.§9
rco.pushUnionEdge

Stores the clipped top and bottom, the x at the top and dx/dy, with a direction sign. A non-finite edge is counted and dropped (and forces the full clear); a horizontal edge or one outside the band is skipped.

  • The buffer holds 16,384 edges. Inside `walkRowChunked` the first `uSkip` edges that would be stored are counted and passed over, because an earlier buffer-full has already taken them.
sortCrossings(n)Sorts one sub-scanline's crossings by x, each carrying its direction; an insertion sort, as a scanline holds a handful.
rco.sortCrossings

Sorts one sub-scanline's crossings by x, each carrying its direction; an insertion sort, as a scanline holds a handful.

growXS()Doubles the crossing buffer when a sub-scanline has more crossings than it holds, and counts it in `coreStats.xsGrown`.
rco.growXS

Doubles the crossing buffer when a sub-scanline has more crossings than it holds, and counts it in `coreStats.xsGrown`.

gatherCrossings(ys, n, nAct)Appends the x and direction of every active union edge that spans sub-scanline `ys`; returns the new count.§9
rco.gatherCrossings

Appends the x and direction of every active union edge that spans sub-scanline `ys`; returns the new count.

emitRuns(y, n, w)Resolves one sub-scanline's crossings into its non-zero-winding runs and deposits each into row `y` at weight `w`.§9
rco.emitRuns

Sorts the crossings, walks the winding count, and for each interval where it is non-zero deposits +w at its start and −w at its end, clamped to [0, TW]. Two cells a run however long, because the resolve's running sum carries the value across it. Overlapping rings therefore count once: the region is winding 1.

walkUnion(yb0, yb1)Walks the loaded union edges down rows [yb0, yb1) at 16 sub-scanlines a row and deposits the covered runs as a winding-1 region.§9
rco.walkUnion

Edges are bucketed by the row they start in and join an active list when the walk reaches it; each sub-scanline, at y + (k + ½)/16, goes through `gatherCrossings` and `emitRuns` at weight 1/16 times the family's union sign, and the edges that end inside the row are dropped before the next.

  • Sixteen sub-scanlines put an edge within 1/32 device px of its true y (`UNION_K`).
fillPaper(out, r, g, b, a)Paints the whole plate the paper colour before any family, or transparent black for a drag-plane plate.§9
rco.fillPaper

A full-sized, aligned plate is filled as 32-bit words from one written pixel. An opaque plate makes a blit a copy; a transparent one (`a` 0) is un-premultiplied by `unpremultiply` at the end of the plate.

unpremultiply(out)Divides a transparent plate's colour by its alpha, because the resolve accumulated premultiplied colour and `ImageData` is straight alpha.§9
rco.unpremultiply

Pixels at alpha 0 or 255 are left alone. Without it every antialiased edge of a drag-plane plate darkens.

widthOf(code)The count of numbers in one loop record by its code: 3 for a line, 8 an arc, 9 a cut line, 16 a cut arc; an unknown code reads as an arc.
rco.widthOf

The grammar of `geometry/loop.js`, repeated here as four numbers so the worker bundle carries no Loop class; the two tables must agree.

arcForced(sweep)How many halvings bring a sweep to a quarter turn or less, capped at 3: the splits made before a piece is pruned or counted.§9
rco.arcForced

The sagitta is infinite past a half turn and the chord-count formula is poor beyond a quarter turn, so a piece is bisected this many times before anything is asked of it. `emitArc` refuses a sweep past a whole turn, so there it is at most 2; the cap bounds a direct caller (it is exported for the tests).

arcDepth(ax, ay, bx, by, sweep)The bisection depth D for one arc piece, so that each of its 2^D chords stays within 1/16 device px of the arc, computed without a radius.§9
rco.arcDepth

0 when the whole piece's sagitta is already within `ARC_TOL`. Otherwise the piece is split into its forced sub-arcs with `chordMidK`, and each sub-arc's chord count n ≥ θ / (2·arccos(1 − 2·tol·sin(θ/2)/L)) is rounded up to a power of two; D is the forced splits plus the deepest of those, never below the forced ones.

  • A function of the piece and the tolerance only, never of the plate, so neighbouring plates flatten one arc to the same chords and agree at the seam. The arccos argument is clamped to [−1, 1] and D to 24 (`MAXD`, counted in `coreStats.arcClamped`); without the clamps a tiny radius gives NaN and the descent never ends. A clamped depth can miss the tolerance: measured 0.11 device px at 1e14 px of screen radius, 1.13 at 1e15.
chordOf(ax, ay, bx, by, ox, oy, mode, yb0, yb1)Emits a refused arc record as its straight chord, as a deposited edge or a union edge, so its loop still closes.§9
rco.chordOf

Takes scale-only coordinates and subtracts the plate origin, as the flattener's own chords do. Returns the edges deposited, or −1 when the union buffer is full. The chord is also the term `itemShoelace` gives such a record, so the area and the deposit agree.

emitArc(ax, ay, bx, by, sweep, cx, cy, ox, oy, mode, yb0, yb1)Flattens one arc piece into chords within 1/16 device px, centre-free and pruned against the plate, and deposits them or loads them for the union pass.§9
rco.emitArc

The gates first: a non-finite end is dropped (counted, full clear forced); a non-finite sweep or one past a whole turn is counted and drawn as its chord through `chordOf`, the over-turn throwing under the debug checks; a whole turn is split once at the antipode, the only place the record's centre is read, and is drawn as its chord when that centre is not finite.

  • Otherwise `arcDepth` gives D and the piece is bisected on a preallocated stack with one bulge coefficient per depth (`bulgeK`, `chordMidK`). Past the forced splits each node's chord box, grown by its sagitta, is tested against the plate: a node on no row of it is dropped; one wholly to the right is dropped on the fast path and becomes a vertical edge at TW on the union path; one wholly to the left becomes a vertical edge at column 0 carrying the node's own height; at depth D the chord is emitted.
  • Coordinates arrive scaled but not shifted, and the plate origin is subtracted per chord, so every plate computes the same chords and only the prune differs. Adds 2^D to the plate's chord count. Returns the edges deposited, or −1 when the union buffer filled. A refused record is drawn as its chord because an open outline leaks: accumulation is signed, and the recorded case painted 34,944 units of ink out to the plate's edge for an item of 7,110.
emitItem(job, it, rx, ry, ox, oy, Zq)Deposits every edge of one fast-path item of a job: its loops' lines and flattened arcs, or its flat rings, in plate-local device pixels.§9
rco.emitItem

Walks each sub-chain between its `subs` offsets and closes it back to its start. A point maps as (x + res)·Zq − the plate origin: the residual is added before the scale and the exact integer origin subtracted after, so two neighbouring plates describe a shared point to the last bit. Loop records are read by code, lines and cut lines as edges, arcs and cut arcs through `emitArc` with the scale-only coordinates. Returns the edges deposited.

itemShoelace(job, it, rx, ry, ox, oy, Zq)Twice the signed area of one item's rings in plate-local pixels, arcs included exactly: the core's fallback for a family's union sign.§9
rco.itemShoelace

Lines add the shoelace term; an arc adds its chord's term plus `arcAreaTerm`, the radius-free segment; a whole turn adds ±2πr² from its centre, because its ends coincide and would carry no sign. A record `emitArc` refuses keeps its chord's term alone, as it is drawn.

  • `renderPlate` sums it over a family's union items only when the job declares no sign in `attr[8]` (a hand-built job).
loadUnionItem(job, it, rx, ry, ox, oy, Zq, yb0, yb1)Loads one union item's edges, clipped to a row band, into the union edge buffer; false when the buffer overflowed.§9
rco.loadUnionItem

The same record walk and coordinate mapping as `emitItem`, with arcs flattened in union mode, so every plate loads the same edges.

loadUnionBand(job, meta, attr, first, last, ox, oy, Zq, yb0, yb1)Empties the edge buffer and loads every drawn union item of one family, clipped to rows [yb0, yb1); false when they do not fit.§9
rco.loadUnionBand

Empties the edge buffer and loads every drawn union item of one family, clipped to rows [yb0, yb1); false when they do not fit.

loadBandCounted(job, meta, attr, first, last, ox, oy, Zq, yb0, yb1)`loadUnionBand`, keeping the guard counters' increase from the family's first load that fits.§15
rco.loadBandCounted

A family's geometry is re-read once per band, per halving and per buffer-full, and each read counts the same refused records again. The first load that fits enumerates every record, so `unionPass` sets `arcOverTurn`, `nonFinite` and `arcClamped` from that load's increase and the guards count records, not passes.

walkRowChunked(job, meta, attr, first, last, ox, oy, Zq, y)Walks one pixel row whose union edges do not fit the buffer even alone, gathering each sub-scanline's crossings over successive buffer-fulls.§9
rco.walkRowChunked

For each of the 16 sub-scanlines the family's edges for the row are loaded one buffer-full at a time (`uSkip` advancing), the crossings of every fill gathered, and `emitRuns` run once on the whole row's winding, so no ink is lost (OPEN-FLAGS F75). Depositing each buffer-full's union on its own would count their overlap twice.

  • The price is the row's geometry read 16 times per extra buffer-full, recorded at 41–43 ns an edge a pass. The chord count keeps only the one complete pass, and the extra buffer-fulls are counted in `coreStats.unionRefills`.
unionPass(job, first, last, ox, oy, Zq, y0, y1)Fills a family's union items over its rows as one exact-winding region, in as few row bands as the edge buffer allows.§9
rco.unionPass

Tries the family's whole row range and, while its edges do not fit, halves the band (counted in `unionSplits`). A band that fits goes to `walkUnion`; a single row that still does not fit goes to `walkRowChunked`; then the next band.

  • At the end the three record guards are set from the first complete load, so a record refused once is counted once.
renderPlate(job, plateIndex, out, counts, timings)Paints one plate of a packed job into an RGBA buffer: paper, the prune, then every family in paint order through the deposit, the union pass, the resolve and the clear.§9
rco.renderPlate

Fills the paper (transparent when the job's paper alpha is 0) and marks each item whose box, scaled by `Zq`, reaches the plate; an item that misses could deposit nothing the resolve reads, so the prune is exact. Families are runs of `meta[1]` and must ascend (it throws otherwise). A family with a drawn item gets a row range from its drawn items' boxes, rounded outward with 1e-6 px of slack; its fast-path items go through `emitItem`, its union items through `unionPass`, and `resolveFamily` blends it with its first drawn item's colour and alpha before `clearFamily`.

  • The union deposit's sign comes from `attr[8]`, the packer's family sign summed over all its union items drawn or not (`itemShoelace` when that is 0), so every plate of a family agrees on ink against hole, and a union item and a fast-path item of one family add where they meet. `counts` receives the plate's eight counts and `timings` its phase clocks when given.
  • Called by the raster worker for each plate of a strip, and by `RasterRenderer`'s sync path on the main thread.

raster/rasterWorkerClient.js · worker/rasterWorker.js 548 + 161 lines

The raster worker pool on the main thread: one strip queue ordered by priority, the per-quantum staleness rule, the buffer pool, the end-job contract, and the inline fallback that runs the worker's own entry on this thread. The raster worker's entry, bundled to `public/raster-worker.js`: rasters each plate of a strip with `rasterCore.renderPlate` into one reused scratch and posts back the pixels, per-plate timings and counts, painted-id sets, guard words and the job's buffers. `runJob` is also the inline path.

How many raster workers to run: min(4, max(1, cores − 1)), unless a test or `?rasterWorkers=N` overrides it.

Parses `rasterWorkers=N` from a query string, capped at 4; null when absent or not positive.

workerUrl()The worker script's URL: `/raster-worker.js` under `PUBLIC_URL`.

The worker script's URL: `/raster-worker.js` under `PUBLIC_URL`.

ensureRasterPool()Spawns the worker pool if it is not up yet; the renderer's constructor calls it so the first render does not pay for it.§9
rwc.ensureRasterPool

Four workers loading the bundle cost tens of ms on a desktop and up to a hundred each on a phone. Returns the live worker count, 0 on the inline path.

spawnPool(late)Creates the workers once per session and wires their messages and errors; with no `Worker`, or a constructor that throws, it marks the pool broken, which is the inline path.§9
rwc.spawnPool

A spawn from the dispatch path is late and counted in `spawnedLate`. Does nothing under a transport, once broken, or once spawned.

terminateWorkers()Terminates every worker and forgets the pool, reporting nothing.§9
rwc.terminateWorkers

`destroyRasterPool` is the teardown that also reports the in-flight jobs.

destroyRasterPool()Teardown: terminates the workers and reports every in-flight job as dropped, since a terminated worker never answers.§9

Teardown: terminates the workers and reports every in-flight job as dropped, since a terminated worker never answers.

abandonInFlight(why)Reports every in-flight job as dropped with its id, so the caller can end it in the store; each job's capacity stays held until it answers.§9
rwc.abandonInFlight

A worker slot is marked abandoned, not freed: the worker is still drawing into its one scratch, and a second job would overwrite pixels the first one's `ImageData` aliases. A slotless job (inline or transport) is held by the `heldNoSlot` count. A result arriving later finds no record and only releases the hold, so each id is reported once.

releaseAbandoned(slot)Releases an abandoned job's hold when its answer comes — the slot, or one of `heldNoSlot` — and says whether to pump.§9
rwc.releaseAbandoned

Releases an abandoned job's hold when its answer comes — the slot, or one of `heldNoSlot` — and says whether to pump.

onWorkerError(e)A worker failed to load or threw outside a job: marks the pool broken for the session, reports each in-flight strip dropped, re-queues them and pumps them onto the inline path.§9
rwc.onWorkerError

Each stranded strip is re-packed under a new job id, so the caller must still end the old one.

activeCount()The workers available for strip sizing: the transport's count, the pool's (spawning it late if needed), or 1 for the inline path.§9
rwc.activeCount

The workers available for strip sizing: the transport's count, the pool's (spawning it late if needed), or 1 for the inline path.

freeSlot()A worker with no job; `null` for the slotless paths when they have room; `undefined` when everything is busy.§9
rwc.freeSlot

A transport takes as many jobs as the pool would and the inline path takes one; both count abandoned slotless jobs as held. Spawns the pool late if needed.

dispatch(entry, slot)Mints a job id, has the caller pack the strip, records it in flight and posts it to its worker, the transport, or the inline `runJob`.§9
rwc.dispatch

A pack that throws or returns null is reported dropped with the new id (`pack`, `empty`). The posted-at time is the main thread's; the wire and post time goes to `postMs`.

  • The inline path runs the worker's own `runJob` on a later microtask, so both paths draw the same pixels and jsdom checks the shipped code.
onFailed(jobId, err, slot)A job's terminal failure: frees its slot, reports it dropped with the error, and pumps; an unknown id only releases an abandoned hold.§9
rwc.onFailed

A job's terminal failure: frees its slot, reports it dropped with the error, and pumps; an unknown id only releases an abandoned hold.

onMessage(slot, data)A worker's answer: frees the slot, returns the job's buffers to the pool, derives the timings, totals the guards and counts, checks staleness, then calls `onDrop` for stale plates and `onResult`.§9
rwc.onMessage

Queueing time is the main thread's wall time minus the phases the worker reports, since the worker returns durations only. A `raster-error` message goes to `onFailed`. A result with no record is ignored except to release an abandoned hold. A stale arrival fires both `onDrop` (naming the stale plates) and `onResult`; the caller ends the id once.

plateBitmap(px)Converts one plate's raw RGBA to an `ImageBitmap`, or null where the scope has no `createImageBitmap`.§9
rwc.plateBitmap

The layer composes bitmaps only; where this is null (jsdom) the caller puts the raw pixels.

rasterWorkerReport()The worker client's report: mode, worker counts, queue and in-flight sizes, held slots, live quanta, job totals, bytes, timings, the guard and count totals and the buffer pool.§15
rwc.rasterWorkerReport

`heldSlots` is the capacity abandoned jobs still hold; `liveRequests` counts the quanta with a newest frame on record, and falls only at the next submit or drop.

resetRasterWorkerClient()The suite's reset: empties the queue and the in-flight map, terminates the workers, and clears the broken flag, ids, overrides, buffer pool and counters.
rwc.resetRasterWorkerClient

It reports nothing in flight; the live teardown is `destroyRasterPool`.

resetGuards()Zeroes the raster core's guard counters, so a job's guards are its own.§9
rwk.resetGuards

Zeroes the raster core's guard counters, so a job's guards are its own.

runJob(msg, opts)Rasters every plate of one strip into the one RGBA scratch and returns the wired result: bitmaps or pixel copies, ids, timings, counts, guards and the job's buffers.§9
rwk.runJob

Each plate is serialised (a bitmap awaited, or the bytes copied) before the next is drawn, because the scratch is reused. A plate no item reached after the prune stays null: nothing is drawn there. Times are durations only; receipt-to-start, start-to-finish and serialisation partition the worker's time, so the main thread's queueing subtraction cannot hide a phase.

  • Exported because `rasterWorkerClient`'s inline path runs it on the main thread; jsdom always takes that path.

raster/MovePlane.js 342 lines

The drag plane: the picture under, of and over a selection split by z into layers of plates, rastered while the selection exists — cut coarser where it would not fit its cap, with a quick coarse level asked for first — so a drag moves the selected ink as a translated bitmap and re-rasters once at the drop (DESIGN.md §9).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
resetPlaneStats()Zeroes the drag plane's counters.§15
mvp.resetPlaneStats

Zeroes the drag plane's counters.

idsHash(ids)A short FNV-1a hash of an id set, the same for the same ids in any order: the part of a layer's tag that names its members.§9
mvp.idsHash

A short FNV-1a hash of an id set, the same for the same ids in any order: the part of a layer's tag that names its members.

rangeOf(cells)The bounding plate range of a cell list, or null when it is empty.§9
mvp.rangeOf

The bounding plate range of a cell list, or null when it is empty.

MovePlaneThe drag plane: a selection's picture split by z into layers of plates, kept ready while it is selected, so a drag moves bitmaps and re-rasters only at the drop.§9
mvp.MovePlane

Layers in paint order: BELOW (everything except the selected runs and the runs above them, opaque, with the paper), then each run of selected families (SEL, transparent, drawn at the pointer's offset) and of unselected families above one (OVER, transparent, in place). A dragged object therefore passes under ink above it.

  • Only a selection with no ink on screen is refused. Past 5 layers the smallest unselected run between two selected ones is drawn under the selection; past the plate cap (40 on a desktop, 24 on a phone) the layers are cut up to 3 octaves coarser and drawn magnified, the coarsest taken whatever it costs. A quick level 2 octaves coarser again is asked for first and drawn until the main level is whole; until either is, the selected layers are drawn alone, or a small selection is rastered on the main thread (`RasterRenderer._planeStopgap`). The plates live in `PlateStore` under the plane's own tags, pinned (DESIGN.md §9).
MovePlane.constructor()Points `stats` at the module's counters and starts the plane empty and idle.§9
mvp.MovePlane.constructor

Points `stats` at the module's counters and starts the plane empty and idle.

_reset()Empties the plane — selection, list, both levels, the drawn level, the stopgap, layers, tags, keys, ranges, offset, landing times — sets it idle and bumps `gen`.§9
mvp._reset

The caller compares `gen` to know it must free the old layers' plates. `layers`, `r` and `selR` mirror the main level; `tags` and `keys` cover both levels.

showing (getter)Whether the plane is drawn this compose: while it is dragging or landing.§9
mvp.showing

Whether the plane is drawn this compose: while it is dragging or landing.

cellCount()The number of plates the plane pins.§9
mvp.cellCount

The number of plates the plane pins.

aim(st, list, view, cfg, max, dpr, live)(Re)aims the plane at a selection, a list and a view; true while it is valid for them.§9
mvp.aim

Does nothing while dragging or landing. A new selection key, frame, quantum or zoom resets it, and with no selected ids it is refused; a new list, id set or cap under the same selection re-cuts it, so a pan keeps the plates of every layer whose members are unchanged. The zoom is compared as well as the quantum because a settled view is `q` "e" at any exact zoom.

_cut(list, ids, view, cfg, max, dpr, live)Cuts the plane: groups the pack's on-screen families in paint order into selected and unselected runs, merges runs past the layer cap, and picks a main level that fits the plate cap and a quick level under it.§9
mvp._cut

Families come from `rasterPack.paintFamilies`, so the layers split exactly where the pack paints; a family with no item box on the view's plates is skipped, and unselected families below the first selected run stay in BELOW. Past `MOVE_PLANE_LAYERS` the smallest unselected run sandwiched between two selected ones is merged away, so it is drawn under the selection (counted in `merged`).

  • The main level is the first of 0 to 3 octaves coarser (`_level`) whose plates fit the cap — at most 16 for a level drawn magnified, that is coarser or with the view between quanta — else the coarsest (counted in `overCap`). A plane of more than 4 plates also gets a quick level 2 octaves under the main, kept when it has fewer plates, fits the cap together with the main, and is within 16. Refused only when no selected ink is on screen.
_level(runs, view, k)Builds the plane's layers at `k` octaves coarser than the view: each layer's cells, tag and keys, the plate count, the bounding ranges and BELOW's cell set.§9
mvp._level

The level's quantum is the view's less 4k (derived from the zoom when the view is a settle) and the view's plate range is mapped onto its grid. A run's cells are its item boxes on that grid; BELOW covers the union of every run's cells and omits every run's ids.

  • A layer's tag is `z<n>_<quantum>_<members hash>`, so a re-cut that changes a run's members is a new layer and never reuses the old plates. BELOW's cell set is what `PictureLayer` reads to skip the view's own plates under a whole BELOW mid-drag.
requests(list)One store request per layer, the quick level's first — BELOW with its omitted ids, the others with only their own ids on transparent paper — or null when refused or landing.§9
mvp.requests

Each is off camera, priority 2, mode `plane`, at its level's zoom, and carries its cell list instead of a range.

_whole(lvl, store, selOnly)Whether every plate of a level, or of its selected layers only, is cached and live.§9
mvp._whole

Whether every plate of a level, or of its selected layers only, is cached and live.

checkReady(store)Whether the main level is cached and live; once true it stays true for this plane.§9
mvp.checkReady

`pick` falls back to the quick level or the selected layers until it is.

pick(store)Chooses the level to draw this compose: the main level whole, else the quick level whole, else the selected layers of either alone; null when none is in.§9
mvp.pick

Sets `cur` and `partial`. While partial the layer draws only the SEL layers, and the plates underneath still show the ink where it was, so the other packs do not omit the selection.

dragTo(dxCss, dyCss, dpr)Enters the drag state and sets the offset to the pointer's displacement since the drag's start, in whole device px.§9

Between repaints a camera step or a drag is a CSS transform on the canvas, and it never reads the ink canvas (DESIGN.md §9).

Built by `RasterRenderer._makeOverlay` on the first selection decision and pushed onto the renderer's `_layers`, so `setSize`, the plate store's release and `destroy` reach it. `show` takes the decision from `overlays._selectionAnts` (runs and marks as render-list pieces in frame units) and `PictureLayer`'s published view, paints through `antPaint.paintPhase`, and never reads the ink canvas.

  • The plane is painted at the view of the moment and the canvas carries only the delta to the current view as a CSS transform (`s = k/k0`, translate `(t − t0·s)/dpr`), so a camera step between repaints is a style write. The canvas sits at z-index 2, above the ink and the Two.js `<svg>` and under the chevrons' SVG.

The paint-time view composed with this transform equals the published `k, tx, ty`, so a camera step between repaints moves the plane without painting it. A paint view whose `k` is not finite gives a scale of 1.

The view maps frame units to device px (`p·k + t`) with no origin in it. `dec.off` is the drag in CSS px; rounding it makes a drag between repaints an integer translate that cannot resample the plane.

Ensures the plane first, records the paint view in `_paintAt`, and copies `paintPhase`'s dashes, stamps, pixels and time into the report. `repaint` counts a repaint, and one made while the crawl is frozen also counts in `repaintsDuringGesture`. Clears the dirty flag and `uncoveredPx` and stamps `_lastRepaintAt` for the uncovered-screen throttle.

`rect` is integers, half-open, clamped to the plane; an empty one writes nothing, so a caller that wants the whole plane passes it. Returns the pixels written and records `blitMs` and `blitPx`. Without a context or an `ImageData` (jsdom) it writes nothing and returns 0.

Measured: 0.049 ms for a 200-row band. `paintPhase` calls it first, so a phase depends on nothing the buffer held.

noteRows(buf, y0, y1, x0, x1)Widens the buffer's painted-row range and its dirty rect to take in one stamp's pixels.§9
anp.noteRows

Widens the buffer's painted-row range and its dirty rect to take in one stamp's pixels.

dashIntervals(len, on, off, phase, out, fit)The lit intervals of one run at one crawl phase, as start/end pairs along its own length in device px.§9
anp.dashIntervals

A run at least one cycle long is fitted to a whole number of cycles (`n = round(len/cycle)`, the pattern scaled to fit) so no dash is a runt; a shorter run, or a mark (`fit` false), carries the full-size pattern and slides. The phase offset is `phase/8` of the run's own fitted cycle, so every run completes its cycle in the same eight steps.

  • Returns the pairs needed and writes at most `out.length/2`; a caller given more grows its array and calls again, so no array is allocated per run. A cycle boundary landing within rounding of the run's end is not counted as a dash.

anp.stampSegment

Coverage is `clamp01(h + 0.5 − |d⊥|)` times the two axial ramps: exact for an axis-aligned edge, an approximation of area for a rotated one. Each row walks only the x span where both constraints can be non-zero. A pixel is written, in the ink's colour, only where its alpha rises; a zero-length dash paints a dot of radius `h`.

  • The composite is `max`, not a sum, so two crossing runs paint solid, never darker. A non-finite coordinate is refused and counted in `antStats.nonFinite`.

anp.joinExt

The miter term fills the wedge two rectangles leave on the outside of a turn. It is capped at half the shorter chord, and a reversal takes `4h` into that cap; uncapped, a tight turn inflated a speck by 34 % (D132).

stampPolyline(buf, pts, n, h, ink, e0, e1)Stamps a device-space polyline as one dash, each chord extended at its joins so the band has no notch where they meet.§9
anp.stampPolyline

Interior joins take `joinExt`; the two ends take `e0` and `e1`: 0 for a cap, 0.5 px where the dash carries on into a stretch not stamped here, or the seam's own join on a closed run.

stampDisc(buf, cx, cy, r, ink)Paints a solid dot of radius `r`, max-composited, with the band's own one-pixel radial ramp: a speck is one disc.§9
anp.stampDisc

Once the band's half-width reaches a circle's radius, a ring of chords closes over its own centre and leaves wedges at every join (measured 12 % short across), so a speck is stamped as a disc instead.

At most four arc pieces sharing one centre and one radius whose sweeps total a full turn. `circleLoop` builds every mark as two half-turns, so this recognises the marks the decision makes.

pieceBox(p, k, tx, ty, out)A conservative device-space box for one piece, for the test that skips pieces off the plane.§9

An arc of up to a half turn takes its chord's box grown by the bulge `r·(1 − cos(sweep/2))`; a longer one takes the whole circle's box.

A copy of `curveOutline.cubicAt` with the view folded in: this module imports only `antRuns`, so a worker can take it.

pushPt(n, x, y)Appends a device-space point to the polyline scratch, skipping a repeat of the last one, and returns the new count.
anp.pushPt

Appends a device-space point to the polyline scratch, skipping a repeat of the last one, and returns the new count.

appendPiece(p, u0, u1, L, h, k, tx, ty, n)Appends the lit stretch [u0, u1] of one piece to the polyline being built, so a dash across several pieces is stamped as one polyline.§9
anp.appendPiece

A line adds its two end points. An arc is walked about its own centre in chords whose outer-edge sagitta is at most 1/16 device px (`chordStep(R²/(R + h))`), each pushed out by half its sagitta so the band straddles the true circle; an arc of radius at most 1/16 px is one chord. A cubic (only an unresolved stroke's capsule outline) is sampled by `cubicSamples` and cut by the samples' own cumulative length, rescaled to `pieceLength`'s.

  • Using the arc's centre is safe here, unlike in the ink's centre-free flattener: this is float64 over render-list coordinates the packer bounds at 2.6e5 frame units, where the cancellation is under 1e-6 device px.
  • Stamping piece by piece instead leaves an unfilled wedge at every piece boundary: measured on a speck, 214 rather than 255 at the boundary pixel and the dot 12 % short across.
cubicSamples(p, k, tx, ty)Samples one cubic in device px at the 1/16 px bar, with cumulative lengths, and returns the segment count.§9
anp.cubicSamples

The count is `ceil(sqrt(dev/tol))` from the control points' deviation off the chord, between 1 and 256.

sampleAt(ns, s, out, slot)The point at length `s` along the sampled cubic, interpolated within its segment.§9
anp.sampleAt

The point at length `s` along the sampled cubic, interpolated within its segment.

seamJoinExt(pieces, n, firstEnd, lastStart, total, h, k, tx, ty)The join extension at a closed run's seam, from the chords that meet there, so the loop's first and last half-dashes join like any corner.§9
anp.seamJoinExt

Builds the head's first chord and the tail's last with `appendPiece` itself, so they are the chords the stamp will use, and hands them to `joinExt`. Falls back to the bare 0.5 px overlap when either end's piece is off the plane or yields no chord (D132).

samePt(a, b)Are two points equal to a relative 1e-9, `antRuns`' own tolerance, which that module does not export?
anp.samePt

Are two points equal to a relative 1e-9, `antRuns`' own tolerance, which that module does not export?

geometryCloses(pieces, n)Does the run end where it starts (the first finite piece's start against the last's end), for a run that carries no `closed` flag?§9
anp.geometryCloses

A mark built by `circleLoop` may carry none; without this check a speck is painted as a ring of chords instead of one disc (D134).

paintRun(buf, pieces, closed, h, on, off, phase, k, tx, ty, ink, fit)Paints one run or mark: measures its pieces, places its lit intervals and stamps each lit stretch as one polyline.§9
anp.paintRun

A piece with a non-finite number is refused and counted; a piece whose device box misses the plane by more than the band is off-plane and not stamped, which breaks a dash there. A closed run whose dashes wrap the seam joins its first and last stretches with `seamJoinExt`, and a speck whose one dash wraps is a single `stampDisc` of radius R + h.

  • There is no cap on the work (F38): what bounds it is the decision's cut to the retained window and the off-plane skip.
inkOf(css)The ink colour as `[r, g, b]`: `css.ink` as given, unpacked from 0xRRGGBB, or `SEL_INK_RGB` by default.§9

The ink colour as `[r, g, b]`: `css.ink` as given, unpacked from 0xRRGGBB, or `SEL_INK_RGB` by default.

paintPhase(buf, dec, view, phase, css)One crawl phase of one selection decision into the buffer: clears what the last phase painted, then paints every run and mark.§9
anp.paintPhase

Runs take the band and dash scaled by `selAntScale(dec.inkPx)` and fitted to whole cycles; marks take the fine band unscaled and unfitted, so their pattern slides across them and blinks. Band and pattern are CSS px times `css.dpr`; the geometry is frame units mapped by `view` (`p·k + t`, no origin). A non-finite view refuses the whole decision. Returns what this call placed, stamped, wrote and refused.

  • Measured at F39's report camera (4,756 runs): 14.2–33.9 ms a phase, against 107–190 ms of raster plus 45–149 ms of packing through the general rasteriser.
