Only the suites call it. The renderer hands `antStats` to `rasterPerf.attach` as its `ants` source, so the report carries them.

raster/rasterPerf.js 1,154 lines

The raster path's performance ring: one row per main-thread task (render, camera step, job arrival, crawl tick, settle) in fixed typed arrays, its time split into five buckets (ENGINE, RASTERISER, TRANSFER, BROWSER, OVERLAY) with a one-word verdict, and the `raster` section of the dev report. It imports only `now.js` (DESIGN.md §14).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
wall()The default wall clock, `Date.now()`, for row stamps; `attach` or the suite can replace it.
rpf.wall

The default wall clock, `Date.now()`, for row stamps; `attach` or the suite can replace it.

ensure()Allocates the ring (timers, counts, wall stamps) and the job and drop record pools on the first note.§15
rpf.ensure

Once only, so an SVG-only session pays nothing: 400 rows × 40 slots, 131.2 KB in all. `reset` is the only thing that frees it.

mkJobRec()One empty worst-job record, filled in place by `takeJob`.§15
rpf.mkJobRec

One empty worst-job record, filled in place by `takeJob`.

mkDropRec()One empty drop record, filled in place by `noteDrop`.§15
rpf.mkDropRec

One empty drop record, filled in place by `noteDrop`.

attach(s)Takes the sources the report reads (picture layer, plate store, worker, packer, core and ant stats), the engine's perf-log hook and optional clocks.§15
rpf.attach

Called in `RasterRenderer`'s constructor. The module imports only `now.js`, so these arrive here rather than being imported.

detach()Forgets the sources; the ring and its rows are kept, so a report sent after a teardown still has them.§15
rpf.detach

Called from `RasterRenderer.destroy`.

reset()Frees the ring, zeroes every total, histogram, pending patch, submit stamp, drop tally and statistic, and restores the default clocks.§15
rpf.reset

The suites' reset; no app code calls it.

beginFrame(frameSeq, kind)Opens a row for one main-thread task: clears its slots, stamps both clocks and writes its `frameSeq` and kind.§15
rpf.beginFrame

A row still open is closed first and flagged `truncated`. `RasterRenderer._openRow` is the caller, for render, camera, arrival and settle tasks.

endFrame()Closes the open row with `mainMs` as the bracket's own time, and sends a render row of 8 ms or more (any, in trace mode) to the engine's perf log.§15
rpf.endFrame

Returns the row, or null with `orphanEnds` counted when no row was open.

add(slot, ms)Adds milliseconds to one timer slot of the open row; a negative or non-finite value is ignored.§15
rpf.add

With no row open it counts `orphanAdds` and records nothing. `RasterRenderer._add` maps a slot name to its index through `T`.

bump(slot, n)Adds to one count slot of the open row, or counts an orphan when none is open.§15
rpf.bump

No app code calls it; the suites do.

noteView(view)Records the published view (mode, quantum, stretch, dpr, revision, frame) and writes its quantum, mode and stretch onto the open row.§15
rpf.noteView

A `sync` view flags the row `rasOnMain`, so the rasteriser's phases count inside `mainMs`. The last view is kept for crawl rows, which have none of their own.

closeRow(extraFlags, endAt)Finishes the open row: its wall span, both residuals, the running totals and histograms, and a place in the queue for the next rAF patch.§15
rpf.closeRow

`residualMain` is `mainMs` less the main-part timers (and the worker-part ones in sync mode); `residualWall` is the queued-to-blitted `wallMs` less the wall-part timers. Worker rows' phases also go to `workerT`, so `ras.plateResidual` comes from one set of rows and cannot go negative on a sync frame.

  • A truncated row takes `mainMs` and its wall span at the moment it is closed. Up to 64 rows wait for a rAF delta; past that they count as `pendingLost`.
perfExtra(row)The fields a slow render row sends to the engine's perf log: `frameSeq`, kind, `mainMs` and the main residual.§15
rpf.perfExtra

The fields a slow render row sends to the engine's perf log: `frameSeq`, kind, `mainMs` and the main residual.

noteSubmit(req, nPlates, nStrips)Stamps a request's queued-at time before it is posted, with how many strips will arrive against it, and counts its plates as misses on the open row.§15
rpf.noteSubmit

Kept in a 64-deep ring of parallel arrays, with no allocation per post. `platesWanted` is these misses plus the hits `noteCompose` adds, so no plate counts twice.

queuedAtFor(seq, postedAt)The queued-at stamp an arriving job claims: the newest submit of its `frameSeq`, at or before its post, with strips still unclaimed.§15
rpf.queuedAtFor

When every such submit is claimed it takes the newest one at or before the post, and -1 when there is none. One frame can post at more than one quantum under one `frameSeq`; the strip counts and the post time are what tell those posts apart.

noteJob(info, res)Records a worker job's arrival on the open row: queue wait, transfer times, bytes, and the worker's per-plate phase timings and counts.§15
rpf.noteJob

Reads durations only, because the worker's clock has its own origin. The earliest claimed queued-at opens the row's queued-to-blitted span. The job goes to the worst-jobs list, and one of 8 ms wall or more (any, in trace mode) to the engine's perf log as `rasterJob`. With no row open the job is counted and nothing else.

  • The per-plate stride is read off the arrays; the suite pins it against `rasterJob.js`'s exports.
noteBitmap(ms)Adds `createImageBitmap`'s time to `br.bitmap`, a wall duration because the decode runs off the main thread.§15
rpf.noteBitmap

Adds `createImageBitmap`'s time to `br.bitmap`, a wall duration because the decode runs off the main thread.

noteCompose(ms, plates, blits)Adds a compose's time to `br.blit` and its blits to the row; on a non-arrival row its plates count as cache hits.§15
rpf.noteCompose

On an arrival row the plates composed are the ones that arrived, which `noteJob` has counted. On the arrival path the timed span is the whole plate-batch handler: store puts, paper fill, blits and re-post.

noteDrop(req, d)Records a stale or dropped job: a drop on the open row, a full record in an 8-deep log, a count by reason, and a `rasterStale` perf-log entry.§15
rpf.noteDrop

Every drop is tallied by its `why` (`tallyDrop`), so a session that dropped hundreds keeps the distribution beyond the last eight.

noteCrawl(rep)Records one overlay crawl tick as a row of its own, kind `crawl`, from `OverlayLayer.report()`.§15
rpf.noteCrawl

Closes a still-open row as truncated first. Crawl rows take negative `frameSeq`s, so they never collide with a render's. The tick's decide, paint, blit and live times fill the OVERLAY timers and its dashes, stamps, pixels, blit pixels and repaints the ant counts; `mainMs` is their sum unless the report gives one. The last published view supplies the row's quantum and mode, and `bytes` becomes the report's `overlayBytes`.

onFrame(deltaMs, ts)The frame meter's rAF hook: patches the interval onto every row waiting for it and writes `br.inferred = rafDelta − Σ mainMs` onto the last of them.§15
rpf.onFrame

BROWSER time is attributed by that subtraction, never measured. The interval's other rows are flagged `shared`; flags also mark a task longer than its interval and a remainder clamped at 0, and a row the ring has overwritten counts as `pendingLost`. A row no tick reaches reports `br.inferred` as null.

  • `useKobinEngine` sets it as `frameMeter.onFrame`.
growth()What the growth log samples on the raster path: the plate cache's count and bytes and the packer's memo bytes, or null with nothing attached.§15
rpf.growth

`packedBytes` is the packer's memo, not the bytes transferred. Read by `instruments.js`'s growth log and by the report.

report(opts)The dev report's `raster` section: ring shape, slot names and parts, totals, histograms, up to 50 rows with verdicts, the worst jobs, the drops, memory and each source's report.§15
rpf.report

Bounded by construction (F58): at most 50 rows, 25 jobs and 8 drops, histograms rather than samples, and a `notes` object that explains the counters. Rows are joined to the `LongFrames` instrument's entries by wall-clock overlap when it is passed. `size.sectionBytes` is the section's own size; `reportBytes` is left null for `reportSend.js` to patch in after its one stringify.

  • Read by `report.js` (`raster.perf`) and in the console as `E.renderer.perf.report()`.
byteLen(s)A string's UTF-8 size in bytes, for the report's size bar (F58), because `length` counts characters.§15
rpf.byteLen

`TextEncoder` where there is one (measured: 92 MB in 32–38 ms); otherwise a scan that allocates nothing (204–277 ms on the same 92 MB), which is what jsdom takes. A lone surrogate counts 3 bytes. `reportSend.js` measures the whole report body with it.

firstNamed(o, first)A copy of a counters object with the named keys first, in order, then the rest as they stand.§15
rpf.firstNamed

Puts the counters that mean a record was refused at the top of the `pack`, `core` and worker-guard sections.

workerOut()The worker pool's own report with its guard counters put refusals first; null with no pool source.§15
rpf.workerOut

The worker pool's own report with its guard counters put refusals first; null with no pool source.

pickRows()The ring rows the report keeps: the 25 worst by `mainMs` and the last 25, deduplicated and in time order.§15
rpf.pickRows

The ring rows the report keeps: the 25 worst by `mainMs` and the last 25, deduplicated and in time order.

rowOut(row, loaf)One ring row as report JSON: identity, `mainMs`, residuals, non-zero timers and counts, flag names, its verdict and any overlapping long frame.§15
rpf.rowOut

`br.inferred` is null unless a rAF delta reached the row, never 0. `wallMs` appears only on a row with a queued-to-blitted span.

loafFor(t, mainMs, loaf)The long-animation-frame entry that overlaps a row's interval most, with the overlap, or null.§15
rpf.loafFor

Only the `LongFrames` instrument's kept worst entries are searched, so a row that joins none is not evidence of anything.

verdictFor(base)A row's one-word verdict: the bucket holding at least half its main-thread time, or `BROWSER`, `trivial` or `ambiguous`, with why.§15
rpf.verdictFor

`trivial` at or under 1 ms. `ambiguous` when the residual exceeds max(1 ms, 10 % of `mainMs`) or no bucket reaches half. `BROWSER` when a known rAF interval over 50 ms has `br.inferred` above `mainMs`, whatever the task's own split; `top` still names the largest main-thread bucket. A rAF delta shorter than the task leaves the bucket named with `corroborated: false`.

  • The 50 ms floor on the BROWSER clause is there because under it `rafDelta − mainMs` is mostly vsync idle (D267).
takeJob(info, res, workerMs, staleN, q)Keeps an arrived job in the 25-slot worst-jobs list when its posted-to-arrived time beats the smallest kept.§15
rpf.takeJob

Its queue wait comes from the stamp `noteJob` already claimed, never a second claim.

jobsOut()The kept worst jobs as report JSON, slowest first.§15
rpf.jobsOut

`postedToArrivedMs` is the client's posted-to-arrived span, narrower than the row's queued-to-blitted `wallMs`; `postMs` and `recvMs` sit beside it and are not added in.

tallyDrop(why)Counts one drop by its reason; past 12 distinct reasons a new one counts as `other`.§15
rpf.tallyDrop

06 Connectivity and hits

Is it still one object, and did you click on it

connect.js 191 lines

Connectivity across a ceded doorway. Everything here rounds towards still-whole: an object wrongly left whole merely drags as one lump; one wrongly severed comes apart in the user's hands.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
asRect(r)Accept either rectangle shape. Plumbing.
con.asRect

Accepts either rectangle shape the codebase uses, so callers do not have to care which one they hold.

sidesOf(R, x, y, tol)Which sides of the doorway a point lies on. A corner lies on two, which is why this is a list — a ring turning the corner has to stay on the boundary through it, or one contact reads as two.§10
con.sidesOf

Which sides of the rectangle a point lies on, within a tolerance.

  • A corner lies on two, which is why this returns a list: a ring that turns the corner has to be able to stay on the boundary through it, or one contact reads as two separate ones.
tOn(R, side, x, y)A point's place in the perimeter parameter, 0 to 4. Normalised, so the parent measuring in its units and the child measuring the same rectangle 4,096× larger give the same number — no transform is ever composed across the crossing. The left side runs to 4, never round to 0: wrapping it turned a short arc into one spanning almost the whole perimeter, and severance never fired at any depth.§10
con.tOn

A point's position in the perimeter parameter — one unit per side, running 0 to 4 clockwise from the top-left corner.

  • Normalised, which is the whole trick: the parent measures the rectangle in its own units and the child measures the same rectangle thousands of times larger, and in this parameter those are the same numbers. That is what lets a contact found at one level be compared with one found at the next without ever composing a transform across the crossing.
  • The left side runs to 4, never round to 0. Wrapping it turned a short arc up the left edge into one spanning almost the whole perimeter, which then overlapped everything, and severance never fired at any depth. The circularity belongs in the comparison and nowhere else.
merge(arcs, eps)Coalesce touching intervals, so a ring with a thousand boundary vertices costs what a simple one costs.§10
con.merge

Sorts and coalesces overlapping intervals.

contactArcs(rings, rect, tol)Where a piece's ink meets the doorway, as intervals.§10
con.contactArcs

Where a piece's ink meets a doorway, as intervals in the perimeter parameter.

  • Walks each ring's edges. An edge with both ends on the same side of the rectangle contributes that whole stretch; a lone vertex on the boundary contributes a zero-length interval, which is recorded but does not by itself mean two regions are joined.
  • Coalesces the result, so a ring with a thousand boundary vertices costs the same downstream as one with two.
arcsTouch(A, B, tol)Do two pieces meet along the same stretch of doorway? This one question is the whole severance test. Compares against ±4 shifts — that is where the circularity belongs, and nowhere else.§10
con.arcsTouch

Do two sets of contacts share a stretch of the boundary?

  • A stretch, not a point — and that distinction is the whole question a cut asks. When an erase reaches the edge of a tile, the two pieces it leaves necessarily meet that edge at the *same* point, the one the eraser crossed. So a point contact is the signature of a completed cut, not of a join.
  • Accepting point contact meant a tile cut cleanly in two still reported itself as connected to both halves of its parent, and the object never came apart however carefully it was cut. Measured on the simplest case: a real contact spanning 1.47 of the perimeter against a false one of exactly zero length.
  • Compares against the interval shifted either way as well, because the perimeter is a circle and an arc straddling the origin is split across both ends.
tOfPoint · arcOverlapsThe rest of the perimeter arithmetic.§10
con.tOfPoint

The same question asked about one point instead of a ring — used by the erase debug overlay so it classifies a boundary by asking exactly what severance asks.

con.arcOverlaps

Whether two interval sets overlap at all, including at a point.

Groups: add · find
union · classes		Union-find. The family graph's connected components — the object is severed exactly when the graph falls apart.§10
con.Groups.add

Adds one member to the union-find structure.

con.Groups.find

Union-find with path compression: which component a member belongs to.

con.Groups.union

Union-find: joins two members' components. The family graph's connectivity is its cycles.

con.Groups.classes

The components, as lists of members.

Groups.constructor(n)A union-find over `n` ids, each its own class.§10
con.Groups.constructor

A union-find over `n` ids, each its own class.

hittest.js 63 lines

Distances and inside-ness for clicking.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
distToPolyline · distPointToSeg
distSegToSeg · distSegToPolyline		How far a click is from a stroke's centreline.§12
hit.distToPolyline

The shortest distance from a point to a polyline — how a click finds a stroke, with the pen width as the slack.

capsuleTouchesRings(a,b,r,rings)Does a pen-width capsule touch this ink?§12
hit.capsuleTouchesRings

Does a pen-width capsule touch this ink? The eraser's proximity test, before any boolean runs.

lasso.js 152 lines

The enclosure test the selection rule rests on.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
pointInPolygon(poly, p)Is a point inside the loop?§12
las.pointInPolygon

Is a point inside a closed loop, by ray casting.

segsCross(a, b, c, d)Do two segments cross?§12
las.segsCross

Do two segments properly cross? Four orientation signs.

rectInsidePolygon(poly, rect)Is an upright rect wholly inside the loop? The lasso's fast accept for a frame or an object's box; when it fails, the ink itself is asked (loopTester, _inkInsidePolygon).§12
las.rectInsidePolygon

Exact, not a corner test: one corner inside (even-odd) plus no loop edge crossing or lying inside the rectangle (`polygonMissesRect`). For a concave loop all four corners can be inside while the boundary dips through the middle.

  • A frame whose box it accepts is taken whole; an object it rejects is tested on its ink when its box meets the loop's box (`selection._inkInsidePolygon`, F32).
loopTester(poly)The lasso loop, prepared once to answer 'is this point inside?' and 'is this ring wholly inside?' many times.§12
las.loopTester

A ring is inside when its first vertex is inside (even-odd) and no ring segment crosses a loop edge. The loop's edges are bucketed into a 32 × 32 grid over its box, so a segment tests only the edges in the cells it touches; asking every pair cost 30 ms an object.

  • `_lassoFind` builds one per lasso for the ink test an object gets when its box fails (F32). A loop of under three points answers no to everything.
polygonMissesRect(poly, rect)Does a closed polygon's boundary stay out of a rectangle: no edge crossing a side and no vertex inside?§12
las.polygonMissesRect

With one corner inside, that makes the rectangle wholly enclosed (`rectInsidePolygon`). The erase uses it to find frames lying inside a mark's flattened ink, which it takes whole (`_eraseFramesPass`).

geometry/antRuns.js 486 lines

The selection indicator's geometry, on the pieces the renderer draws: runs split at tile seams and cut to the retained window, their lengths and SVG path data, and where the ink meets the sides of the view. Nothing is flattened.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
isCubic(p)Is this piece a cubic `[p0, p1, p2, p3]` — the capsule outline of a stroke not yet resolved?§12
ant.isCubic

Is this piece a cubic `[p0, p1, p2, p3]` — the capsule outline of a stroke not yet resolved?

isLine(p)Is this piece straight: a line, or an arc with a non-finite or non-positive radius?§12
ant.isLine

Is this piece straight: a line, or an arc with a non-finite or non-positive radius?

startOf(p)A piece's first point, cubic or not.§12
ant.startOf

A piece's first point, cubic or not.

pieceLength(p)One piece's length: a hypot for a line, r·|sweep| for an arc, the mean of chord and control polygon for a cubic.§12
ant.pieceLength

The canvas ant painter walks runs by this length too (`antPaint.paintRun`), so its dash phase and the lengths decided here agree.

runLength(pieces)The length of a run or a whole loop.§12
ant.runLength

The decision drops a run under half a pixel on screen by it.

onRectEdge(p, rect, eps)Does a straight piece lie along one side of `rect`, within `eps`? Then it is a cut — a tile seam or a cede window — not an edge the ink has.§12
ant.onRectEdge

Only a line can: an arc crosses or grazes a line and never runs along one. `loopRuns` stops the ants there, and the Renderer never splits such a line by length.

loopRuns(loop, rects)Split one loop into runs at its seam pieces, so the ants stop at a tile cut and pick up on the next piece.§12
ant.loopRuns

`rects` is `[{ rect, eps }]`: the tile that clipped the piece and its family's attach windows. A loop with no seam is one closed run; otherwise the runs are open, each the free edge between two cuts. Reads the loop through `at`, so a Loop or an array will do.

runPathData(run, ox, oy, k, plan)SVG path data for a run, relative to `(ox, oy)` and scaled by `k`, with arcs planned exactly as the ink's are.§12
ant.runPathData

The fold the renderer applies, so the numbers reaching the browser are screen-sized at any depth. Arcs go through `planArc` (the arc command, or `chordCubic` cubics), planned at `k` × 1.25, the drift a decision may make before it is redone. Two decimals, `-0.00` written `0.00`.

  • Only the SVG renderer asks for it; the canvas painter keeps the pieces. Measured at F39's density: the string cost 8.24–8.92 ms and 278.1 KB a decision, the pieces 0.33–0.65 ms.
loopsBounds(loops)The axis-aligned bounds of loops — arcs exact at the cardinal angles their sweep passes, cubics by their control points; null for nothing.§12
ant.loopsBounds

The axis-aligned bounds of loops — arcs exact at the cardinal angles their sweep passes, cubics by their control points; null for nothing.

norm(a)An angle into [0, 2π).§12
ant.norm

An angle into [0, 2π).

arcOffset(p, th)How far along an arc's sweep the angle `th` falls, from 0 at its start to |sweep| at its end, or −1 when the arc does not pass it.§12
ant.arcOffset

An angle a rounding error short of the start (1e-9 rad) reads as the start, not as a full turn away.

arcHasAngle(p, th)Does the arc pass the angle `th`?§12
ant.arcHasAngle

Does the arc pass the angle `th`?

edgeSpans(loops, rect, inside, inset)Where the ink meets each side of the view: its crossings with a line just inside each side, walked by winding into intervals.§12
ant.edgeSpans

Returns `{ left, right, top, bottom, covered }`, each side's spans clipped to it. The line runs `inset` inside the side because a boundary lying along the side is degenerate for a winding scan.

  • `covered` is the view flooded: no crossing and `inside` true at the centre, or every side spanned end to end. `overlays._selEdges` draws the edge ants and chevrons from it.
spansOf(cross, lo, hi)Crossings `[pos, dir]` along one line, sorted and walked into the intervals of non-zero winding within [lo, hi].§12
ant.spansOf

Sorts `cross` in place; intervals that touch are merged.

above(v, line)The half-open side test: a point exactly on the line counts as the low side, so a vertex on the line is crossed by exactly one of its two pieces.§12
ant.above

The half-open side test: a point exactly on the line counts as the low side, so a vertex on the line is crossed by exactly one of its two pieces.

crossVertical(p, X, out)A piece's crossings with the vertical line x = X, pushed as `[y, dir]`.§12
ant.crossVertical

Lines by interpolation under the half-open rule, arcs analytically with `arcCrossCounts` deciding the ends, cubics by `crossCubic`.

arcCrossCounts(p, th, v)The half-open rule for an arc meeting a line at angle `th` with velocity `v` across it: does this crossing count?§12
ant.arcCrossCounts

Grazing never counts. At the arc's start it counts if the arc leaves to the high side, at its end if it arrived from it, and in between always — what the line rule says of a vertex, so a vertex is counted once whichever pieces meet there.

crossCubic(c, axis, V, out)A cubic's crossings with the line `coord = V`: 24 samples along it, each sign change bisected 40 times.§12
ant.crossCubic

Pushes `[other coordinate, dir]`. Only the capsule outline of an unresolved stroke has cubics, and few are ever on screen.

crossHorizontal(p, Y, out)A piece's crossings with the horizontal line y = Y, pushed as `[x, dir]`.§12
ant.crossHorizontal

The counterpart of `crossVertical`; `insideLoops` runs its ray through it.

insideLoops(loops, pt)Is a point inside the ink? Non-zero winding from the crossings of the ray from the point towards +x.§12
ant.insideLoops

The crossing code the edge scan uses, so lines, arcs and cubics are all answered; `edgeSpans`' covered test asks it at the view's centre.

samePt(a, b)Are two points the same, within 1e-9 relative?§12
ant.samePt

Are two points the same, within 1e-9 relative?

endOf(p)A piece's last point, cubic or not.§12
ant.endOf

A piece's last point, cubic or not.

inRect(q, r)Is a point inside a rectangle, edges included?§12
ant.inRect

Is a point inside a rectangle, edges included?

arcSideOffsets(p, axis, V, out)The offsets along an arc, strictly between its ends, where it crosses the line `axis = V`.§12
ant.arcSideOffsets

The offsets along an arc, strictly between its ends, where it crosses the line `axis = V`.

clipPiece(p, rect)The parts of one piece inside `rect`, in order: a line by Liang–Barsky, an arc cut where it crosses the sides, a cubic kept whole if its hull meets the rect.§12
ant.clipPiece

An arc part is kept when its midpoint is inside and keeps the piece's own end point wherever it ends at one. A piece wholly inside comes back as itself.

localFrame · pickScale		Pick the integer scale from the geometry's own extent, then snap the origin onto that same grid. Both halves matter: local, so the scale follows the shape's size rather than its position; snapped, so it is still the global grid and two booleans over abutting geometry cannot round a shared edge two ways. Before this, error tracked how far the drawing had been panned — 137 px at 2×107 from the origin.§11

Picks the integer scale a polygon operation will run on, and the local origin it runs about.

  • Both halves matter. The scale is taken from the geometry's own extent, so it follows the shape's size rather than its position; and the origin is snapped onto that same grid, so it is still the global grid rather than a per-call one.
  • Re-centring without snapping would anchor the grid differently for every call, and two operations over abutting geometry would then round a shared edge two different ways — which is a hairline crack.
  • Before this, rounding error tracked how far the drawing had been panned: 0.07 px at the origin, 0.26 px at 10⁵, 3.7 px at 4 × 10⁶, and 137 px at 2 × 10⁷. It also caused the 'the shape changed where I did not touch it' symptom, because a boolean re-quantises its entire subject — cutting one end of a stroke moved the other end, and the far edge walked further with every later cut.

Every ring is wound positive and written into a `RingWriter`; a single point or a full reversal takes a whole disc. It needs no window, which is why it exists: the default path's caps take their span from the rect, so two plates got two caps and a hairline between them. Reached through `strokeStripNear(..., { joins: 'round', tol })`.
