08 The facade

KobinEngine.js and the five files mixed onto its prototype · routes input to the right collaborator and merges the result — and the erase jobs and the report that run beside it

It holds no geometry and no ordering logic of its own. Split here into six groups by what they are for, because reading it as one list tells you nothing.

KobinEngine · instruments

Four instruments, running at once. They exist because a timer inside the engine reported 11 ms while the browser reported a 1.5-second frame — a gap that cost four wrong diagnoses.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
LongFrames: start · _take
report · stop		The browser's own account of a slow frame: how much was script, which functions, how much was forced layout, and what is left over for painting — the one number no timer inside the engine can ever see.§15
ins.LongFrames

The browser's own account of a slow frame, kept as the worst handful.

  • Records, per slow frame: how long was spent before rendering began, when style and layout started, and a per-script breakdown with function names — including how much of each script was *forced* style and layout, which is the classic invisible cost.
  • Whatever is left after script and style-and-layout is paint and compositing, and that subtraction is the whole point: it is the one thing no timer inside the engine can ever see directly.
  • It exists because the frame meter said a frame took 1.5 seconds while every timer in the engine said the work took 11 ms. That gap cost four wrong diagnoses before this closed it.
EventLatency: start · _take
report · stop		Input to pixels, straight from the browser.§15
ins.EventLatency

Input-to-pixels latency, straight from the browser, kept as the worst handful. The only instrument that measures what the user actually waits for between touching the screen and seeing ink.

GrowthLog: maybeSample · reportWhat accumulates over a session — object counts, cached tiles, empty buckets.§15
ins.GrowthLog

What accumulates over a session: object counts, cached tiles, empty buckets, heap where the browser exposes it.

  • Sampled on a schedule rather than per operation, because the question it answers is about drift over minutes, not cost per frame.
FrameMeter: poke · _start
record · report · stop		Frame timing, always on because it costs nothing until something is slow.§15
ins.FrameMeter

Frame timing: a histogram plus the worst frames with timestamps, so a stall can be lined up against the operation log and the journal.

  • Always on, because it costs nothing until something is slow — but it cannot tell a backgrounded tab from a freeze, so very long entries need reading with that in mind.
notePerf · _perf · _noteFast
fastStats · _thin		The operation log. High-frequency operations are aggregated, or a single pinch would evict everything else; the 8 ms floor is what once hid a session with 62 seconds elapsed and 157 ms recorded.§15
eng._perf

Records one operation in the rolling performance log, with the level, the in-level zoom, a wall-clock timestamp, and any extra fields the caller supplies.

  • Below an 8 ms floor an entry is dropped unless the caller insists or trace mode is on. The floor exists because the log holds 300 entries and a single pinch would otherwise evict everything else — but it is also what once hid a session with 62 seconds elapsed and 157 ms recorded, which is why trace mode can remove it.
eng._noteFast

Aggregates a high-frequency operation instead of logging each one.

  • Zoom and pan steps happen hundreds of times per gesture. Keeping a count, a total and a worst case costs nothing and survives in the log, where individual entries would be evicted within seconds.
_note(entry)The journal: what the user did, not what the document became. Which erase, where, at what zoom, what it cut, whether the object came apart — and why anything was refused.§15
eng._note

Appends an entry to the journal — the record of what the *user* did, as opposed to what the document ended up as.

  • A stroke entry carries the pen width, the line width in frame units, and a thinned copy of the samples. An erase entry carries the eraser size and an initially empty list of cuts that the background worker fills in as it goes.
  • This is what turns a bug report from a snapshot of wreckage into a sequence of gestures that produced it.
reportFamilies · _keepDebugMark
_eraseDebugOverlay		Diagnostics for multi-level families and for what a mark actually touched.§15
eng.reportFamilies

Diagnostics for multi-level objects: which pieces belong to which family, where their doorways are, and what an erase actually touched — the report fields that made severance debuggable at all.

KobinEngine and the files mixed onto it

Wiring, settings, the two render paths — and, since the 2026-08-31 split, the five files whose methods engine/mixin.js copies back onto this same prototype: erasePipeline, overlays, selection, sceneOps, files. They are still the engine’s methods; they live in another file. instruments, rectMath, mixin and now are the small pieces that came out with them.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
constructor · resize · destroyWires the collaborators together and subscribes to the document so a vanishing object cannot leave a stale selection.§4
engine-life.constructor

Wires the collaborators together: the box tree, the document, the camera, the tile cache and the renderer.

  • Injects one pure function into the document so it can convert between boxes without owning a camera or a tree.
  • Subscribes to the document so a vanishing object cannot leave a stale selection — and deliberately ignores a re-home, which is a change of address rather than the object going away.
activeLevel · inScale · inPanX
inPanY · nativesByLevel
crossings · levelObjects
tiles · _hasFat		The compatibility surface the interface and the tests read. Pass-throughs.
engine-life.activeLevel

The compatibility surface the interface and the tests read: camera fields, objects by box, the record view, the current display list, and the ported display invariants. Pass-throughs.

setTool · setPenType · setColor
setWidth · setOpacity
setEraserSize · setOpacityGroups
setDebug · setPreBake · setTrace
setRetainScenes · setScaleDef
setLazyOutlines · setTileDebug
setEraseDebug		Tool and diagnostic settings. Plumbing — except that leaving the select tool drops the selection.
eng.setTool

Tool and diagnostic settings, mostly plumbing. `setTool` drops the selection when the tool leaves select, so the indicator cannot linger over a drawing being edited; `setTrace` clears the operation log so a trace starts clean.

_buildList()Merge the tile pieces and the active frame's own objects in id order — so a newer object always draws over an older one regardless of which class it arrived by.§9 §12
_render · _visibleChangedRender, or decide a camera-only sync is enough.§9
eng._render

A full render: on the raster path the frame's perf row opens first; then `_buildList`, `_drainPlates` (after the build, which itself emits), the renderer's render and update, and status. Carries queued by this render's settles are applied to the selection at its end (`_flushCarried`, F93). Ends by poking the frame meter and restarting the ladder's quiet timer.

  • The frame meter is poked here as well as in gestures: the worst stall seen was a cold one, opening a drawing at a deep camera.
eng._visibleChanged

Has the set of visible tiles changed since the last full render?

  • This is the cheap question that decides whether a camera move needs a rebuild or just a new transform.
panBy · zoomAt · zoomFactorAt
pinchUpdate		Input to the camera, then settle and re-render once.§5
eng.panBy

Pan by a pixel delta. A full render when the visible tile set changed, the view drifted past the re-origin budget, or it left the chop window's inner half; otherwise one transform. Restarts the ladder's quiet timer.

eng.zoomFactorAt

Zoom about a point; wheel and pinch both arrive here. The camera applies it, possibly crossing a level or stepping into a neighbouring cell.

  • A full render when the level was crossed, the visible tile set changed, a pending fat stroke must flip to its outline, a piece crossed the fully-present line, the view drifted past the re-origin budget, or it left the chop window's budget. Otherwise one transform is written and nothing is rebuilt. On the raster path the last three are always false.
  • Then the crossing prebake at idle, the ladder's quiet timer restarted, and idle outline fits queued after a crossing or when fat strokes near the gate.
_maybePrebake · _queueIdleFitsWarm the frame an approaching crossing leads to, up or down — on the raster path its plates and a preview — and fit outlines while idle.§9
eng._queueIdleFits

Schedules outline fitting for wide strokes during idle time, so a stroke that is approaching the display gate has its outline ready before it needs it.

_emit · _effectiveZoom
_levelPointToScreen · _objs
_fatOnScreen · _frameWindow
_debugTileRects		Status reporting and the ported display invariants.§15
eng._emit

Publishes the status the interface reads: level, in-level zoom, absolute zoom, whether a crossing is near, and the object count.

KobinEngineThe facade the whole app talks to.§8
eng.KobinEngine

Wires the frame lattice, the document, the camera, the tile cache and a renderer together (the SVG `Renderer`, or `RasterRenderer` with a `PlateStore` when constructed with `raster`) and routes input to whichever one owns it.

  • Its own methods: construction and teardown, the compat accessors, the tool and style setters, the perf log and journal, the render list (`_buildList`, `listFor`), the raster path's plate drain, the drag's plate hold and its one exit (`_endMove`), the crossing prebake and the zoom-out ladder, pan and zoom, pointer input, undo, redo and clear (DESIGN.md §15).
  • Five files are mixed onto the prototype by `mixin.js` (erasePipeline, overlays, selection, files, sceneOps); their methods run with `this` bound to the engine, and `mixin` throws if two claim one name. The quasi-private surface is pinned by `KobinEngine.contract.test.js`.
_beginHold()At a drag's start, records the members and selected frames whose plate events wait until the drop.§9
eng._beginHold

Raster path only, and only when the renderer's drag plane accepts the selection (`planeAccepts`, which also aims the plane); otherwise `_holdMove` stays null and the drag re-rasters each step. Records each member's id, home frame and table, the selected frame roots, and the roots' footprints in every frame the plate cache holds (`_framesFootIn`).

  • Taken once, from `_beginSelectDrag`; released once, by `_releaseMove` (PAPER-PLAN R3).
_planeLost()The renderer's drag plane can no longer draw the drag: releases the hold once, so each step renders.§9
eng._planeLost

Called by `RasterRenderer` when the camera leaves the plane's frame or the view leaves plates under a live drag. Runs `_releaseMove` and clears the drag's `listAt`, so the ants decide from the list as it stands, which now holds the move. Returns the plates dropped.

_planeState()The selection's ids in the current render list, for the raster renderer's drag plane; null with nothing selected.§9
eng._planeState

Collects the members' ids (`_selectionMembers`) and adds every listed piece homed under a selected frame, found by its home, so a selected subtree costs the list's length rather than its object count. Memoised on the selection object and the list; returns `{ key, ids }`.

  • Pulled by `RasterRenderer` each camera step, so the plane is ready before a drag starts (PAPER-PLAN §10 S4). Null on the SVG path.
_dragState()The live drag as the renderer pulls it each frame: the gesture, the held ids and frame roots, and the pointer at the first read.§9
eng._dragState

Null unless a drag is under way and a plate hold was taken. `RasterRenderer._planeStep` moves its plane by the gesture's `last - start`.

_endMove(why)The one exit of a drag (drop, cancel, delete, deselect, undo): releases everything the drag held, renders once, and keeps selected what the drag moved out of the selection.§6
eng._endMove

Takes the drag and its carried ids, runs `_dropHold`, then `_render` with `_dropping` set, so the carries that render's settles make join the drag's. Then, on a drop or when anything was carried, `_reselect`s the carried natives and, on a drop, the dragged frames no selected frame holds any more (`_outsideSelection`) (DESIGN.md §10, F93).

  • On a drop it runs after the move's undo entry is pushed, so a shadow merge the render triggers is recorded on that entry (DESIGN.md §8).
_dropHold(why)`_endMove` without the render, for a document event where rendering would re-enter.§6
eng._dropHold

Clears the drag gesture and its carried ids, turns off the tile cache's batch mode and the Document's merge hold, releases the plate hold (`_releaseMove`), and tells the renderer (`endMove(why, dropped)`) if a drag or a hold was live. The selection's document subscription uses it on a reset or when the last member goes.

_releaseMove()Releases a drag's held plate events as one collapsed invalidation.§9
eng._releaseMove

Drops every plate painting a member, then every plate under the members' drawn boxes at their start and end addresses (`_movedRectsIn`). When frames moved, removes every plate of a moved frame or one under it and stales the subtrees' start and end footprints in the other frames. Clears `_holdMove` first, so it runs once; returns the plates dropped.

  • PAPER-PLAN §5.4's rules 1-4, applied once per drag instead of once per event.
screenToFrame(sx, sy)A screen point in the camera frame's own units; a pass-through to the camera.
eng.screenToFrame

A screen point in the camera frame's own units; a pass-through to the camera.

latticeStep(rect)One step of the integer lattice a boolean would round to, at this rect's scale.§5
rmt.latticeStep

Chosen from the largest magnitude in play, which is what the polygon library does internally.

  • It matters because 'this vertex sits ON the window's edge' has to be judged at that step and not at float epsilon: at a parent's own scale one step is about a thousandth of a unit, which is three whole units - hundreds of screen pixels - down among its children.
rectTol(r)Twice the lattice step: the tolerance a contact is judged at.§5
rmt.rectTol

Used wherever the engine asks whether ink reaches a tile edge. Deriving it from the rect rather than fixing it is what makes the answer mean the same thing at every depth.

rectSpan(r)The larger side of a rect, never zero.§5
rmt.rectSpan

The denominator that turns an absolute tolerance into the normalised perimeter units contacts are compared in.

mixin(target, ...protos)Copies a mixin class's methods onto another prototype, and refuses to overwrite one.§8
mix.mixin

`Object.assign` copies nothing here: class prototype methods are non-enumerable, so it would silently produce an engine with no methods. Descriptors also carry getters and setters intact, which a value copy would invoke and flatten.

  • It throws when two files claim the same name, which is the check that keeps the six files honest - a method duplicated during a move fails the very first test that builds an engine, rather than shadowing its twin.
perfNow()Monotonic time, falling back to the wall clock.§8
now.perfNow

One definition for the whole engine, so every measurement in a report is on the same clock.

KobinEngine · pointer and pen

Drawing, and the resolve queue behind it.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
pointerDown · pointerMove
pointerUp		Timed at the boundary, so the cost of a gesture is measured where the user feels it.§15
eng.pointerDown

The public entry for a press: times `_pointerDown` and records it as `ptrDown` in the operation log (past the 8 ms floor, or always in trace mode) and in the `_noteFast` distribution.

  • Input handlers are where a user feels cost, so the boundary is what is measured.
eng.pointerMove

The public entry for a drag. Times the call and delegates to `_pointerMove`.

  • This fires many times a second, so everything inside is designed to be cheap — the pen appends one sample, the drag recomputes one displacement.
eng.pointerUp

The public entry for a release. Times the call and delegates to `_pointerUp`.

  • Also called indirectly by the camera: crossing a level finalises any live stroke first, through a hook, so a stroke is never left half-written across two coordinate systems.
_pointerDown · _pointerMove
_pointerUp		Everything a gesture can be: draw, erase, pan, lasso, drag. The select tool changes nothing on the way down: a tap selects at pen-up, and a move past SELECT_DRAG_PX starts a drag or a lasso. Pen-up journals a stroke, finalises it, queues the resolve, and pushes exactly one undo entry.§7 §10 §12
eng._pointerDown

Starts the gesture, by tool. First a stroke still open (its pen-up never arrived) is finished as a pen-up would, and a select press or lasso left behind by a tool change is dropped.

  • Pan, or any press while `readOnly` (another tab or device has the pen): remember the point. Whole-object eraser: delete what is under the point. Area eraser: start a background-coloured stroke through the pen pipeline; the cut happens later, in the background.
  • Select: nothing changes on the way down. The press is recorded with what lies under it (`_selPress`); `_pointerMove` turns it into a lasso or a move once it travels SELECT_DRAG_PX, `_pointerUp` treats it as a tap if it never did, and a pinch forgets it (`cancelSelectGesture`).
  • Pen: allocate an id, build the stroke at the pen width over the zoom, attach its live arc chain (`_startPen`), add it to the document as live (unindexed while it grows), and hand it to the renderer.
eng._pointerMove

Extends what `_pointerDown` started. Pan (or read-only) moves the camera; the whole-object eraser erases under the point; the area eraser falls through to the pen path, because it is a stroke.

  • Select: a lasso appends a point once the pointer has moved more than a pixel; a press waits until it has travelled SELECT_DRAG_PX, then `_beginSelectDrag` decides lasso or move; a move in progress takes one `_dragSelection` step.
  • Pen: the sample goes into the stroke and its live arc chain, which rebuilds only the last two gaps, O(1) a point; the line tool replaces its second point and re-seeds a two-sample pen instead.
eng._pointerUp

Ends the gesture. Tap: a select press that never moved goes to `_selectTap`. Lasso: apply the loop if it moved and has three points, then always redraw the selection layer, or the loop stays on screen.

  • Drag: if anything moved, each member whose stored bbox centre has left its cell is re-homed by whole frames (`_normalizeHome`, the one case a move writes coordinates, so its entry keeps geometry snapshots); the move is journaled and pushed as one undo entry, `moveFrames` when frames moved, else `move` or `moveMany`, each member's frames and tables either side. Then `_endMove('drop')`, after the op is on the stack.
  • Stroke: journal it before its samples go, end the live path, finalise it in the document, queue its perimeter resolve and schedule the bake. An eraser pushes one `eraseCommit` entry its background cuts append to; anything else one `add`. Then the one render a pen-up makes.
_startPen(o)Attach the live arc chain, at a tolerance set by the zoom it is drawn at — the moment the raw stroke is swapped for its outline is the only moment the difference could be seen.§7
eng._startPen

Attaches a live arc chain (`BiarcPen`) to a stroke about to be drawn, seeded with its first sample, at a tolerance of half the arc tolerance at the zoom it is drawn at.

  • Every stroke gets one, the line tool included. The swap from the live chain to the resolved shape is the only moment their difference could show, and at this tolerance it is sub-pixel there.
cancelStroke()Abandon the in-progress stroke.§7
eng.cancelStroke

Abandons the in-progress stroke and removes it from the document — used where a gesture is interrupted rather than completed.

_queueBake · _ensureShapeBakes
_stepShapeBakes		The pen-up resolve queue, run in slices. _ensureShapeBakes is the guarantee that no stroke is left raw for ever — after a load, an undo, or a job dropped because its object went away.§7
erp._queueBake

Queues a drawn stroke's perimeter resolve as a job with a cursor in it.

  • Hands the job the arc chain the live pen already built, which skips the single most expensive phase of the resolve — it was paid for a few microseconds at a time while the user drew.
  • Deliberately leaves the pen chain attached to the object: it is what the renderer draws until the resolved outline lands, so the ink does not change shape at pen-up and again when the bake finishes.
erp._ensureShapeBakes

Walks the whole document and queues a resolve for any stroke that is still raw.

  • Cheap, and it is the only thing guaranteeing no stroke is left unresolved forever — after a load, after an undo, or after a job was dropped because its object had been erased while it sat in the queue.
erp._stepShapeBakes

Runs perimeter resolves for up to a time budget and reports whether more remain.

  • For each queued job: skip it if its object is gone or no longer a raw stroke, step it with the time left, and when it finishes install the result: seal an unclosed outline (`_sealed`), bake the stroke into its shape in place, and promote it a level if it is now wider than a frame (`_promoteOversize`).
  • A promotion renders at once (the object changed frames). Otherwise the resolved shape waits for the next render (`_renderPending`, honoured by `flushBakes`): two renders a pen-up were 185 s of a 203 s jsdom session at 1,000 strokes.
  • On a raster engine the plates hold the raw band until re-rastered. A stroke homed in the camera's frame is its own list item, so a camera step re-posts them and no list is built; one homed elsewhere is a projected copy the old list still holds raw, so it takes a render (OPEN-FLAGS F92).
flushBakes · _forceBake(o)Resolve now: for tests, and wherever an erase has reached an object that has not resolved yet.§7
erp._forceBake

Resolves one stroke's perimeter immediately, cancelling any queued job for it.

  • Used where an erase has reached an object that has not resolved yet — the boolean needs both operands as outlines and cannot wait for the queue.
_sealed(res, w)An outline that does not close is sealed rather than refused — the stroke has to become something — and how much edge was fabricated is recorded, because a seal a fifth of the pen wide is invisible and one at 45% is a line drawn across the stroke.§7
erp._sealed

Guarantees a resolved outline actually closes.

  • A stroke whose two edges fail to stitch would otherwise be stored as its two rails plus the slivers between them: no boundary, no meaningful inside, nothing painted, and a drawing that cannot be saved at all because the file format validates closure.
  • Refusing is not an option — the stroke has to become something — so unclosed chains are stitched together and closed with straight lines, and the resulting dust is dropped.
  • Records how much edge was fabricated. A seal a fifth of the pen wide is invisible; one at 45% of the loop's perimeter is a straight line drawn across the middle of a stroke, and the two are indistinguishable without the number.
_promoteOversize(id)Invariant 2, enforced. A stroke wider than a box is promoted to the level above, dividing every coordinate by 4,096 — a change of units, not a loss of accuracy.§5
erp._promoteOversize

Enforces the rule that an object never reaches past its box's immediate neighbours.

  • If the object's extent exceeds one box width, it is moved to the parent level: every coordinate divided by the crossing ratio, which is a power of two, so this is a change of units and not a loss of accuracy — the mantissa is untouched and only the exponent moves.
  • The object becomes a small, finely-detailed object one level up, where the rule holds with room to spare. Repeats until it fits, which for any real gesture is never or once.
  • Line width and pen width are scaled to match, because they are lengths in the same units.

KobinEngine · erasing

The instant mark, the background cut, the descent, and the question of whether the object came apart.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
eraseAt · _eraseWhole(id)The whole-object eraser.§10
erp.eraseAt

The whole-object eraser: hit-test at the point and remove what is under it, as one undo entry.

setEraserSize(px)
_zOf · _doneSet		Eraser size and bookkeeping. Plumbing.
_eraseStrokes()Eraser gestures whose own outline has resolved, oldest first. One still raw is not skipped — it is simply not ready yet.§10
erp._eraseStrokes

Collects the eraser gestures that have a resolved outline, oldest first.

  • An eraser that is still raw is not skipped, it is simply not ready — the same tick resolves outlines before it touches erases, so it arrives here a tick later.
_scheduleBake(delay)One timer, and the soonest request wins — otherwise a pending erase would delay every stroke's resolve behind it.§10
erp._scheduleBake

Arms the single background timer.

  • One timer, and the soonest request wins: a pending 400 ms erase timer must not delay a stroke's resolve, which wants to run immediately. If a sooner deadline arrives the existing timer is cleared and replaced.
_camBusy · _bakeTick
_bakeTickInner		The background loop. Resolve outlines first (an eraser cannot be subtracted until it has one), then fold erasers into ink in slices — charging the next object at what the last one actually cost, and never starving for more than a second and a half.§10
erp._camBusy

True if the camera moved recently enough that a background slice would land on a frame the user is watching.

  • A simple timestamp comparison against a fixed idle window. Being wrong in the cautious direction only delays work; being wrong the other way drops a frame.
erp._bakeTick

The background worker's entry point. Wraps the real work in timing.

  • This is timed because it was once the largest piece of untimed main-thread work in the engine: a slice is budgeted at 8 ms but one object can cost far more, and until it was instrumented none of that reached a report.
erp._bakeTickInner

One slice of background work, then re-arms itself if anything is left.

  • Stands aside while the pointer is down or a drag is in progress, and for a short window after the camera moves — but never for more than about a second and a half in total, so a restless camera cannot starve the queue.
  • Resolves outlines first. An eraser cannot be subtracted until it has a resolved outline, and neither can the ink beneath it.
  • Then folds erasers into ink, object by object, charging the next object at what the last one actually cost so a slice sitting at 7.9 ms does not start another expensive one. A single object costing more than the whole budget still runs, or it would be refused forever.
  • When every object under a mark has been handled, the white mark is removed silently — undo goes through its commit entry, not through the mark.
_nextEraseTarget(Erec)The next object to bake under a mark: the highest by z still under it that the mark's box reaches, after the pass that takes a covered frame whole. Reachability is the only bar.§10
_eraseMayTouch(E, HE, o, HO)A cheap prefilter in the target's frame, projecting the eraser's box and not its geometry. The old form put a whole perimeter inside a loop that runs once per object per scan: 128 ms per slice on a crowded screen.§10
erp._eraseMayTouch

A cheap rejection test: could this eraser possibly touch this object?

  • Projects the eraser's bounding box, not its geometry, into the target's frame — a box maps to a box exactly, and costs a constant amount where projecting the outline rebuilds one arc per piece.
  • The box is cached against the eraser's edit counter so it is computed once per gesture rather than once per candidate.
  • Only has to be cheap and never wrongly negative; the boolean itself is the arbiter and its no-op guard absorbs false positives. The earlier version put a whole perimeter inside a loop that runs once per object per scan and cost 128 ms per slice on a crowded screen.
_eraseOp(E)Resolve the gesture's undo entry before touching the document — a cut that cannot record itself must not happen, because unrecorded cuts were how duplicated, stacked geometry formed.§10
erp._eraseOp

Finds or creates the undo entry that a gesture's background cuts append to.

  • Always called before the document is touched: a cut that cannot record itself must not happen, because unrecorded cuts were how duplicated, stacked geometry formed.
  • After a reload the map is empty, so resumed baking registers a fresh entry — which also makes a resumed erase undoable again.
_bakeOne(Erec, target)One mark against one object. Ceded downward by the descent when the object is homed shallower on an ancestor chain; otherwise cut in place as a job (eraseJob.cutJob), in the erase worker where there is one, applied on the main thread by _applyCut.§10 §11
_noteSeal(res, subject)Count the booleans that had to be sealed. A rise here is the stitch getting worse.§11
erp._noteSeal

Counts the booleans that had to be closed with a fabricated chord.

  • The boolean guarantees closed loops by sealing a chain the walk could not finish. That is a real if small geometric compromise, so it is counted rather than hidden — a rise here is the stitch getting worse.
_inkOutline(o, tol)An object's ink as polygon rings at a tolerance — for the connectivity walk, the erase-debug join notes and the lasso's ink test.§10
erp._inkOutline

A shape is flattened, a fill is its own rings, a stroke is outlined first. The family connectivity walk (`_familyComponents`), the erase-debug join notes (`_familyJoinNotes`) and the lasso's ink test (`_inkInsidePolygon`) read it.

_familyMembers · _familyComponentsThe family graph. Every member is a node; two are joined when their ink meets on the same stretch of a ceded doorway. Asks a geometric question, not whether two boxes are formally parent and child — re-homing can settle two members on different branches in the same place.§10
erp._familyMembers

Every object sharing one family key, across all levels.

  • A family is the pieces of one logical object that ended up at different levels because an erase ceded tiles downward.
erp._familyComponents

Decides whether a family is still one object, by building a graph and finding its connected components.

  • Every member is a node. The only place two members can meet is the boundary of a ceded tile — the parent stops exactly at the rectangle and the child fills exactly the rectangle — so that boundary is where the question is asked.
  • For each member holding a doorway, the rectangle is mapped into each one-level-coarser member's frame and both inks are asked where they touch it. Contact is compared in a perimeter parameter running 0 to 4, so the parent's units and the child's much larger ones give the same numbers and no transform is composed across the crossing.
  • The partner is found geometrically, not by ancestry. Requiring a literal parent box made connectivity depend on bookkeeping: re-homing can settle two members of one object on different branches while sitting in the same place, and the object was reported as three without changing at all.
_resplitFamily(op, key)Severance as pure re-labelling. No geometry is touched, because ceding already left the parent in pieces. The first component keeps the original key so an existing selection stays valid.§10
erp._resplitFamily

Re-labels a family into its connected components, and reports whether it came apart.

  • Pure identity work — no geometry is touched, because ceding already left the parent in pieces. Severance used to need a second cut through the parent, which declined on any cut that was not dead straight, which is what a real scribbled erase always looks like.
  • The first component keeps the original key so a selection already pointing at it stays valid; the rest get fresh keys. The key changes are recorded on the gesture's undo entry so one undo unwinds geometry and identity together.
_bakeRehome · _bakeRehomeInnerThe descent, as one job for the family (eraseDescent.descentJob), in the worker where there is one: every cede virtual, each level's square ink the store's own piece, nothing applied until the whole descent has succeeded (_applyDescent).§10
_rehomeBail · _noteSpentRecord why a cede refused, and what a spent mark looked at. A refusal is otherwise invisible, and invisible refusal is exactly what "I erase and it just disappears" looks like.§15
erp._rehomeBail

Records why a descent refused, against the gesture that made it.

  • A refusal is otherwise invisible: the object is already in the eraser's done set, so the erase never returns to it, and if nothing else was under the gesture the mark is consumed having done nothing. That is exactly what 'I erase and then it just disappears' looks like from the outside.
erp._noteSpent

When a mark is about to be consumed having cut nothing, records what it considered.

  • The done set is the list of everything the gesture looked at and dismissed, so writing it down turns 'the eraser did nothing' from a mystery into a list of objects with a reason beside each.
_flushErasesFor · flushErases
_settleSelectionErases		The barrier: nothing is dragged out from under a mark that has not been applied yet, or the ink takes its un-erased shape with it and the mark stays behind to cut whatever arrives.§10
erp.flushErases

Resolves every pending stroke, lands the cut in flight first when its mark is included (a mark with its last cut in flight looks spent), then bakes each mark's targets, oldest mark first, with `_bakeOne` in sync mode and consumes the mark when nothing is left under it. Never uses the worker; only the landed cut in flight steps a mark down.

  • The tests' settle point, and the barriers': a lasso (`_settleLassoErases`, the marks it meets) and a drag holding a selected frame (every mark).
ErasePipelineThe eraser and the resumable bake behind it, as a mixin.§6
erp.ErasePipeline

Never instantiated. Its prototype is copied onto KobinEngine's, so every method here runs with `this` bound to the engine.

  • A class rather than an object literal because that made the split a MOVE: every method arrived byte-identical, comments and indentation included, with no reformatting for a reviewer to read past. `mixin.js` says why `Object.assign` cannot do the copying.
_candidatesUnder(Erec)The objects still to handle under a mark, top-down by z, from the spatial index; cached on the mark.§10
erp._candidatesUnder

For every level with a route to the mark's frame, that level's index is queried with the mark's box mapped there; every reachable moved object is added too, since it is indexed at its stored bits and drawn elsewhere. Marks, handled ids and anything at or above the mark's z are skipped; the list is sorted by z, then id, highest first.

  • Cached on the mark (`_zScan`) with a cursor, rebuilt when the document's revision or the mark's z changes. Each candidate is checked again when its turn comes (DESIGN.md §7).
_eraseFramesPass(Erec)Before a mark's first target: takes whole the frames its ink covers and that hold nothing drawn above it.§10
erp._eraseFramesPass

Walks frames as the lasso does, out from the mark's frame one hop at a time, skipping a subtree whose box misses the mark. A frame other than the mark's own is taken when its cell grown by the content's reach (invariant 2) and the flatten tolerance lies inside the mark's ink (a corner inside, no flattened chord touching it) and `Document.maxZUnder` is below the mark's z; a taken frame is not descended into.

  • Each subtree is set aside by reference (`removeFrameSubtree`) as one `{ frames }` bake step on the gesture's op, with a journal note; no cut. Runs once per mark per session (`_framesPassed`); after a reload it runs again and finds the frames already gone. Returns how many went (DESIGN.md §7).
_eraserRectInto(rect, HE, o, HO)A mark's rect, drawn in frame HE, in the coordinates object `o` is stored in at its home HO.§10
erp._eraserRectInto

With no table it is `mapRectF`, bit for bit; a moved object's table is undone on the way in (`LevelMap.mapRectObj` with `toHome`). The erase prefilter's box goes through it.

_eraserLoopsInto(loops, HE, o, HO)The mark's loops in the coordinates object `o` is stored in: the clip of an in-place cut.§10
erp._eraserLoopsInto

`LevelMap.projectLoopsObj` with `toHome`: the exact chain, through the object's table when it has one.

_applyCut(Erec, target, r, ctx)The document side of one cut: `cutJob`'s verdict applied and recorded on the gesture's op.§10
erp._applyCut

Nothing if the mark or the target has gone. Adds the seal and dust tallies; a graze changes nothing and takes the target out of the mark's `_uncutOf` set (no ink under the mark, F109). A cut replaces the target with the surviving regions (`eraseReplaceById`) and puts the pieces in the done set; a removal takes the target out. Each is one bake step, with a journal note.

  • The replacement or removal runs inside `_neutralUnder`, so while the mark is above the target the raster plates are kept (its white already paints what went); the target then leaves the mark's `_uncutOf` set, so the mark's step past it is neutral too (F90).
  • A cut that left several regions inside a multi-level family asks `_resplitFamily` whether the object came apart. Returns true when the document changed.
_descentWorld()What a descent job reads from the engine: the lattice, the config, the canvas width and the opacity groups.§10
erp._descentWorld

The world `eraseDescent.descentJob` runs in on the main thread; the worker gets the same fields with the lattice serialised. Tests replace it to watch or fault the square ink.

_applyDescent(Erec, target, r, ctx)The document side of a descent: the target's family swapped for the one the job built.§10
erp._applyDescent

Adds the seal and dust tallies; a refusal is recorded on the gesture's note (`_rehomeBail`), and one the job marks `inkless` takes the target out of the mark's `_uncutOf` set (F109). Nothing if the target was replaced or the mark has gone. The frames the job minted are merged into the lattice first (F67).

  • Then each step in order: its removed object (the target, or one minted a step earlier) taken out, its parents and kids added with real ids in the job's order, virtual ids mapped as it goes, every piece put in the done set. The swap runs inside `_neutralUnder`: the pieces land where the ink was, so under the mark's white no pixel moves (F90).
  • The steps go on the op newest last, so undo unwinds the chain bottom up; the target leaves the mark's `_uncutOf` set; then `_resplitFamily` asks whether the family is still one object.
_removedArea(subject, clip)The area an erase removes, measured as the area of the intersection (F46). Nothing calls it.§10
erp._removedArea

`eraseJob.cutJob` measures the removal the same way inside the job. The intersection's pieces are no longer than the eraser, so its area is exact to the eraser's own ulps where before-minus-after is not.

_boolOpts()The boolean's one option, the freeze radius at this engine's tolerance, passed to every cut and descent job.§11
erp._boolOpts

So an erase stands in for an arc by its chord exactly where the tile chain would have frozen it, and nowhere else (DESIGN.md §5).

KobinEngine · selection and moving

Clicking, lassoing, dragging — and the marching-ants geometry.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
_isSelected(id)
_selectableRects · _rectInActive		Is a native selected (its id, a family member's id, or its home under a selected frame); every native's box in the active frame, the ground truth the suites check the lasso against; one object's box there, through its displacement table.§12
sel._selectableRects

Walks every frame's natives through `Document.at` (which settles pending shifts) and maps each box with `_rectInActive`. No production caller.

sel._rectInActive

One object's bounding rectangle, mapped into the active frame's coordinates.

  • Returns nothing when the two frames have no path between them, which silently drops the object from consideration.
_lassoFind(poly)The tree query. Every frame gets one of three answers — out of reach, enclosed (one entry of the selection: the frame, nothing under it read), or straddling (ask its index and recurse). Walks outward from the current frame, because from the root the scale factor would be 4,096depth before the first useful comparison.§6 §12
sel._lassoFind

Finds what a lasso fully encloses by walking the frame tree outward from the active frame, one hop at a time: out of reach skips a frame and its subtree; enclosed makes the frame one entry of the selection, nothing under it read; straddling asks the frame's index and tests each candidate's box, then its ink (`_inkInsidePolygon`) where the box meets the loop's box. A frame with no native in its subtree (`_inkedFrames`) is skipped, so an empty visited cell is never selected (F93).

  • Objects with a displacement table are indexed at their stored bits and drawn elsewhere, so each one the active frame can reach is judged again where its picture is (F69). A family is taken only when every piece is in; a keyless native is a family of one. Returns `{ ids, frames }`.
  • The prune rests on invariant 2: a frame's subtree lies inside its cell grown by one (DESIGN.md §10).
_setSelection · _toggleSelected
_applyLasso · select · deselect		Selection state, including the ctrl rules: a loop overlapping the selection adds, one drawn purely inside removes.§12
sel._setSelection

Installs ids and frames as the selection, keeping only live ids and frames the lattice still has; with neither it deselects. The primary member (id, edit key, level, object) is the first live id, or the first frame when there are no ids.

  • Families are not expanded here; `_isSelected` and `_selectionMembers` resolve them. Redraws the overlays with a camera-only sync and emits status.
sel._toggleSelected

Adds or removes one object from the selection — the ctrl-click behaviour.

sel._applyLasso

Turns a finished loop into a selection change. First every pending eraser mark whose box meets the loop is applied (`_settleLassoErases`), so the lasso finds the cut-outs rather than the ink under an unapplied mark.

  • Plain: replace the selection, or deselect when the loop caught nothing. Ctrl with the loop catching anything new: add. Ctrl with the loop catching nothing new (drawn inside the selection): remove.
sel.select

Selects whatever is under a point, replacing the current selection.

_selectionRect()The visible union of the selection's families in the active frame. Only the suites read it.§12
sel._selectionRect

Unions the drawn boxes (bbox, half the line width, the residual) of every listed piece whose family is selected. With none drawn: the primary member's box where its picture is (F68), or failing that its box in its own frame.

_dragSelection(sx, sy)The move. Each member's new home and displacement table from the displacement since the drag started, once per home frame; selected frames re-addressed. No stored coordinate is touched. Every member expands the same displacement, so members sharing an ancestor take identical digits and cannot drift apart.§6
sel._dragSelection

Recomputed from where the drag started. The displacement is snapped to 2^-10 of the camera level's unit (F55); each member's new home and table is computed once per (home frame, starting table) (`_displaceMember`); re-homes are one `rehomeManyById` a target frame, table changes one `setOffsetsById` each. No stored coordinate is touched (DESIGN.md §8).

  • Selected frames move as frames (`_dragFramesStart`, `_dragFrames`). With the raster drag plane drawing the move, the step is a camera-only sync and no list is built; otherwise it renders.
  • Members sharing a home frame and a table take one answer, so their relative positions cannot drift. A member it could not move is recorded with why and journaled at pen-up (F35).
_normalizeHome(id)Put an object back inside its own box after a move, so invariant 2 holds again before anything else looks at the document.§5
_selectionMembers · deleteSelection
_selectionStatus		The selection's ids with their families, and what happens to them: delete removes the objects and sets selected frames aside as containers (removeFrames).§12
sel._selectionMembers

The selected ids plus the rest of each one's family, de-duplicated, as document records. Selected frames are not expanded: the drag moves them as frames and delete sets them aside as containers.

sel.deleteSelection

First brings the selection up to date: pending carries are applied (`_flushCarried`), and mid-drag the carried natives and the frames the drag tore out join it (`_reselect`).

  • Then removes every selected id and its family one by one, and every selected frame's subtree as containers (`Document.removeFrameSubtree`, O(frames)), skipping a frame under another selected one. One undo entry: `eraseMany`, `removeFrames`, or `deleteMany` holding both. Ends a live drag through `_endMove('delete')`, then deselects and renders.
sel._selectionStatus

The count is the ids plus each selected frame's subtree count (`_subtreeCount`); a frame under another selected one is counted once, through that one. Style is not reported: nothing downstream edits a selection's colour, width or opacity.

_shapeHit · hitTestAt · _hitTestClicking: the topmost thing under the cursor. This is how you reach something at depth, where no loop can bound anything.§12
sel._shapeHit

Is this point inside a resolved outline, allowing a little slack?

sel._hitTest

What is under this point? Returns the topmost object, or nothing.

  • Walks the display list from the top down, testing resolved shapes by inside-ness and raw strokes by distance to their centreline with the pen width as slack.
_selectionAnts()The selection indicator handed to the renderer: ant runs and dots in retained space, a transform, and the screen-edge spans — built from the pieces the render list draws, never from the document. During a drag the first decision is kept and moved by the pointer's travel.§12
ovl._selectionAnts

Builds or reuses a decision (`_selTable`, `_selDecide`) and adds the edge spans (`_selEdges`) per step. During a drag the first decision is kept and moved by the pointer's travel. Null when nothing is selected, the tool is not select, or nothing traces (DESIGN.md §10).

_outlineInView · _splitOnJoins
_familyJoinNotes · _emitOutlineRing		The erase-debug overlay's geometry: an object's boundary clipped to the view, cut where a family join starts and ends, orange where the edge is the piece's own and green where it is a join.§12
ovl._outlineInView

A shape's rings come from `shapeRingsInRect`; a shape whose ink floods the window has no boundary in view and returns none. A fill's rings are clipped to the rect; anything else returns none.

ovl._splitOnJoins

Returns the segment's parts flagged joined or not, or null when it is nowhere near a shared edge. A straight side flattens to one chord, so without the cut a partial join would colour the whole side.

ovl._familyJoinNotes

Recorded against both pieces, each in its own level's coordinates, and cached per family keyed by its members and their edit counters. The erase-debug overlay paints these stretches green.

ovl._emitOutlineRing

Maps points through the object's own picture (`_objPointInActive`), drops sub-pixel chords, and keeps only runs that cover some ground.

everyNth(pts, max)Thins a point list to at most `max` points, for the lasso's hand-precision tests.§12
sel.everyNth

The list itself when it is short enough; otherwise every ceil(n / max)-th point, the last not necessarily included.

SelectionSelecting, hit-testing and dragging, as a mixin.§7
sel.Selection

Same mixin arrangement as ErasePipeline.

_selectTap(P)A select press that never moved: select, ctrl-toggle, or clear, decided at pen-up.§12
sel._selectTap

On paper a plain tap deselects and a ctrl tap keeps the selection. On ink a ctrl tap toggles the object; a plain tap on a member keeps the whole selection, and anywhere else selects the object under the point (`select`, which applies pending erases over it first).

  • Nothing changes on the way down: a press may turn out to be the first finger of a pinch (DESIGN.md §10).
_beginSelectDrag(P, sx, sy)A select press that has travelled SELECT_DRAG_PX: decides between a lasso and a move, and starts it.§12
sel._beginSelectDrag

A lasso when the press was on paper (and not on a selected frame's mark), with ctrl, or with nothing selected. Otherwise a move: an unselected object under the press is selected alone first, then every pending eraser mark over the selection is applied (`_settleSelectionErases`); if that took the selection away, it lassoes instead.

  • A move sets up `_dragSel`, turns on the tile cache's batch mode, takes the plate hold (`_beginHold`) and applies the first step.
  • The erase barrier covers every member, not only the one pressed: ink dragged from under an unapplied mark leaves the mark behind to cut whatever arrives there.
cancelSelectGesture(commitIfMoved)Forgets the select gesture in progress when a pinch starts; a drag that moved is put back, or finished if asked.§12
sel.cancelSelectGesture

Drops an unmoved press and any lasso. A moved drag is finished as a pen-up when `commitIfMoved` (the shell passes it once the press is old enough to have been deliberate); otherwise each member goes back to its start frame and start table and the dragged frames are restored (`_restoreFrames`). Ends through `_endMove('cancel')`.

  • Undo and redo call it first when a drag is live: the drag's start records describe the document the undo is about to change.
_underFrames(level, frames)Whether a frame is one of `frames`, under one, or a shadow of either: the selection's frame rule.§12
sel._underFrames

Uses `LevelMap.isUnder`, which counts shadows; the tile cache uses `isAncestor` instead.

_inkedFrames()Every frame with a native in its subtree: each frame that holds one, and its ancestors.§12
sel._inkedFrames

Stops climbing at an ancestor already seen. The lasso skips frames outside it and the selection drops them, because a visited cell with nothing under it stands for nothing: a selection holding such cells drew a dot each on blank paper (50 in one report, F93).

_outsideSelection(ids)Of a set of frame ids, those no selected frame holds any more, coarsest first and none under another.§12
sel._outsideSelection

The frames a subtree drag or an undo moved out of the selected subtrees (a sub-cell rest re-homed them next door), so they can join the selection as frames.

_reselect(ids, torn)Keeps the selection standing for the same ink after ink crossed cell edges: carried natives join as ids, torn frames as frames, empty frames leave.§12
sel._reselect

The frames are the selection's plus `torn`. A native no selected frame holds joins the ids; one listed and held by a selected frame again leaves them. Frames with no native under them (`_inkedFrames`) are dropped. Nothing is set when all that already holds; otherwise `_setSelection` (DESIGN.md §10, F93).

_objPointInActive(o, level, p)A point of a native, mapped into the active frame where its picture is drawn.§12
sel._objPointInActive

Through the native's displacement table when it has one (`mapPointObj`), else a plain frame-to-frame map. Null when the frames have no path between them.

_inkInsidePolygon(o, level, ink)Whether an object's ink, not only its box, lies wholly inside the lasso; asked of objects whose box straddles the loop.§12
sel._inkInsidePolygon

First the points the object already has (a stroke's samples, a fill's vertices, a shape's piece ends; a few hundred at most), mapped where the picture is and tested one by one; any outside answers no. Only then is the outline flattened at 3 screen px (LASSO_INK_TOL_PX), capped at 3,000 points a ring, and each ring tested against the prepared loop.

  • The cheap reject is where most crossed objects leave: flattening a scribble of twenty thousand arcs costs 14 ms even coarsely (measured). An outline that throws answers no.
_dragFramesStart(d, camDepth)Records, once per drag, the start address and shift of every frame the drag moves as a frame.§6
sel._dragFramesStart

For each selected root not under another: its subtree to three levels below the camera (`LevelMap.subtreeStart`; deeper frames follow their parent pointer), leaving out empty childless containers. Each gets an entry `{ from, to, shiftBefore, shiftAfter, settled, merged }`, which becomes part of the `moveFrames` undo op.

  • Sets `Document.holdMerges`: a shadow the drag makes is merged only once the op is pushed.
_dragFrames(d, camDepth, tx, ty)One drag step for the frames: re-addresses each from its start address, the sub-cell rest kept as a shift on the frame.§6
sel._dragFrames

Targets come from the start record (`LevelMap.moveSubtreeTargets`, `displaceFrame`'s arithmetic frame for frame). A frame's new shift is its starting shift plus this step's rest; a frame a render settled mid-drag is unsettled first. The targets are applied in one two-phase `readdressMany`; each changed address is noted (`noteRefile`), the shift set, and the frame's entry recorded as the owner of later settles. Returns whether anything moved.

  • No native is touched: a frame's shift is settled into its natives' tables at the first read of its list (DESIGN.md §8).
_frameUnderPoint(sx, sy)The selected frame whose mark is within 8 px of a screen point, or null.§12
sel._frameUnderPoint

The mark is the frame's origin on screen. A press there drags the selection, as a press on selected ink does.

_displaceMember(from, below, camDepth, tx, ty)Where one member goes for a drag displacement: its new home frame and table, or why it cannot move.§6
sel._displaceMember

Homed at or above the camera's depth: the displacement enters the table at the camera's depth (`addOffset`). Deeper: `LevelMap.displaceFrame` turns the whole-cell digits into a new home and the rest enters the home-level entry. A carry out of the home level moves the member to the neighbour cell. Stored coordinates are never touched (DESIGN.md §8).

  • Pure in the lattice's state, so `_dragSelection` asks once per (home frame, starting table) and every member sharing those takes the same answer; registration rests on that.
_subtreeCount(f)How many natives a selected frame stands for (its list, its subtree's and its shadows'), for the status count.§12
sel._subtreeCount

O(frames): sums `Document.count` over `LevelMap.walk`, reading no native.

mergeClose(rects, gap)Unions rects lying within `gap` of each other, so several specks on one pixel become one dot.§12
ovl.mergeClose

One greedy pass: each rect grows the first kept rect it is near, or is kept. Used on the dots of selected objects too small to trace (F73), with a 2 px gap.

clipRect(r)A clip or attach rect as `{ rect, eps }` for the ants' seam test, the tolerance from `rectTol`.§12
ovl.clipRect

A clip or attach rect as `{ rect, eps }` for the ants' seam test, the tolerance from `rectTol`.

asLTRB(r)A rect in either spelling, as left/top/right/bottom.
ovl.asLTRB

An `x0/y0/x1/y1` rect is converted; any other is returned as it is. `eraseDescent.asLTRB` is the same one-liner.

mergeSpans(list, gap)Merges overlapping or nearly touching spans into the fewest runs.§9
ovl.mergeSpans

Used on the screen-edge ants: a shape with several fingers of ink touching the top of the view produces several spans, and drawing each separately would put a gap between marks that are visually one run.

OverlaysThe selection indicator and the erase debug view, as a mixin.§9
ovl.Overlays

Everything the engine draws that is not ink. Same mixin arrangement as ErasePipeline.

_selTable(s)The selection's members grouped by frame, with each frame's union boxes, one per displacement table (F68).§12
ovl._selTable

Each selected id expands to its family, erased marks dropped, each object once. A member of a family spanning several frames is listed but adds no box: it is drawn through its pieces. A selected frame is one box, its own cell, and its natives are never read.

  • Returns `{ byLevel, ids, levelOf, cross, frames, count }`, cached against the selection object and the document's revision.
_selFrameRect(info, L, F)Where a frame's selected members are drawn, as one rect in the active frame's units.§12
ovl._selFrameRect

The union of the frame's boxes, each mapped through its members' displacement table (`mapRectObj`) or exactly; null when none reaches F. The frame-dot decision reads it (F68).

_selDecide(s, table)Decides the ants: which frames are one dot, and which pieces of the render list get runs, in retained coordinates.§12
ovl._selDecide

A frame whose selected content is under 2 px on screen is one dot and none of its members is visited. Every other selected piece in `_lastList` (its own id, or homed under a selected frame) is traced: its loops, shifted by `piece.res`, cut into runs at its seam rects, clipped to the retained window, runs under half a pixel dropped. A member too small to trace, under 8 px, is a dot where its picture is; dots on one pixel merge (F73).

  • Kept for the whole of a drag; otherwise reused while the list, selection, revision, frame and origin stand, the view is inside the retained window and the zoom is within 1.25x of the decision's. The SVG renderer gets path strings (`runPathData`), the canvas painter the pieces themselves (DESIGN.md §10).
_selPieceLoops(piece)A render-list piece as loops of arcs and lines: the geometry its ink is drawn from.§12
ovl._selPieceLoops

A shape's own loops; a fill's rings as line loops; a stroke's capsule outline, as the renderer draws it. Cached on the piece against the array it was made from, because a native in the list is the document's own object and an edit replaces its loops.

_selSeamRects(piece, table, F, cache)The rects a piece may have been cut on, its own clip and its family's attach windows, where the piece is drawn.§12
ovl._selSeamRects

A straight run lying along one is a seam and gets no ants: both 'no ants on a tile edge' and the F37 join rule. Family windows are mapped into F through each member's table (`mapRectObj`) or exactly and shifted by the piece's residual; cached per piece id, with the piece's own clip added on each call.

_selEdges(dec, off)Where the selected ink meets the sides of the screen, recomputed on every step as the view moves.§12
ovl._selEdges

Only pieces straddling the view are scanned (`edgeSpans`), the view shifted back by a drag's offset. Spans become screen coordinates, merge across 1.5 px gaps, drop under 2 px, and take a chevron from a fifth of their side. Returns `{ list, covered }`; a selection wholly in view gives none.

KobinEngine · undo, files, scenes

The boundary between the engine and everything that outlives a session.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
undo · redo · clearOne gesture is one action. Undo and redo cancel a live drag first, do nothing in a read-only tab, and re-schedule background work, because an undo can leave strokes unresolved.§10
eng.undo

Undo and redo cancel a live drag first (its start records describe the document about to change), run the document's undo or redo inside `_keepingSelection`, so the natives and frames it moves out of the selected frames stay selected, then re-schedule the background bake and render, because reversing an action can leave strokes unresolved or erases unapplied. Clear drops the bake jobs and resets the document, the lattice, the camera and the renderer. All three do nothing while `readOnly`.

eng.redo

The mirror of `undo`: cancels a live drag, runs `Document.redo` inside `_keepingSelection`, re-schedules the bake and renders. Returns false when nothing was redone.

snapshot · loadSnapshotThe development snapshot (dev-0): camera, natives and lattice, for tests and tools. A report carries a kobin-2 extract that report.loadReport turns back into one.§15
fil.snapshot

`loadSnapshot` is still how a report is reopened: `report.loadReport` rebuilds a dev-0 snapshot from the report's extract and loads it, which is how a browser bug becomes a failing test offline (DESIGN.md §13, §14).

  • Loading loads the lattice, mints every frame the natives name, loads the natives, clears the scene state, settles the camera and renders.
serializeDrawing · loadDrawingThe real save format. Loading settles the camera into a legal state, which is what stopped the first interaction after opening a file paying for a whole crossing.§13
fil.serializeDrawing

The kobin-1 envelope around the engine's own state. `meta.sceneIndex` is the scene client's last state (`exportForSave`). `frames` is null for the whole drawing, a list for only those frames' natives, or [] for the envelope alone, which the autosave writes as the canvas header.

  • Loading (`loadDrawing`) validates everything before touching state, loads the lattice, mints every frame the natives name, loads the natives, settles the camera into a legal state, clears the erase bookkeeping and drops any cut in flight. Measured: an unsettled camera made the first pan after a load cost 200 ms and every later one 0.2 ms.
fil.loadDrawing

In order: decode (it throws first), load the lattice, mint every frame the natives name, drop the bake queue, load the natives (the reset event clears the tiles, the selection and, on the raster path, the plate memo and the carried picture), set and settle the camera into a legal zoom, clear the erase bookkeeping and any cut in flight, reschedule the bake, take the file's name, scale bar and scenes, clear the renderer, render, and queue idle outline fits.

  • `{ render: false }` skips the render: the store restore (`useKobinEngine.restoreFrom`) and `foldStore` load the snapshots this way, replay the op log, and render once, a task later (on the Magnum Opus the load and a cold render were one 5-7 s task, STALL 2026-09-23).
refreshScenesThe scene list brought up to date through the scene client: inline, now; with the worker, the next batch is started and the list as it stands comes back.§14
sco.refreshScenes

Calls `SceneClient.flushNow` and returns `docMeta.scenes`.

jumpTo · sceneZoomGo to a scene at its natural zoom: the camera fitView gives for its rect in its frame, then the ordinary crossing.§14
sco.jumpTo

Sets the camera to `fitView(rect)` in the frame, lets `_maybeCross` bring an out-of-range scale to a legal level, clears the renderer and renders. A camera move, never a document change; a stroke in progress is ended first.

renameSceneA user's name for a scene: shown in the list at once, taken by the index with the next batch; a renamed scene keeps its id and name through merges.§14
sco.renameScene

Through `SceneClient.rename`; an engine without a client renames the row in `docMeta.scenes` directly. Trimmed, at most 120 characters.

FilesThe two save formats, as a mixin.§11
fil.Files

kobin-1 (persist.js), the file format and the envelope the local store writes beside its frames; and dev-0, which the tests load and a report's extract is turned back into. Same mixin arrangement as ErasePipeline.

_mintNamedFrames(natives)Mints every frame a loaded file's natives name, before the natives are added (F67).§13
fil._mintNamedFrames

`LevelMap.ensureId` per frame key, so no native is homed in a frame the lattice lacks. `loadSnapshot` and `loadDrawing` call it after the lattice loads.

fitView(rect, w, h)The camera that frames a rect, centred, in a w × h viewport: `jumpTo`'s fit and `snapshotView`'s, one implementation.§14
sco.fitView

Returns `{inScale, inPanX, inPanY}`, or null when the scale is not a positive finite number. CSS px for `jumpTo`, device px for `snapshotView`, so a thumbnail frames a scene exactly as jumping to it would.

SceneOpsThe engine's scene calls, as a mixin: the scene index's client, jumping to a scene, and a scene's picture.§14
sco.SceneOps

Same mixin arrangement as ErasePipeline.

_initScenes(on)Make the engine's scene client, or none for an engine that never lists scenes (`scenes: false`, the thumbnails' copy).§14
sco._initScenes

Make the engine's scene client, or none for an engine that never lists scenes (`scenes: false`, the thumbnails' copy).

snapshotView(req)A picture of a rect in a frame, framed by `fitView` at a camera that is never set: one raster job on one plate, for the Scenes panel.§14
sco.snapshotView

The world is shifted by the job's pack-time `offset` so the rect lands on plate (0, 0); the picture is the plate's top-left `w × h` device pixels, each capped at PLATE_PX (512). No crossing is made.

  • Null off the raster path, for an unknown frame or an unfittable rect. A frame never visited pays its tile bake inside the call, synchronously (F59).
sceneReport()The scene client's account for a report: where the index runs, how many objects wait, whether a restore or a batch is under way, and its counters.§15
sco.sceneReport

The scene client's account for a report: where the index runs, how many objects wait, whether a restore or a batch is under way, and its counters.

eraseJob.js 92 lines

The geometry of one erase cut as a job: the boolean, the removal measured locally, the graze rule and the dust cull, with no document in reach, so the same function runs on the main thread and in a raster worker (`runCut`). It also moves a job and its result between threads as transferable buffers.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
dustBarFor(bakePx, f)The dust bar: a quarter pixel at the zoom the mark was drawn at, in the subject's units.§10
ejb.dustBarFor

`DUST_PX / bakePx`, scaled by `f` (the mark's units into the subject's). Undefined when the mark recorded no zoom, and then the pen rule decides (DESIGN.md §7, F66).

cutJob(j)The geometry of one cut: the boolean, the removal measured locally, the graze rule, the components and the dust cull.§10
ejb.cutJob

Subtracts the clip from the subject and measures what went as the area of subject ∩ clip (F46). Graze rule `cut` refuses a removal at or under the smaller of 1e-4·rE² and 1e-6 of the subject's area; `cede` refuses under 1e-4·rE² alone, rE being half the eraser's box. Then the result's components, less dust (`dropDust` against the pen and `dustBar`).

  • Returns `{ kind: grazed | removed | cut, regions?, stats, removed, dust }`, regions as Loops. Imports geometry only and touches no document: the same function runs on the main thread, in the erase worker, and in a descent's last link (DESIGN.md §7).
own(l)A loop as a copied `{ buf, idx }` pair, ready to transfer to a worker; the caller's Loop stays usable.
ejb.own

A loop as a copied `{ buf, idx }` pair, ready to transfer to a worker; the caller's Loop stays usable.

wrap(x)A transferred `{ buf, idx }` pair as a Loop again.
ejb.wrap

A transferred `{ buf, idx }` pair as a Loop again.

wireJob(j)A cut job as a worker message plus the buffers to transfer: copies, so the document keeps its own.§10
ejb.wireJob

A cut job as a worker message plus the buffers to transfer: copies, so the document keeps its own.

unwireJob(m)A cut job back from a message, its loops wrapped as Loops.§10
ejb.unwireJob

A cut job back from a message, its loops wrapped as Loops.

wireResult(r)A cut result as a message; a cut's regions are transferred, not copied, since nothing else holds them.§10
ejb.wireResult

A cut result as a message; a cut's regions are transferred, not copied, since nothing else holds them.

unwireResult(m)A cut result back from a message, a cut's regions wrapped as Loops.§10
ejb.unwireResult

eraseDescent.js 327 lines

The rehome descent as one job per family: every cede down to the erase level runs on a virtual document, each square's ink derived exactly as the tile store derives it, and nothing reaches the document until the whole descent has succeeded. Runs on the main thread, or in a raster worker on a copy of the lattice.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
asLTRB(r)A rect in either spelling, as left/top/right/bottom.
eds.asLTRB

The same one-liner as `overlays.asLTRB`.

VirtualDocThe objects a descent reads and mints, kept apart from the document.§10
eds.VirtualDoc

The target is its one real object; everything a virtual cede mints takes a negative id. Implements the few `Document` calls the descent needs (`getById`, `add`, `removeById`, `editKey`) with the same record shape.

VirtualDoc.constructor(seed)Seeds the virtual document with `{ obj, level }` records, the level as a string; virtual ids start at -1.§10
eds.VirtualDoc.constructor

Seeds the virtual document with `{ obj, level }` records, the level as a string; virtual ids start at -1.

allocId()The next virtual id, -1, -2, ..., so a virtual object can never be taken for a real one.§10
eds.allocId

The next virtual id, -1, -2, ..., so a virtual object can never be taken for a real one.

getById(id)A virtual record `{ obj, level }` by id, or null.§10
eds.getById

A virtual record `{ obj, level }` by id, or null.

add(obj, level)Puts an object in the virtual document at a frame; returns the object.§10
eds.add

Puts an object in the virtual document at a frame; returns the object.

removeById(id)Takes an object out of the virtual document; returns its record, or null.§10
eds.removeById

Takes an object out of the virtual document; returns its record, or null.

editKey(o)An object's family key: its editId, else its id, as `Document.editKey` has it.§10
eds.editKey

An object's family key: its editId, else its id, as `Document.editKey` has it.

squareInkOf(world, vdoc, id, F, i, j)The tile store's piece for one object in square (i, j) of frame F, derived from the level above as the store derives it.§10
eds.squareInkOf

Runs `classifyUp`, then `solidQuad` or `deriveStep`, on the one object and on the same numbers `TileStore._bakeUp` uses, so the kid a cede mints is the store's piece bit for bit (F42). An object homed in a cell around the parent is first projected into the parent's coordinates, if its box meets the square's pre-image.

  • Returns `{ loops, clip, tile }` (shape loops, or a covering fill's clip as a rect loop), or null when the square holds none of the object's ink.
descentJob(world, input)The whole rehome descent for one target, on a virtual document: every cede down to the erase level, then the last link's cut.§10
eds.descentJob

Refuses unless the route from the target's frame to the mark's is a pure descent. At each crossing, for each object the step above minted: the frame F0 holding its picture (through its table), the eraser's box grown by half its size and widened to cover the cell the next crossing enters, and at most a 2x2 block of F0's squares, the square under the box's centre first and alone when its window covers the box. Each square's ink (`squareInkOf`) is ceded into a kid one level down; at the last link the kid is `cutJob`'s result under the `cede` graze rule.

  • Nothing touches the document. The result is `{ steps, stats, minted }`, each step `{ removedId, parents, kids }`, or `{ refused, stats, inkless }` when no square was ceded or the last link refused, so a refusal needs no unwinding. `inkless` says the link it stopped at found none of the target's ink near the eraser (none, dust or a graze) and read every square it needed: the engine's mark then holds nothing whole there (F109). `minted` lists the frames the job added or re-parented on the lattice it ran on (F67). The same function runs on the main thread and in the erase worker (DESIGN.md §7).
own(l)A loop as a copied `{ buf, idx }` pair, ready to transfer; the caller's Loop stays usable.
eds.own

The same helper as `eraseJob`'s `own`.

wrap(x)A transferred `{ buf, idx }` pair as a Loop again.
eds.wrap

A transferred `{ buf, idx }` pair as a Loop again.

objOut(o, transfer)An object copied for a worker message: runtime fields dropped, its loops copied into buffers pushed onto `transfer`.
eds.objOut

Drops `_bbox`, `_home`, `_ver` and `_zScan`.

objIn(o)An object back from a message, its loops wrapped as Loops.
eds.objIn

An object back from a message, its loops wrapped as Loops.

wireDescent(world, input)A descent job as a worker message: the target and the eraser copied, the lattice as `LevelMap.serialize()`.§10
eds.wireDescent

Carries the canvas size, config, opacity groups, freeze radius and the mark's frame beside them; the mark's zoom (`bakePx`) rides for the dust bar.

unwireDescent(m)In the worker: the world and input rebuilt, with a LevelMap loaded from the serialised lattice.§10
eds.unwireDescent

The descent runs on this copy, so any frame it mints comes back in `minted` for the engine to merge.

wireDescentResult(r)A descent result as a message: each step's objects copied out and their buffers transferred; a refusal as it is.§10
eds.wireDescentResult

A descent result as a message: each step's objects copied out and their buffers transferred; a refusal as it is.

unwireDescentResult(m)A descent result back from a message, every step object's loops wrapped as Loops.§10
eds.unwireDescentResult

eraseWorkerClient.js 76 lines

The cuts in the shared worker pool (B-PYRAMID-2b, 2026-09-29): a cut or a descent is a `JobQueue` job at `PRIO.cut` posted to a raster worker, with one worker kept for cuts while any is pending; a promise of its result, or null when the pool is broken, in which case the pipeline runs the same job inline, as jsdom always does.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
cutQueue()A `JobQueue` over the raster pool for cuts alone: the SVG path's (the raster renderer's queue carries plates and cuts together).§7
ewc.cutQueue

A `JobQueue` over the raster pool for cuts alone: the SVG path's (the raster renderer's queue carries plates and cuts together).

cutSlots(queue)How many more cuts the bake's lookahead may send: the pool's size less the cuts queued or out; 0 when the pool is broken.§7
ewc.cutSlots

How many more cuts the bake's lookahead may send: the pool's size less the cuts queued or out; 0 when the pool is broken.

submit(queue, {kind, barrier, job})One cut or descent as a `JobQueue` job of kind "cut" at `PRIO.cut`, posted to a raster worker (`runCut`): a promise of its result, or null when the pool is broken (the pipeline runs the job inline).§7
ewc.submit

While any cut is pending the queue keeps one worker for cuts. A barrier's jobs go first. A job a worker error lost goes back to the head of its priority once (`requeue`); the one the watchdog found silent, a second loss, or a job that threw rejects with `err.why`, and the pipeline refuses the pair over ink — never inline, where the same job would stall the page (PLAN §5.9 item 1).

resetEraseWorkerClient()Tests only: the counters back to zero.
ewc.resetEraseWorkerClient

Tests only: the counters back to zero.

eraseWorkerStats()For the report: cuts posted, run inline, landed, requeued and lost.§14
ewc.eraseWorkerStats

For the report: cuts posted, run inline, landed, requeued and lost.

report.js 704 lines

The dev report's assembly (DESIGN.md §14, OPEN-FLAGS F58): the instruments, the save, move, erase and scene state, the recent history, and a local extract of the drawing in kobin-2 frame form that `loadReport` turns back into an engine. Built task by task with a yield between; it only reads the engine.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
msg(err)An error's message cut to 200 characters, for the report's `errors` entries.

An error's message cut to 200 characters, for the report's `errors` entries.

r3(v)A finite number rounded to six significant figures; anything else returned unchanged.

A finite number rounded to six significant figures; anything else returned unchanged.

macroYield()A yield to the event loop through a MessageChannel, which a hidden tab does not throttle the way it throttles timers.§15
rep.macroYield

One shared channel: each call queues its resolver and posts a message, and the messages resolve them in order. Without `MessageChannel` it falls back to `setTimeout(0)`; Node's port is `unref`ed so a test process can exit.

  • Chained timers in a hidden tab run once a second, and once a minute after five minutes hidden: measured 2026-09-22, a 20-task report over `setTimeout(0)` took 11 minutes to send.
brief(v, depth, key)A bounded JSON copy of any value: the form every free-form part of the report takes.§15

Keeps primitives and cuts strings at 160 characters; summarises typed arrays (`{ f64: n }`), natives (`nativeBrief`) and Maps and Sets (their size); cuts arrays to their first 20 with the count; stops three levels down. Functions and `_`-prefixed keys other than `_seq` are dropped, and an object past 24 keys ends with its key count.

  • An array under a key starting `below` is written as a displacement table's file form (`encodeBelow`).
nativeBrief(o)A native as its id, type and size, never its geometry: what `brief` writes for anything with loops, points or rings.§15

A shape's piece count or a stroke's point count, then `z` when it differs from the id, `editId`, the erase flag and the displacement table in its file form.

boxOf(b)A bounding box as `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` at six significant figures, or null.

numbersOf(o)How many doubles a native's kobin-2 span holds: the unit the extract's estimate and the whole drawing's parts are sized in.§15

One for the header count, then per loop one plus its stored numbers (a shape), per ring one plus two per point (a fill), or two per point (a stroke).

  • Mirrors `format2.pushGeometry`'s count; a change to the span grammar changes both.
