buildReport(E, opts)Builds the dev report section by section, each its own task with a yield between, so no build holds the main thread whole.§15
rep.buildReport

In order: meta, camera, counts, raster, instruments, memory, moves, erase, scenes, save, cloud, errors and history; then the local extract (`buildExtract`, unless `opts.extract` is false) and the families it touches (`familiesOf`). `build` records the total ms, each task's ms and the longest; the headline (`headlineOf`) is computed last from the finished sections.

  • Every section is caught: one that throws is named in `build.errors` and the rest of the report stands. The save, cloud, page-error and console sections are the caller's state, taken as given and `brief`ed.
  • It must only read: nothing here mints a frame, settles a shift or emits a document event (DESIGN.md §14).
metaOf(E, opts)The report's who-and-where: time, reason, renderer, route, URL flag names, device, and the engine's modes and gesture in progress.§15
rep.metaOf

The route is the hash with its query cut off; the query goes in as parameter names only (at most 12). Device: user agent, platform, cores, memory, touch points, online, device pixel ratio, window and engine sizes, visibility. Engine: tool, trace, pre-bake, retained scenes, opacity groups, and whether a stroke, erase, lasso or drag is under way.

cameraOf(E, sub)Where the camera is: its state, depth, effective zoom and view, the chain of frames to the root, and its ring and children.§15
rep.cameraOf

The chain walks parents from the camera's frame (at most 200), each with its cell, native count, child count, shift and shadow; the ring and the first 30 children carry native counts. `latticeFrames` is the lattice's size.

countsOf(E)The document in numbers: natives, pieces, shapes, strokes, fills, erase marks, frames, moved objects, undo and redo depth.§15
rep.countsOf

One pass over every frame's list; `byFrame` is the 40 most populated frames and `listed` the last render list's length.

rasterOf(E, sub)The renderer's section: the raster perf ring, plate store, picture layer, move plane, overlay, ladder and drain queues; for SVG only its group count.§15
rep.rasterOf

`perf` is `rasterPerf.report`, a module singleton attached to the last renderer built; `plates` is this engine's own store. The layer's uncovered cells are what the headline's paper figure reads.

instrumentsOf(E, sub)The engine's instruments: the last 300 perfLog entries, the fast-path stats, frame meter, long frames, event latency and growth.§15
rep.instrumentsOf

DESIGN.md §14 says what each measures.

memoryOf(E, sub)Memory: the JS heap where the browser exposes it, the plate store's bytes, a census of the tile cache and the undo stack's length.§15
rep.memoryOf

`performance.memory` is Chrome's; elsewhere `heap` is null. Without a plate store the plate figures are `rasterPerf.growth()`.

tileCensus(store)The tile cache counted: tiles, pieces, tiles by direction (up or down), and the 12 frames whose tiles hold the most pieces.§15
rep.tileCensus

The tile cache counted: tiles, pieces, tiles by direction (up or down), and the 12 frames whose tiles hold the most pieces.

movesOf(E, sub)The move state: the selection and its first 50 members, a drag or hold in progress, the shifted and shadow frames, and the last ten move ops.§15
rep.movesOf

Members carry level, type, z, editId, displacement table (file form) and box; shifted and shadow frames are capped at 50 each; the recent ops are the undo stack's `move`, `moveMany` and `moveFrames`, `brief`ed.

eraseOf(E, sub)The erase state: pending marks and their bake progress, the bake queue, the cut in flight, the seal, repair and failure counters, and the worker's stats.§15
rep.eraseOf

Each of the first 50 marks carries its level, z, bake px, box, how many ids its bake has done and whether it is committed; `heldMs` is how long the bake has been held back.

scenesOf(E, sub)The scenes: their count, the first 60 `brief`ed, and the scene index's own report where the engine has `sceneReport`.§15
rep.scenesOf

The scenes: their count, the first 60 `brief`ed, and the scene index's own report where the engine has `sceneReport`.

historyOf(E)The recent history: the gesture journal whole, the last 30 undo ops and the last 10 redo ops.§15
rep.historyOf

The journal is the last 40 gestures with their pointer paths (DESIGN.md §14), which is what a replay of a report drives.

familiesOf(E, ex, run)The multi-native families the extract touches, and for each which of its members still form one connected piece.§15
rep.familiesOf

One task finds them: every non-erase native in the extract names its edit key, one pass over all natives collects each key's members, and the first 12 with more than one member are kept. Each then gets a task of its own computing `_familyComponents`, as `reportFamilies` does for the whole drawing.

  • A family with a moved member (a displacement table) gets no components: `_familyComponents` maps its parent through `objShift`, which can mint a frame, and the report only reads.
  • Counting only the extract's keys avoids `editGroup`'s index over every native (measured: 218 ms cold on 42,856 natives, for no family at all).
headlineOf(rep)The numbers `tools/report-read.js` leads with, gathered at the top of the report.§15
rep.headlineOf

When and why, renderer, camera frame, depth and zoom, native, piece, frame and lattice counts, the paper figures from the raster perf picture, the worst long frame, heap, pending marks, selection size, whether the save is failing, and the extract's size and whether it was cut.

buildExtract(E, opts, run)The local extract: the natives on and around the screen in kobin-2 frame form, cut to a byte budget, with the lattice, so `loadReport` can rebuild the view.§15
rep.buildExtract

Scores the candidates (`scorer`) in slices of 1,500 natives, chooses by tier and size within `maxBytes` (4 MB of JSON by default; `chooseNatives`), encodes each frame's chosen natives in slices of about 512 KB of estimate (joined, spans offset), then attaches the lattice (`latticeFor`). The camera and screen size go with it; `stats` counts the candidates, the chosen, the on-screen, selected and listed ones kept and dropped, and the too big.

  • The slices are what keep it off the main thread: 16,079 cold natives scored in one task took 401 ms, and one frame's 3 MB encoded in one took 170 ms.
scorer(E, zoomOut, minPx)Sets up the extract's scoring: per-frame work lists a slice at a time can `consider`, and a `finish` that adds the selection wherever it is.§15
rep.scorer

A native's score is its size in screen px at the zoom-out that first brings it on screen (1 when it is on screen). Its tier is 0 on screen (in the last render list and meeting the view), 1 selected, 2 in the render list (the tile window), 3 around; a tier-3 native past `zoomOut` (4,096) or under `minPx` (0.25 px) is left out.

  • A frame that cannot be mapped to the camera's is counted `unreachable`; one whose largest native is under `minPx` and holds nothing on screen or selected is skipped (`tinyFrames`). Otherwise its candidates are a rect query around the view plus its moved natives, or its whole list when the frame has a pending shift.
  • A moved native is judged where its picture is: `shiftAt(below, 0)` in its home's units, plus the frame's pending shift.
chooseNatives(list, maxBytes)Picks the extract's natives: sorted by tier then score, each taken while the estimated bytes still fit.§15
rep.chooseNatives

Past the cap the scan goes on, since a smaller native further down may still fit. Every one left out is counted (on-screen ones separately), and one over a quarter of the budget is named in `tooBig` (up to 20). Returns the chosen ids by frame and the set of their frames.

latticeFor(E, homes)The extract's lattice: whole up to 20,000 frames; beyond that the chains to the root of the camera's frame, its ring and every extract frame.§15
rep.latticeFor

Only a whole lattice lets `loadReport` map every frame as the engine did; a trimmed one says so (`trimmed: { kept, of }`).

drawingPlan(E, maxBytes)Cuts the whole drawing into parts of about `maxBytes` of doubles (1 MB by default), per frame, each native once: the plan for the whole-drawing opt-in.§15
rep.drawingPlan

The plan holds the natives by reference, so a part encodes them as they are when it is sent. A native larger than the cap is a part of its own.

  • The size bounds a main-thread task: encoding is about 45 ms a MB, and 3 MB parts reached 372 ms.
drawingChunk(step, part)One planned part as a kobin-2 frame chunk (`format2.packChunk`) with the header `{ frame, part, objects }`.§15
rep.drawingChunk

One planned part as a kobin-2 frame chunk (`format2.packChunk`) with the header `{ frame, part, objects }`.

extractToSnapshot(ex, drawing)A report's drawing as a dev-0 snapshot for `loadSnapshot`: the extract's frames, or the whole drawing's parts when they are given.§15
rep.extractToSnapshot

`drawing` is the parts' chunk bytes, already gunzipped; each is unpacked and decoded into its frame. The camera and the lattice (`crossings`) are the extract's either way.

loadReport(E, rep, opts)Loads a report's extract, or its whole drawing, into an engine at the recorded camera and screen size.§15
rep.loadReport

Resizes `E` to the recorded screen unless `resize` is false, then `loadSnapshot`; returns the native and frame counts and whether it was the whole drawing. A report with no extract (a v1 report, which carried the whole document as `snapshot`) throws.

  • Called by `reportSend.replayReport` in a page and by `__testkit__/reportReplay.js` in jsdom.

09 Features

Two things built on the engine, obeying its constraints: the scene index and the scale bar

sceneIndex.js 1,795 lines

The scene index (DESIGN.md §11): a pure core, saved in the file and updated one batch of changed objects at a time, never re-clustered. It keeps every scene's members, grids, anchor and origin, applies the rules in the scenes-v3 bible's order, and returns the panel's list and the saved state; it runs in the scene worker and inline.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
frameLog(f, depth)A frame's absolute log size: log2 of its longer side, less 12 per depth, so sizes compare across frames.§14
six.frameLog

A frame's absolute log size: log2 of its longer side, less 12 per depth, so sizes compare across frames.

cellIx(v)A coordinate's grid cell index, floored and clamped to ±2^25 so a cell key fits one number.§14
six.cellIx

A cell key is `(i + OFF)·KEYM + (j + OFF)` with OFF = 2^25 and KEYM = 2^26, under 2^52; a chunk further out lands in the edge cell instead of overflowing the key.

fitsSpread(lo, hi)Does a range of absolute log widths fit one scene: within ZOOM_SPREAD (4 octaves), with a 1e-9 tolerance.§14
six.fitsSpread

Does a range of absolute log widths fit one scene: within ZOOM_SPREAD (4 octaves), with a 1e-9 tolerance.

now()A millisecond clock for a batch's timing: `performance.now()` where there is one, else `Date.now()`.
six.now

A millisecond clock for a batch's timing: `performance.now()` where there is one, else `Date.now()`.

FrameTableThe scene index's own copy of the frame tree: frame records, and the similarity that maps any frame's coordinates into any other's.§14
six.FrameTable

Records are `{id, parent, depth, cx, cy, sx, sy}`: the cell centre in the parent and the frame's pending shift. `update` keeps the pre-batch record of every frame it changes, so a batch can measure a move in the tree as it was (`map(..., old)`) until `settle`.

  • Mappings are cached; a batch with frame records clears the cache.
FrameTable.constructor()An empty table: no current records, no pre-batch records, two empty mapping caches.§14
six.FrameTable.constructor

An empty table: no current records, no pre-batch records, two empty mapping caches.

get(id)A frame's current record.§14
six.get

A frame's current record.

depth(id)A frame's depth, or null for a frame the table does not hold.§14
six.depth

A frame's depth, or null for a frame the table does not hold.

update(recs)Take a batch's frame records; returns the frames whose parent, depth or cell changed (moved subtrees), those whose shift alone changed, and those that went.§14
six.update

A `gone` record deletes the frame and lists it in `gone`. A record equal to the current one is ignored; a shift-only change goes in `shifted`; anything else replaces the record and, for a frame that existed, goes in `moved`.

  • Every replaced record is kept in `prev` for `map(..., old)` until `settle`, and the mapping caches are cleared.
settle()Forget the pre-batch frame records once the batch has measured its moves.§14
six.settle

Forget the pre-batch frame records once the batch has measured its moves.

_rec(id, old)A frame's record: the pre-batch one when `old` is asked and the frame changed this batch, else the current.§14
six._rec

A frame's record: the pre-batch one when `old` is asked and the frame changed this batch, else the current.

parentOf(id, old)A frame's parent id, now or (`old`) before this batch.§14
six.parentOf

A frame's parent id, now or (`old`) before this batch.

under(id, roots)Is the frame one of `roots`, or beneath one in the current tree?§14
six.under

Walks parents, at most 4,096 steps. How a batch finds the items and scenes a moved subtree carries.

_up(id, depth, old)Walk a frame up to its ancestor at `depth`, accumulating the scale and offset that map its coordinates into the ancestor's.§14
six._up

Returns `{f, s, ox, oy}` with `p_ancestor = p·s + (ox, oy)`: each step divides by R and adds the cell centre. Null when the chain ends first.

six.depth

A frame's depth, or null for a frame the table does not hold.

_across(a, b, old)The offset between two frames at one depth, summed from their common ancestor down (Horner), so frames near each other keep every partial sum small however deep that ancestor.§14
six._across

Walks both chains up in step until they meet (null with no common root or past 4,096 steps), then accumulates `(off + a.cx − b.cx)·R` from the top down: `p_b = p_a + off`.

map(from, to, old)The similarity `p_to = p_from·s + o` between any two frames (null when they share no root), cached; `old` maps through the tree before this batch.§14
six.map

Both frames go up to the shallower depth (`_up`), then across at that depth (`_across`); the target's scale is divided out. The pre-batch mapping has its own cache, cleared by `settle`.

encodeIds(ids)Sorted ids as a saved member string: base-36 gaps, a run of consecutive ids written `gap.extra`.§14
six.encodeIds

The `m` (objects) and `e` (erase footprints) strings of `meta.sceneIndex`: `5.2` is 5, 6, 7.

decodeIds(str, max)Read a saved member string back into ids; a malformed token, or one that would take the total past `max` (MAX_IDS, 10^7), ends the decode, keeping what was read.§14
six.decodeIds

The bound is on the whole string, not on one run, so a damaged string loses only the tail of one scene's members.

rectCover(t, r)The share of rect `t`'s area that rect `r` covers (0 for an empty `t`).§14
six.rectCover

The one overlap measure behind MATCH_OVERLAP: names kept aside, legacy scenes and parts.

grow(bb, loc, n)Widen a bounding box `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` by the first n chunk boxes of a filed position array.
six.grow

Widen a bounding box `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` by the first n chunk boxes of a filed position array.

EMPTY_BB()A fresh empty bounding box, `[∞, ∞, −∞, −∞]`.
six.EMPTY_BB

A fresh empty bounding box, `[∞, ∞, −∞, −∞]`.

newTag()A random tag (up to six base-36 digits) for this session's picture keys, so a version number reached again after an unsaved session never repeats a key.§14
six.newTag

A random tag (up to six base-36 digits) for this session's picture keys, so a version number reached again after an unsaved session never repeats a key.

keyOf(S)A scene's picture key: its session tag and content version, `tag-version` in base 36 (the version alone for a scene saved without a tag).§14
six.keyOf

A scene's picture key: its session tag and content version, `tag-version` in base 36 (the version alone for a scene saved without a tag).

rowKey(R)A panel row's picture key: its scene's `keyOf`, or for a row of several scenes, `e` + the FNV-1a hash of their keys and the id of the scene whose frame it shows.§14
six.rowKey

A panel row's picture key: its scene's `keyOf`, or for a row of several scenes, `e` + the FNV-1a hash of their keys and the id of the scene whose frame it shows.

fnv(str)FNV-1a hash of a string, in base 36: the picture key of a region and of a row of several scenes.§14
six.fnv

FNV-1a hash of a string, in base 36: the picture key of a region and of a row of several scenes.

newGrid()A fresh scene grid: empty `all` and `own` band maps.§14
six.newGrid

A fresh scene grid: empty `all` and `own` band maps.

loopStarts(loops, n)A record's closed loops as an item keeps them: the first chunks that lie within its `n` chunks, a shared frozen `[0]` for one loop from the start, or null.§14
six.loopStarts

A record's closed loops as an item keeps them: the first chunks that lie within its `n` chunks, a shared frozen `[0]` for one loop from the start, or null.

chunkRuns(n, loops, f)The maximal runs of chunks for which `f(k)` holds: along the sequence, or around each closed loop, so a run crossing a loop's start is one run.§14
six.chunkRuns

`loops` is the first chunk of each closed loop. The stray rule and the insert rule's groups read their runs through it, so an outline's first and last chunks are neighbours.

fileIn(bands, b, i0, i1, j0, j1, e, add)Add a chunk entry to, or remove it from, every cell a box covers in band b of a grid map.§14
six.fileIn

A cell is a Set of entries `slot·MAX_CHUNKS + k`; an emptied cell, and an emptied band, are deleted.

SceneIndexThe scene index: every indexed object as an item, every scene with its members, grids, anchor and origin; one `apply(batch)` touches only the scenes the batch reaches.§14
six.SceneIndex

Pure: frames and items arrive as records and nothing reads a document, so the one class runs in the scene worker and inline (DESIGN.md §11; the rules and their order: docs/reference/scenes-v3-design-bible.md).

  • A scene's geometry is in its anchor frame (its coarsest home) less an origin, so a whole scene moved is one origin change. Widths compare across frames as `L = log2(w) − 12·depth`; every distance is in stroke widths (`REACH` 900, `CHUNK` 600).
  • The list it returns folds echoes (nested scenes framing the same subject) into one row each (`_echoes`); the scenes themselves are unchanged.
  • `__oracles__/sceneOracle.js` implements the same rules by brute force; `sceneIndex.test.js` compares the two after every batch.
SceneIndex.constructor()An empty index, its scene, content-version, part and region counters at 1, and a new session tag for its picture keys.§14
six.SceneIndex.constructor

`seedsMax` (32) is the seed count above which a split check labels the whole scene; the tests lower it to exercise that path.

_reset()Clear every structure: frames, items, scenes, width buckets, grid slots, kept-aside names, regions, rows and the query counters.§14
six._reset

The id counters are left alone; `_restore` sets them from the file.

_depth(id)A frame's depth, 0 for a frame the table does not hold.§14
six._depth

A frame's depth, 0 for a frame the table does not hold.

_setGeom(x, r)Give an item its chunks and width: the chunk count (at most MAX_CHUNKS), the first chunk of each closed loop, the absolute log width L and the mass.§14
six._setGeom

The closed loops come from the record's `loops` through `loopStarts`, only those within the kept chunks; without them the chunk sequence is open.

  • Mass is the chunks' total length in widths, at least 1: scale-free ink, which decides the side of a split or merge that keeps the identity.
_mkItem(r)Make an item from a record: a grid slot (a freed one reused), its table residual and its geometry.§14
six._mkItem

Make an item from a record: a grid slot (a freed one reused), its table residual and its geometry.

_dropItem(x)Forget an item and free its grid slot for reuse.§14
six._dropItem

Forget an item and free its grid slot for reuse.

_boxesIn(x, anchor, out, ox, oy)An item's chunk boxes where it is drawn now, in a scene's anchor coordinates less the origin, into `out`; returns the mapping used, or null.§14
six._boxesIn

Drawn position = stored chunk + the table's residual (`tx, ty`) + the home frame's pending shift, mapped home → anchor. A move changes the last two, never the chunks.

_homeBox(x)An item's drawn bounding box in its own home frame: stored chunks plus residual plus the home's shift.§14
six._homeBox

An item's drawn bounding box in its own home frame: stored chunks plus residual plus the home's shift.

_cells(S, x, add)File an item's chunks into (or out of) a scene's grid, and its multi-chunk grid too when the item has three chunks or more.§14
six._cells

The multi-chunk grid (`mgrid`) is what stray-run invalidation queries, so single-chunk dots never pay for it.

_cellsIn(G, x, add)File each chunk of an item into the cells of its own band in `all` and `own`, and of the five coarser bands in `all`.§14
six._cellsIn

Band b = floor(log2 T), cell side `2^(b+1)`: `all[b]` holds the chunks of bands b−5..b (what a query from band b must see), `own[b]` band b's alone (what a finer query must see). Kept apart, a query never walks a coarse cell only to skip what was filed up into it.

_near(S, x0, y0, x1, y1, T, b, fn, G, full)Visit every chunk of a scene within reach of a box: `all[b]`, then `own` of the five coarser bands; `fn(item, k)` returning true stops the search.§14
six._near

Reach is the larger of the query's `T` and the chunk's own, so two inks join at `max(T_a, T_b)`. `full` (from `_components`) skips cells whose entries were all visited. Counted in `stats.queries`.

_scan(g, bb, x0, y0, x1, y1, T, fn, seen)One band's cells around a box, padded by one cell side, testing each entry's chunk against the reach; a cell `seen` already covers is skipped.§14
six._scan

The cell side `2^(bb+1)` exceeds every reach filed in that band, so one cell of padding finds every chunk in reach. Counts cells and entries in `stats`.

_valid(S, m, k)Is chunk k of member m outside a stray run? Always, for a member of under three chunks or in a one-member scene; computed per member when first read.§14
six._valid

Stray chunks are not framed and never bridge (DESIGN.md §11).

_computeValid(S, m)Mark a member's lonely chunks (no other member's ink within reach) and flag every run of STRAY_CHUNKS (2) or more as stray, runs read around closed loops.§14
six._computeValid

Runs come from `chunkRuns`, so a lonely stretch across a loop's start is one run. Writes `m.valid` (1 = valid) and sets `validOk`; `_file`, `_unfile`, merges and splits clear `validOk` when a neighbour changes.

_invalidateNear(S, x)Make the multi-chunk members within reach of an item recompute their stray runs when next read.§14
six._invalidateNear

Queries the multi-chunk grid only: over every chunk it was measured at 30.6 M of the Magnum Opus build's 30.8 M grid entries (dense stippling, hundreds of dots within reach of each).

_mkScene(anchor, idn)Make an empty scene in an anchor frame, with a new identity unless one is given, a new content version under this session's tag, and register it by id.§14
six._mkScene

Make an empty scene in an anchor frame, with a new identity unless one is given, a new content version under this session's tag, and register it by id.

_newIdn()A new scene identity: the next `s<n>` id, the default name `Scene <n>`, unnamed, stamped with this batch.§14
six._newIdn

The batch stamp (`born`) is what lets `_reclaim` give a scene born this batch a name kept aside.

_setIdn(S, idn)Give a scene another identity (a merge's winner, a split's, a reclaimed name), re-keying the by-id map.§14
six._setIdn

Give a scene another identity (a merge's winner, a split's, a reclaimed name), re-keying the by-id map.

_drop(S)Remove a scene from the index and its width buckets, without keeping its name aside.§14
six._drop

Remove a scene from the index and its width buckets, without keeping its name aside.

_rebucket(S, gone)Keep a scene in the width buckets its range covers (one per 4 octaves of L), or take it out of all of them.§14
six._rebucket

The buckets are how `_candidates` finds the scenes whose range can meet an item's without scanning every scene.

_range(S)Recompute a scene's width range from its members when one at an end left, and re-bucket it.§14
six._range

Recompute a scene's width range from its members when one at an end left, and re-bucket it.

_touched(S)Mark a scene changed: a new content version under this session's tag (its picture key), its frame due, its saved member string stale.§14
six._touched

Mark a scene changed: a new content version under this session's tag (its picture key), its frame due, its saved member string stale.

_file(S, x, quiet)File an item into a scene at its current position, re-anchoring the scene first when the item is homed coarser; false when no mapping joins them.§14
six._file

Sets the item's filed boxes, reach `T = REACH·w·s` and band, and adds it to the grids, mass, range and box. Unless `quiet` (a restore, a merge or a split, which settle stray runs wholesale), its neighbours' stray runs are invalidated.

_unfile(S, x)Take an item out of a scene: its neighbours' stray runs invalidated, its grid entries, mass and multi-chunk count removed.§14
six._unfile

The range is marked for recomputation when the item sat at an end, and `lost` is set so `_finish` re-anchors the scene at its coarsest remaining home.

_reanchor(S, anchor, fresh)Move a scene's geometry into another anchor frame: every member re-filed there, the origin carried across, or (`fresh`) reset at the first member's box.§14
six._reanchor

`fresh` is for a scene whose anchor moved this batch: the filed positions are no longer comparable, so members are filed where they now are and their stray runs recomputed.

  • The scene's last frame is mapped into the new anchor too (through the pre-batch tree when `fresh`), since a name kept aside is recorded in it.
_reanchorOld(S, target)A scene whose anchor frame went this batch (a shadow merged into its resident) re-filed in `target` through the pre-batch tree, every member at its filed position.§14
six._reanchorOld

Filed boxes, reach and origin are scaled and mapped, so the placement that follows sees who moved. Where no pre-batch map joins the two frames, `_reanchor(fresh)` files the members where they now are.

_staticRef(id, moved)Where a displacement is measured: the frame, walked up the pre-batch tree while it went or moved this batch; null past the root.§14
six._staticRef

Where a displacement is measured: the frame, walked up the pre-batch tree while it went or moved this batch; null past the root.

_framesGone(gone, moved)Frames that went this batch: the scenes anchored in one are re-anchored in the nearest frame above that stayed, and names kept aside there are remapped into it.§14
six._framesGone

Runs right after the frame records, before any item record is read; the frame above is `_staticRef`'s.

_newScene(x)A new scene of one item, anchored at its home with the origin at the item's box corner.§14
six._newScene

Dropped again (null) when the item cannot be filed.

_candidates(x)The scenes an item may join: a width range within the spread with it, and a bounding box within the larger reach of its box.§14
six._candidates

Found through the width buckets, each scene tested once per call. The box test is a prefilter; the chunk test is `_insert`'s.

_insert(x)The insert rule: an item joins the scenes its chunks touch, merged while their widths fit, or starts a scene of its own.§14
six._insert

Each chunk is tested against the valid chunks of every candidate at reach `max(T_a, T_b)`. The chunks are split into groups at runs of STRAY_CHUNKS untouched chunks, read around closed loops (`chunkRuns`); the group touching most (tie: the one holding the lowest chunk) decides. Its scenes, most-touched first then oldest, merge while the merged range fits ZOOM_SPREAD, and the item joins (DESIGN.md §11).

  • So a long line from one drawing to another through empty paper does not merge them.
_idWinner(A, B)Which identity survives a merge: the renamed scene if exactly one was renamed, else the one with more ink, else the older.§14
six._idWinner

Which identity survives a merge: the renamed scene if exactly one was renamed, else the one with more ink, else the older.

_merge(A, B)Merge two scenes: the one with the deeper anchor (tie: fewer members, then the younger) re-files its members into the other; the identity winner's id and name go to the result, the loser's are kept aside.§14
six._merge

Members are filed quietly, and every multi-chunk member's stray runs are recomputed when next read.

_tomb(S)Keep a scene's id and name aside with its frame and width range, so a scene later covering that frame can take them back.§14
six._tomb

`_tombRecord` makes the record, `_pushTomb` keeps it.

_tombRecord(S)A scene's kept-aside record: id, name, anchor, frame and width range; null for a scene with no frame.§14
six._tombRecord

A live scene is framed as it stands; an emptied one uses its frame and range from the end of the last batch.

_pushTomb(rec)Keep a record aside, stamped with the kept-aside clock; at most TOMB_MAX (256), the oldest dropped.§14
six._pushTomb

Keep a record aside, stamped with the kept-aside clock; at most TOMB_MAX (256), the oldest dropped.

_kill(S)Keep a scene's name aside and remove the scene.§14
six._kill

Keep a scene's name aside and remove the scene.

_splitCheck(S, seeds, full)After members left a scene, split it into its components: the heaviest keeps the id and name (tie: the one holding the smallest id), the others become new scenes numbered in order of their smallest id.§14
six._splitCheck

Components come from `_seedComponents`, a search from the neighbours of what left, or, with `full` or more than `seedsMax` seeds, from labelling every member (`_components`).

  • The scene object keeps the component the search left open (the part never walked), else the heaviest; the others are re-filed into new scenes and identities follow.
_seedComponents(S, start)The components reachable from seed members, by an interleaved search per seed that stops once at most one search is still open.§14
six._seedComponents

A scene is connected by invariant, so every component holds a seed; searches that meet are merged. The open search's component is the rest of the scene, returned unwalked with `.rest` marking it. Null when fewer than two components are found.

_components(S)Label every member of a scene: its components, by flood fill over the grid.§14
six._components

A cell whose entries are all visited is skipped: a scan from one component never reaches another's ink. A dense scene (the Magnum Opus has ~4,900 dots within two join distances) costs its filings once rather than its size at every member.

_bbExact(S)Recompute a scene's bounding box from its members' filed chunks.§14
six._bbExact

Recompute a scene's bounding box from its members' filed chunks.

_frameOf(S)A scene's frame in its anchor's coordinates: its valid ink (stray runs left out), padded FRAME_PAD, at least MIN_FRAME_PX at the zoom where its thickest stroke is REF_STROKE_PX.§14
six._frameOf

Also refreshes the scene's bounding box. A one-member scene is framed on all its ink; null for a scene with no chunks.

_itemsTouch(items, B)Does a valid chunk of these items, filed in their own scene, come within reach of a valid chunk of scene B?§14
six._itemsTouch

Stray runs bridge nothing here, as at an insert. Maps each chunk from its scene's anchor into B's. `_rejoin`'s chunk test.

_rejoin(S, own)A scene moved whole lands: it merges with the compatible scenes its moved ink (`own`, all its members by default) now touches, oldest first, while the range fits.§14
six._rejoin

Candidates are prefiltered by range and bounding box; the chunk test (`_itemsTouch`, valid chunks on both sides) uses `own` only, so ink that stood still, or a scene merged in on the way, pulls in nothing more.

apply(batch)One batch of changes: frames (those that went first), placed items (moved whole or re-inserted), removals with pieces filed back and split checks, inserts in id order, re-joins, heirs, renames; returns the scene list and the saved state.§14
six.apply

Item records are gone, new (a `hint` names the object an erase piece replaced), re-shaped, re-placed, or `attr` (a z change: the scene's content version, its picture key, moves on and nothing else). A re-shape that is a pure translation counts as placed, and so does every item whose home frame moved or shifted. A record's `loops` travel with its chunks: a translation takes the new ones, a re-shape without new chunks keeps the old.

  • Per scene in id order: leaving members go; pieces and re-shaped objects are filed into the scene of what they replaced while the width range allows (storage, not new ink), else inserted; the rest is split-checked. An emptied scene keeps its name aside, or, when members that moved away emptied it, passes it to `_heirs`.
  • Each scene then holding ink that moved whole re-joins through that ink alone. `_finish` frames, reclaims names, and sets parents, parts and regions (DESIGN.md §11). A `restore` batch goes to `_restore` instead. Returns `{scenes, changed, export, ms, stats}`.
_heirs(heirs)A scene emptied by members that moved away passes its id and name to the scene holding most of their ink, when that scene was born this batch (tie: the one holding the smallest of their ids); otherwise the name is kept aside.§14
six._heirs

Run after the inserts and re-joins, in the emptied scenes' id order; the id is not given when a live scene already holds it.

_translated(a, b, wa, wb)Are chunk records `b` those of `a` shifted by one displacement: same count, lengths and width, within 1e-6 of a reach?§14
six._translated

Are chunk records `b` those of `a` shifted by one displacement: same count, lengths and width, within 1e-6 of a reach?

_placeScenes(placed, movedFrames, removeFrom, inserts, rejoin, fullSplit, leave)Items placed anew, per scene: every member that stays moved by one displacement is a rigid move (the origin follows, the moved ink re-joins where it lands); otherwise the moved members leave and are inserted again.§14
six._placeScenes

Displacements are measured in `_staticRef`'s frame, the nearest at or above the anchor that neither went nor moved: the old position through the pre-batch tree, the new through the current one.

  • A rigid move touches no grid cell and keeps the content version (the picture key); its moved members go on the re-join list, and whichever scene holds them after the inserts re-joins through them. A scene whose anchor moved but which did not move whole is re-anchored in that static frame and split-checked whole.
_finish(t0, legacy)The end of a batch: scenes that lost members re-anchored at their coarsest remaining home, changed scenes re-framed, then names reclaimed, parents, rows (`_echoes`), parts and regions.§14
six._finish

Returns `{scenes, changed, export, ms, stats}`. `legacy` (an old file's scenes on a first build) is the pool `_reclaim` draws names from.

_parts(S)Part records for a scene wider than MAX_SPAN_PX at its thickest width: its valid ink cut in two at the emptiest line across the long axis until every piece fits.§14
six._parts

The emptiest line is the lightest of 32 bins of an ink histogram over the middle 60 % (a tie goes to the middle), at most 12 cuts deep. Output only.

  • Parts are in the scene's local coordinates, so a rigid move keeps them; a part keeps its id and given name while it covers MATCH_OVERLAP of a previous part's frame.
_regions()Group more than MAX_SIBLINGS rows under one parent row (or at the top) into region records, by median splits of their shown frames' centres across the wider spread.§14
six._regions

Output only. Centres are mapped into the parent row's anchor (at the top, the heaviest row's); a group of one makes no region. A region is keyed by its parent row's founder and holds its rows' founders, which stay put through a rename or a fold.

  • A region keeps its id and given name while its founder set overlaps an earlier region's (any key) by MATCH_OVERLAP (shared ÷ union), each earlier region taken once.
_reclaim(legacy)Scenes born this batch take a kept-aside id and name whose frame they cover by MATCH_OVERLAP with a compatible width range, best cover first.§14
six._reclaim

Covers are compared rounded to 1e-9, so two names kept aside with one frame tie; ties go to the name kept most recently, then the older scene. A name whose id is live on another scene is skipped. With `legacy` (an old file's scenes on a first build) the pool is those scenes, with no range test, and nothing is taken out of it.

_parents(changed)Set each scene's parent: the scene whose frame holds its frame's centre with the smallest Lmax above its own (tie: the older).§14
six._parents

When at most an eighth of the scenes changed, only the changed ones, those whose parent changed or vanished, and those a changed coarser scene now contains are recomputed; otherwise all.

_echoes()Fold echoes into the panel's rows: top-down, a scene joins the row of its nearest ancestor (up to ECHO_UP, 8, generations) whose tightest frame and its own hold each other's centres, sizes within ECHO_ZOOM (3×).§14
six._echoes

A row's frames span at most ZOOM_SPREAD, and two renamed scenes never share one. A row shows its tightest frame and its renamed member's id and name, else its founder's (the first, coarsest member); its parent row is its founder's parent's, its ink and count its members' sums.

  • Output only: scenes, parents and the saved state are unchanged (scenes-v3 bible, Echo rows).
_echoJoins(R, S)Does a scene echo a row: its frame and the row's tightest hold each other's centres, sizes (`frameLog`) within ECHO_ZOOM, the row's span still within ZOOM_SPREAD, and not a second renamed scene?§14
six._echoJoins

Does a scene echo a row: its frame and the row's tightest hold each other's centres, sizes (`frameLog`) within ECHO_ZOOM, the row's span still within ZOOM_SPREAD, and not a second renamed scene?

_contains(P, S)Does P's frame hold the centre of S's frame, mapped into P's anchor?§14
six._contains

Does P's frame hold the centre of S's frame, mapped into P's anchor?

records()The panel's list of echo-folded rows: roots by ink, heaviest first, each followed by its parts and its child rows; a crowd of sibling rows listed under its regions.§14
six.records

A row carries its shown scene's `id` and `name` (the renamed member's, else the founder's), its tightest member's frame as `level` and `rect`, `depth`, `hash` (`rowKey`), `auto`/`pinned` and `count` (every member's objects). Its parts are the tightest member's; parts and regions carry `kind`, a child row its `parent`, a region's row its `region`.

  • A part's `hash` is the tightest member's key and its number, a region's `r` + the FNV-1a hash of its rows' keys. An unnamed part reads `<scene> · k`, an unnamed region `<first> and N more`.
rename(id, name)A user's name on a scene, part or region (trimmed, at most 120 characters); a renamed scene keeps its identity through a merge with an unnamed one.§14
six.rename

False for a blank name or an unknown id.

exportState()The saved state, `meta.sceneIndex` v 3: the counters, each scene's shell with its member strings and picture key (version and session tag), the kept-aside names and the regions.§14
six.exportState

A scene's `m` (objects) and `e` (erase footprints, by −id) strings are cached until its membership changes. `dirty` and `erase` are added by the client (`SceneClient.exportForSave`).

_restore(batch, t0)A load: the saved scenes rebuilt as shells, every object filed straight into its saved scene with no joins, and the objects the index never saw inserted by the ordinary rule.§14
six._restore

A shell with no object left keeps its name aside; one whose members no longer fit ZOOM_SPREAD drops those below the top 16×; one that lost members is split-checked whole. The saved `dirty` ids are left out of their shells and inserted; `attr` records are ignored.

  • A restore starts a new session tag; each shell keeps its saved version and tag, so an unchanged scene keeps its picture key and a new version is never keyed like an old one.
  • With no saved state (an old file) it is a fresh build, the old scenes lending their ids and names by frame overlap (`_reclaim(legacy)`).
  • Renames the batch carries are applied too: a scene's before framing, a part's or region's after `_finish`, when those exist; then the rows and regions are folded again (a name can part two scenes' row) and the list and state exported again.

sceneClient.js · sceneWorkerClient.js 774 + 58 lines

The main-thread side of the scene index: it turns the Document's events into item records at idle (chunks along the ink, the width it counts with, the table's residual) and sends one batch at a time to the index. It also records the fine eraser's footprints and writes the state a save carries. Opens the worker (`public/scene-worker.js`) that holds a scene client's index and posts it one batch at a time; where there is no Worker, or it failed, the client runs the index inline.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
now()A millisecond clock for the client's slices and waits: `performance.now()` where there is one, else `Date.now()`.
scc.now

A millisecond clock for the client's slices and waits: `performance.now()` where there is one, else `Date.now()`.

chunker(max)A running chunk builder: points go into one box until it would outgrow `max` on a side; the next box starts at the last point, so the chunks cover the ink with no gap.§14
scc.chunker

Each chunk is `x0, y0, x1, y1, len`, `len` the path length it covers. `put(x, y, jump)` with `jump` starts a new run (a new loop) with no length from the last point; `starts` lists each run's first chunk.

walkLoops(loops, max)Walk a shape's loops once: chunks along the outline, each loop's first chunk (`loops`), and its area and perimeter for its mean width.§14
scc.walkLoops

Reads the stored Loop records (line, arc, cut line, cut arc), subdividing every piece at half a chunk so a long line or arc never becomes one box. The area is the shoelace sum plus each arc's segment term.

walkPoly(rings, max, closed)Chunks along polylines, each segment subdivided at half a chunk: a stroke's centreline (open), or a fill's polygons (`closed`: each ring run back to its start, its first chunk returned in `loops`).§14
scc.walkPoly

Chunks along polylines, each segment subdivided at half a chunk: a stroke's centreline (open), or a fill's polygons (`closed`: each ring run back to its start, its first chunk returned in `loops`).

boxSize(out)The longer side of the bounding box of a chunk list, 0 when it is empty.
scc.boxSize

The longer side of the bounding box of a chunk list, 0 when it is empty.

sceneGeom(o)An object as the index sees it: the width it counts with, its chunk records in stored coordinates and each closed loop's first chunk, cached on the object.§14
scc.sceneGeom

A shape counts its thickness now, mean width 2·area ÷ perimeter, capped at its pen (walked a second time only when under half its pen); a pen-less shape or fill counts its size as one chunk; a stroke counts its pen (`lwFrame`). Chunks are CHUNK widths long, doubled until there are at most MAX_CHUNKS (2,048).

  • `loops` is null for a stroke's open centreline; a one-loop outline shares a frozen `[0]`. Cached in `o._sc`; the client drops it on a geometry change. A zero-length chunk (a dot) counts one width of ink.
isInk(doc, o)Does the index hold this object: not an eraser mark, not a stroke still being drawn, and not a ceded patch (`attachRect`, storage) while its family keeps ink outside patches?§14
scc.isInk

A patch whose family has nothing else left is the drawing, and counts as ink (`orphanPatch`).

orphanPatch(doc, o)Is this ceded patch all that is left of its family: no other member that is neither an eraser mark nor a patch?§14
scc.orphanPatch

Is this ceded patch all that is left of its family: no other member that is neither an eraser mark nor a patch?

SceneClientThe main-thread side of the scene index: a dirty set from the Document's events, item records prepared at idle, one batch at a time to the index in its worker or inline.§14
scc.SceneClient

The scene list lands in `docMeta.scenes`; the saved state rides `serializeDrawing` as `meta.sceneIndex` (`exportForSave`). Never runs while a stroke, a drag or a lasso is live, and waits behind the raster and erase workers for at most 3 s (DESIGN.md §11).

  • It also records the fine eraser's footprints and rebuilds the index from the file on a load or a reset.
SceneClient.constructor(E, { ... })Subscribe to the engine's Document, its objects and its ops, with empty dirty, z-change, gone-frame, patch-family, sent and footprint state; `worker: false` forces the inline index.§14
scc.SceneClient.constructor

The index itself opens on the first batch (`_mode`). `gen`, bumped by every restore, tells a worker result for the current document from one for the document before; `frameEv`, bumped by every frame event and settle, tells a prep that spanned one. The footprint caps are FOOT_MAX (512) and FOOT_CHUNKS (8,192).

destroy()Stop: cancel the schedule, unsubscribe from the Document and terminate the worker.§14
scc.destroy

Stop: cancel the schedule, unsubscribe from the Document and terminate the worker.

onChange(fn)Listen for each landed batch's result; returns the unsubscribe.§14
scc.onChange

Listen for each landed batch's result; returns the unsubscribe.

_onEvent(ev)A Document event marks the objects it touched dirty and schedules a batch; a reset or a load starts a full restore.§14
scc._onEvent

A live stroke waits for its finalize; an attribute-only change is kept as a z change (`attr`); a geometry change drops the object's cached `_sc`; an add, finalize or remove re-checks the patches of the object's family (`_family`).

  • Frame events count in `frameEv`. A frame merge or split dirties its ids, an added frame its objects; a removed frame is noted and the ids sent from it are dirtied at the flush (`_takeGone`); frame records themselves are diffed at the flush.
_family(o)An object added to or gone from a family with a ceded patch: that family's patches are re-checked at the flush, since whether a patch counts as ink depends on the rest of its family.§14
scc._family

An object added to or gone from a family with a ceded patch: that family's patches are re-checked at the flush, since whether a patch counts as ink depends on the rest of its family.

_onOp(ev)An erase bake hints each piece with the object it replaced, so it keeps that scene, and records the fine eraser's footprint; an eraser gesture's undo or redo turns its footprints off or on.§14
scc._onOp

A new action ends the redo branch, so footprints turned off by an undo are dropped for good. A settle counts as a frame event (`frameEv`); its natives' change events follow.

  • The hint rides the piece's first item record; the index files the piece into the replaced object's scene when the width range allows (storage, not new ink).
_footprint(markId, step)A cut by an eraser finer than the ink it cut: the mark's chunks within its reach of the cut shape become a footprint item, hosted by a surviving piece in that frame.§14
scc._footprint

Only when the eraser's pen, mapped into the cut object's frame, is thinner than the ink's counted width; a coarser one is removal. The boxes are mapped into the host's stored coordinates through its table and keyed by the host piece (item id −host); the frame's depth is kept so the footprint can follow a re-homed host.

  • One per cut, so a swipe across two drawings bridges nothing (DESIGN.md §11). The footprints are then capped (`_capFoot`).
_capFoot()Keep at most FOOT_MAX (512) footprints and FOOT_CHUNKS (8,192) chunk records: the oldest are marked to drop, and their scenes go with them.§14
scc._capFoot

Keep at most FOOT_MAX (512) footprints and FOOT_CHUNKS (8,192) chunk records: the oldest are marked to drop, and their scenes go with them.

_footItems(items)The footprints' item records for a batch: each followed to its host, re-hosted in the family when the host is gone, dropped when none is left.§14
scc._footItems

A host re-homed to a frame of the same depth (a carry, a merged shadow) takes the footprint with it, stored coordinates unchanged. Otherwise a new host is a piece of the same edit group in the footprint's frame with the same table residual.

  • A footprint turned off (its gesture undone) is sent as gone but kept for the redo; one marked to drop is sent as gone and forgotten. Only changed records are sent.
_cancel()Cancel the scheduled tick, timer or idle callback.§14
scc._cancel

_schedule(delay)Schedule one tick at idle (`requestIdleCallback`, 1 s timeout), or on a timer where there is none; a tick already scheduled stands.§14
scc._schedule

_busy()Must the index wait? Always while a stroke, a drag or a lasso is live; behind an erase job in flight or the raster worker's queue for at most MAX_WAIT_MS (3 s).§14
scc._busy

Must the index wait? Always while a stroke, a drag or a lasso is live; behind an erase job in flight or the raster worker's queue for at most MAX_WAIT_MS (3 s).

_tick(deadline)One idle tick: retry in 150 ms while busy; else step a restore, or prepare the dirty objects' records in a time slice and send the batch when they are done.§14
scc._tick

A slice is SLICE_MS (8 ms) at most, 4 at least, within the idle deadline. Nothing is sent while a batch is in flight. A new batch starts from `_takeGone` and notes `frameEv`; `_sendPrepared` sends it.

_sendPrepared(p)Send a prepared batch: the ids a frame event dirtied during the prep folded in first, then the z changes, the footprints, the frame diff and the renames.§14
scc._sendPrepared

Frame records are read at the send and item tables per slice, so after a frame event mid-prep (a settle moves a frame's shift into its natives' tables) the ids it dirtied are prepared into the batch (`_fold`) or its halves disagree. A z change goes as an `attr` record only for an object the index holds and the batch does not already carry.

_hasWork()Is there anything for a batch: dirty ids, z changes, gone frames, families to re-check, renames, footprints or a changed frame?§14
scc._hasWork

Is there anything for a batch: dirty ids, z changes, gone frames, families to re-check, renames, footprints or a changed frame?

_takeGone()Dirty the ids sent from frames removed since the last batch (one pass over `sent` for them all) and the patches of families that gained or lost an object.§14
scc._takeGone

Dirty the ids sent from frames removed since the last batch (one pass over `sent` for them all) and the patches of families that gained or lost an object.

_fold(st)Prepare the dirty ids into a batch already prepared, one record per id: a later record replaces an earlier one, keeping its chunks (with their loops) and erase hint when it has none.§14
scc._fold

Prepare the dirty ids into a batch already prepared, one record per id: a later record replaces an earlier one, keeping its chunks (with their loops) and erase hint when it has none.

_resyncWanted()Should a restore run now? With a worker, always; inline, only for a document of at most 5,000 objects or when `flushNow` forces it.§14

scc._mode

Where the index runs: in a worker if one opens (tried on the first call), else an inline SceneIndex.

_prepStep(st, budget)Turn dirty ids into item records until the budget runs out: gone for what is no longer ink, else home, width, table residual and (when new or re-shaped) chunks with their closed loops' first chunks; true when done.§14
scc._prepStep

Only what differs from the record last sent goes out; a new object carries its erase hint. A ceded patch's family is noted (`patchFam`) so its patches are re-checked when the family changes. The clock is read every 64 ids.

scc._frameRec

_frameDiff()The frame records that changed since the last batch, and `gone` for removed frames; remembers what it sent.§14
scc._frameDiff

_startResync(kind, state)Start a full restore: forget everything sent and waiting and rebuild the index from the file (`load`), or (`reset`) from the state given, else the last export.§14
scc._startResync

Bumps the generation and forgets the batch in flight, so a worker result for the document before is dropped when it arrives; notes `frameEv` for the prep. A load also drops the footprints; the file's are read in the restore's first step.

_loadFoot(list)Read the file's saved footprints (`sceneIndex.erase`), an undone gesture's still off, skipping malformed entries, then cap them (`_capFoot`).§14
scc._loadFoot

Read the file's saved footprints (`sceneIndex.erase`), an undone gesture's still off, skipping malformed entries, then cap them (`_capFoot`).

_resyncStep(budget)Step a restore: read the file's footprints, prepare a record for every object in slices, then send one restore batch with the saved state.§14
scc._resyncStep

Ids a frame event dirtied during the prep are folded in (`_fold`). A load restores from the file's index; a reset from the state it was given, falling back to the file's. The state is used only when it is v 3 with a scene list.

  • Otherwise the old `meta.scenes` lend their ids and names by frame overlap (only v2 rows, `s<n>` with no `kind`, since a v3 part's or region's id would collide with the index's own) and `sceneSeq` seeds the id counter.
_send(batch, ids)Send a batch: inline, applied at once; to the worker, one in flight at a time, tagged with the client's generation.§14
scc._send

The in-flight record keeps a restore's state, so a save meanwhile keeps what it carries as dirty. A result or failure from an earlier generation (a restore began since) is dropped. A worker failure terminates the worker and sends the index inline for good; either failure goes to `_failed` with the batch and its ids.

_failed(err, batch, ids)The index failed on a batch: warn, drop the inline index, and rebuild it from the last saved state with the failed batch's ids and everything dirty since listed as `dirty`.§14
scc._failed

The saved state is the last export, else the file's; a restore inserts the `dirty` ids by the ordinary rule. A failed restore is retried from the state it carried.

_landed(out)A batch's result: keep its saved state and timings, put the scene list in `docMeta.scenes`, tell the listeners, and schedule again if anything is owed (`_owed`).§14
scc._landed

scc.flushNow

Never inside a stroke, a drag or a lasso: it schedules instead and returns false. Forces the restore a large inline document otherwise leaves waiting (`_resyncWanted`). At most 1,000 rounds.

rename(id, name)A user's name for a scene: shown in `docMeta.scenes` at once, sent to the index with the next batch.§14
scc.rename

A user's name for a scene: shown in `docMeta.scenes` at once, sent to the index with the next batch.

exportForSave()The saved state for a file: the index's last export (or the file's own, before the first restore) with the names given since, every id not yet indexed as `dirty`, and the footprints as `erase`.§14
scc.exportForSave

`dirty` includes the ids of the batch being prepared and of an ordinary batch in flight, and what a restore under way carries as dirty (a rebuild after a failure); a load inserts them by the ordinary rule.

  • An undone gesture's footprints are saved too, marked `off`, since the op log brings the redo back after a load; dropped ones are not.

swc.setSceneTransport

workerUrl()The scene worker's script: `PUBLIC_URL` + `/scene-worker.js`.

Each client owns one worker, since the index is state. Replies are matched by id; a worker error marks it broken for the session and rejects what is pending, and the client goes inline.

Physical truth only: how big each unit is, what it is called, how it prefixes. No ladders, no bands, no rungs.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
buildRungs(defs)Turns a chain of size ratios into absolute unit sizes.§14
cat.buildRungs

Walks a ladder definition and multiplies out its `ratioFromPrev` chain into real metre values.

  • It anchors on the Planck length rather than on the metre. The definitions are written as ratios between neighbours because that is how the sizes are actually known and checked ('an inch is 25.4 mil'), and anchoring at the bottom means the smallest units — where the exponent is most extreme — are exact by construction rather than by division.
safeLog10Meters(meters)log10 of a size, without throwing at the ends of the float range.§14
cat.safeLog10Meters

Returns negative infinity rather than NaN for a size that has underflowed to zero, so a unit at the very bottom of the catalogue degrades to 'unimaginably small' instead of poisoning every comparison it takes part in.

registerUnit(rung)Files one unit in the shared registry, first definition winning.§14
cat.registerUnit

Every ladder is built independently but they share units — a metre is a metre on all of them — so the first ladder to define one fixes its physical size and later ladders adopt it.

  • That is what keeps the ladders commensurable: two ladders can disagree about which units they *contain* and can never disagree about how big one is.
repairLogFactors()Recomputes every log size once the whole registry exists.§14
cat.repairLogFactors

A pass over the finished registry, replacing each unit's log size with one taken from its linear size wherever that is finite.

  • The Planck chain is then overwritten with exact exponents from a table. Those units are separated by powers of a thousand, and multiplying the ratios out accumulates error at exactly the end of the range where there is least room for it; stating the exponents directly costs twelve lines and removes the question.
getUnit(name)One unit's record, or null.§14
cat.getUnit

The registry lookup everything else goes through.

unitMeters(name)How big one unit is, in metres.§14
cat.unitMeters

Null for an unknown name, which is how `validateScaleDef` rejects a saved scale naming a unit this build does not have.

unitLog10Meters(name)The unit's size as a log, which is what the resolver actually works in.§14
cat.unitLog10Meters

Soft-fails to NaN on a hot path rather than throwing. Every caller is inside a resolve that runs on each frame of a zoom, and one unknown unit should cost one reading, not the session.

  • Falls back to computing the log from the linear size if the cached one is not finite.
allCatalogUnits()Every registered unit, smallest first.§14
cat.allCatalogUnits

Sorted by log size, so the picker's full table reads from the Planck length up to the largest parsec multiple without any per-caller sorting.

prefixNameForShort(short)'k' to 'kilo'.§14
cat.prefixNameForShort

The SI prefix table, read backwards, for building a full display name.

cat.capitalizeWord

Used only for assembling full unit names.

cat.unitFullName

Assembled from the unit's kind rather than tabulated, so adding a prefixed unit needs no new name.

  • Named exceptions come from a small table first — the bodies and the astronomical units have real names that no rule would produce.
  • This is what makes the picker's *table* mode readable: at the point where there are too many units to show as chips, showing symbols alone would be a wall of two-letter codes.

cat.allUnitsTableRows

The last rung of the unit picker, when the reader has asked for everything.

Distinguishes a derived unit (km, nm) from a named one (inch, parsec, Planck length), which is what the picker's later rungs partition on.

Exists as its own function because it *is* a membership rule — `NoSiPrefixUnits` is built directly on it — and reading `filter(isNoSiPrefix)` says what the rung means.

The heart of the whole thing, and it is DATA rather than code: a table of per-ladder overrides over one default band of 1 to 500.

  • It is per (ladder, unit) because the same unit is preferred over different ranges on different ladders — on the ultra-imperial ladder a mile is preferred from a quarter, on standard imperial from a half — and the reason is that the ladder decides what the neighbouring rungs are and therefore what the mile has to cover.

Exists for exactly one case, and states it: the ultra-imperial ladder needs a quarter-mile, because the gap between a mile and a foot is too large for the ordinary grammar to fill sensibly.

The generator the whole resolution runs on. For each rung it works out which round numbers of that unit would produce a bar between the minimum and maximum pixel width, and emits one candidate stop per number.

  • All of it in log space, and every extreme guarded: a rung whose magnitudes fall outside the float envelope is skipped rather than allowed to produce an infinity.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
formatSciValue(value)A number in scientific notation, with a real Unicode exponent.§14
nic.formatSciValue

Renormalises after rounding, so a mantissa that rounds up to ten becomes 1 with the exponent raised rather than being printed as 10x10^n.

  • Emits superscript digits directly. `SciText` converts those to real markup at display time, because fonts draw the Latin-1 superscripts and the U+2070 block from different designs and an exponent like 37 comes out visibly mismatched.

nic.formatScaleNumber

Thousands separators above a hundred, three significant figures below, and scientific notation outside 0.001 to 5000.

  • The same function formats the zoom readout when no scale has been set, which is why an extreme zoom shows a power of ten rather than a fifteen-digit decimal.
formFor(value)Plain or scientific, for one value.§14
nic.formFor

One decision, made once, so the label and the candidate agree about which form the reading is in.

niceValuesForUnit(unit, opts)The round numbers this unit may show, inside a window.§14
nic.niceValuesForUnit

The 1/2/5 grammar, per decade, plus whatever extra values the ladder allows.

  • Inches are the one exception in the grammar. Between .02 and 1 the decimals are suppressed and the fraction chain takes over - an eighth, a sixteenth, a thirty-second - because that is how inches are read. A quarter and a half come back as plain decimals, which is also how they are read.
  • Never throws: a bad or inverted window returns nothing, and an exponent range too wide to enumerate is refused rather than looped over.
bestInBoundsNice(unit, mpp, ...)The best round number for ONE unit at this zoom.§14
nic.bestInBoundsNice

Quantises onto the unit you asked for rather than searching for a better one - that is the resolver's job, and this is used once the unit has already been decided, by a pick or by the extreme fallback.

  • Scores by closeness to the bar's target width, in log space.
  • Carries its own last-resort branch for the far ends of the range, where no ordinary candidate fits: the nearest 1/2/5 mantissa at the target exponent, bar clamped. A scale bar at the Planck length should be approximate rather than absent.

Clamped to about plus or minus 308 decades. Every conversion out of log space goes through it, so an extreme intermediate produces a very large or very small number rather than an infinity or a zero that would divide badly two lines later.

lmt.targetLogLen

The log of the number plus the unit's log size - an addition rather than a multiplication, which is the point of working in log space at all.

The bridge between the drawing and the physical world, and the only place the two meet.

scaleBar/resolve.js 214 lines

The resolution: the lowest in-range number wins. One rule, replacing every handoff table the specification used to list.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
pastIncumbentEnterEdge(ladderId, unit, tLog)Has the zoom moved far enough past the current unit's band to justify changing?§14
rsv.pastIncumbentEnterEdge

The anti-flicker margin, about five per cent past the edge of the band, expressed additively in log space because a proportional margin is an addition there.

  • It matters less than it once did. The resolution is a pure function of the zoom now - the pool is collapsed to one representative per unit before anything is ranked - so a cold resolve and a walked one agree by construction, and the wide preference bands do most of the anti-flicker work.
candidatesOnLadder(ladderId, mpp)Every legal bar on a ladder at this zoom.§14
rsv.candidatesOnLadder

A named export over `Ladder.candidatesAt`, kept because the tests and the picker rules read it directly.

extremeCandidates(ladderId, mpp)The fallback when nothing on the ladder fits.§14
rsv.extremeCandidates

Past the ends of a ladder - deep inside an atom, or out beyond the largest parsec multiple - no round number of any rung produces a bar of a sensible width.

  • Rather than show nothing, it takes the floor or the ceiling rung, whichever the zoom is nearer, and quantises onto it with the bar clamped. The reading is then honest about the unit and approximate about the width, which is the right way round.
readingFromStop(stop, mpp, reason)Packages a winning candidate as the reading the HUD renders.§14
rsv.readingFromStop

Carries the reason it won - user band, standard band, prefer-one-or-more, or bounds fit - which is what makes the resolution explainable rather than magic.

resolveReading(mpp, session, opts)THE RULE: the lowest in-range number wins.§14
rsv.resolveReading

The centre of the scale bar, and what replaced a pile of hand-written handoff tables.

  • Collapse before ranking. The pool holds many stops per unit; it is reduced to ONE representative per unit - the value that unit would actually show at this zoom - before anything is compared. That is what makes the comparison a comparison between UNITS rather than between values of one unit, and what makes the whole resolve a pure function of the zoom.
  • Then one rule. A user's range wins if it claims a candidate. Otherwise a candidate inside its unit's preferred band beats one that is not. Among those, the LOWEST DISPLAYED NUMBER wins, where a value outside any band only counts if it is at least one. Ties break on closeness to the target bar width, then rank, then value.
  • That single rule subsumes every handoff the specification used to list separately: 200 yd beats 500 ft because 200 is the lower number; a sixteenth of an inch beats 50 mil because a banded sub-one value still counts; one foot beats ten inches because both are outside a band and one is the lower value at or above one.
  • An all-sub-one pool pulls to the finest rung. Below every band the honest reading is the smallest unit, not a fraction of a larger one.

scaleBar/pick.js 158 lines

What a reader's unit pick does — switch ladders, or install a range whose edges are found by scanning the resolver.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
autoSpanForUnit(ladderId, unit)Finds where a unit would NATURALLY be chosen, by scanning the resolver.§14
pck.autoSpanForUnit

Sweeps sixteen decades of zoom, asking the automatic rule what it would show at each step, and records the span over which the answer is this unit.

  • Derived rather than tabulated, and that is the point. The earlier design carried a table of far edges per unit which had to be maintained in step with the preference bands, and silently disagreed with them whenever one moved. Asking the resolver means the answer cannot disagree with the resolver.
  • About four hundred probes, run once per pick - a human action - so the cost does not matter.
applyUnitPick(pickedUnit, mpp, session)What happens when the reader picks a unit.§14
pck.applyUnitPick

Two outcomes, and choosing between them is the whole design.

  • If some ladder would already show that unit here, just switch ladders. Asking for inches where an imperial ladder would have shown inches is not an override, it is a change of system, and it should not install anything that has to be torn down later.
  • Otherwise install a user range. The unit is quantised onto a legal round number and a range is installed spanning from where the reader is now out to the edges of the unit's natural territory. Zooming inside that span keeps the unit; outside it the automatic rule resumes; the range persists until another pick.
  • A pick of a different unit tears down any existing range first, so the state cannot accumulate.
