scaleBar/format.js · validate.js · index.js 18 + 20 + 108 lines

The visible label, the persisted definition, and the facade the editor calls.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
formatUnitSymbol(unit)The unit's symbol, with the Planck subscript corrected.§14
fmt.formatUnitSymbol

One substitution, and it exists because the catalogue spells the Planck length with a letter that has no subscript form in the font stack.

formatScaleLabel(reading)The visible label: the number, then the symbol.§14
fmt.formatScaleLabel

Presentation only. Number grammar lives in `nice.js`; this assembles.

  • Prefers whatever specialised label the reading carries - a fraction, or a scientific form - and falls back to formatting the raw value.
validateScaleDef(raw)Accepts a saved scale definition, or rejects it whole.§14
val.validateScaleDef

Four fields and nothing else: a length, a unit, the bar width it was drawn at, and the zoom it was drawn at.

  • Legacy `minUnit` fields from older documents are dropped rather than migrated. Preferred ranges replaced that mechanism entirely, so carrying them forward would preserve state nothing reads - which is worse than no state, because it looks meaningful.
computeScale(effectiveZoom, scaleDef, session, opts)The facade: zoom in, reading out.§14
sbi.computeScale

Three steps, and the order is the design. Convert the zoom to metres per pixel; tear down a user range that has nothing left to claim; resolve on the sticky session.

  • Returns the session as well as the reading, because the resolve updates display-only fields, and the caller owns that state. The ladder and the range are never changed here - installing those belongs to a pick or to clearing the scale, both of which are human actions.

10 Shell

Everything between the engine and the person

hooks/useKobinEngine.js 1,044 lines

The editor's engine lifecycle: mounts the engine with the renderer the URL chooses, wires input to it, owns the tool and style state, runs the local autosave into the kobin-2 store (DESIGN.md §13), and hands the sync session its controls (read-only, saving gate, flush, reload).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
now()Monotonic time, falling back to the wall clock.§13
hok.now

The saver's one clock: its serialise and write timings, the debounce ceiling, the failure backoff and the store reload's duration all read it.

rasterFromUrl(href)Decides the session's renderer from the URL: raster by default, SVG under `?svg` or an explicit `?raster=0`.§9
hok.rasterFromUrl

Reads the query wherever it is, in the hash (where the router keeps it) or the search. `svg=0`, `false` or `off` does not gate, and a bare `?raster` decides nothing. Both names must end at `&`, `#` or the end of the URL, so `?svgExport` or `?rasterWorkers` decide nothing.

  • Read once, at construction: the renderer owns a canvas, a plate cache and a worker pool, so the dev panel's control rewrites the URL (`hrefWithRaster`) and reloads.
hrefWithRaster(href, on)The same URL with the `?svg` gate cleared (`on` true) or set (`on` false), where the query already lives.§9
hok.hrefWithRaster

Removes every `svg` and `raster` parameter and any `?` or `&` left dangling, then appends `svg` at the end, which is inside the hash route when there is one. The dev panel's renderer control uses it and reloads.

signCursor(plus)Draws the ctrl cursor - an arrow with a plus or minus badge.§13
hok.signCursor

An SVG data URI rather than a stock cursor, because no standard cursor keyword means 'add to selection'. The nearest one, `copy`, shows a plus that means duplicate.

  • The badge is the product's own terracotta, taken from the design file so that the cursor and the selection ants are visibly the same colour.
useKobinEngine({ canvasId, onAutosave, gated, onRefused })THE ENGINE LIFECYCLE the product uses.§13
hok.useKobinEngine

Mounts the engine into a host element with the renderer `rasterFromUrl` chooses, wires pointer, wheel, pinch, resize and keyboard input to it, owns every piece of tool and style state, and runs the local autosave into the kobin-2 store (DESIGN.md §13).

  • Status is throttled to 50 ms, except zoom. A React re-render of the whole editor per pointer event costs about twelve milliseconds, which a gesture cannot afford. Zoom changes are flushed immediately anyway, because the scale HUD reads them and a coalesced burst would make the bar skip a rung.
  • Autosave (`LOCAL_AUTOSAVE`, the kill switch, is on): a write waits 1.5 s behind the last change and never more than 8 s from the first, and flushes on tab hide, pagehide and unmount. It appends the op log's entries, snapshots only the frames an undo, redo or move forced or whose entries have outgrown their snapshot (64 KiB or a quarter of it), and compacts the log to a floor under every snapshot, the undo and redo stacks and every pending mark. A failed write keeps its entries and forced frames, is not retried for the same document state until its backoff lapses (8 s to 256 s), and shows in `saveError` and the report's errors.
  • One writer (SYNC-PLAN R2). With `gated` (the editor) the engine starts read-only and the saver closed until the sync session opens them. Every store write carries the tab's token (`setWriter`); a write the store refuses as `fenced` or `stale` closes the saver, keeps the work in memory and calls `onRefused`. For the session it returns `setReadOnly` (a gesture in progress ends as a pen-up would), `setSaving`, `flushSave`, `idle`, `hasUnsaved`, `keepUnsaved` (the document in memory saved as a new canvas), `knownSeq`, `reloadFromStore` (with `keepCamera` when following another tab or device; resolves the ms it took), `refreshMetaFromStore` (a header-only write followed without a reload: the name, the scale and scene names) and `cloudPushSource`, which reads the local store, never the live document. `onAutosave` says whether a write moved data, so a follower can tell the two apart.
  • The document comes back asynchronously (`loadCanvasStore`: snapshots through `loadDrawing` without a render, then the log replayed) and is rendered a task later (`renderLoaded`), so the load and a cold render are not one long task (STALL, 2026-09-23); `engineReady` waits for both. A store that will not decode is copied into the bin (`backupCanvasDoc`, awaited) before the first autosave may write over it.
  • Two pointers are a pinch. A stroke under 400 ms old when the second finger lands is cancelled rather than finalised, because it was the first finger arriving and not a mark; a blur or a hidden tab ends any gesture in progress as a pen-up would.
fmtZoom(z)A zoom factor as a short human number.§13
hok.fmtZoom

Thousands and millions only where the quotient stays short. Beyond that it hands over to the scale bar's scientific formatter, because dividing by a million and printing the result gave things like `1500646128030403.00M`.

zoomLabel(zoom)The zoom readout, as a multiplier or a fraction.§13
hok.zoomLabel

Below one it reads as a fraction rather than a decimal, because at these depths the decimal is all zeroes.

hooks/reportSend.js 223 lines

The dev report's transport: build, one stringify with the user's identity scrubbed, gzip off the main thread, POSTed in parts to `tools/report-server.js` on :3001, and the whole drawing after it when asked. A send that fails is saved as a file. Dev only: the `?dev` panel and `window.__kobinReport`.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
msg(err)An error's message cut to 160 characters, for the sender's `why`.
rps.msg

An error's message cut to 160 characters, for the sender's `why`.

installConsoleTap(con)Wraps `console.error` and `console.warn`, once, so the last 50 warnings and errors are kept for the report.§15
rps.installConsoleTap

Each entry is its time, level and the arguments joined as text (an Error as name and message, anything else as JSON), cut to 300 characters. The original method still runs, and a failure inside the tap never stops a log.

  • The hook installs it where it exposes `window.__kobinReport`: a dev build, or `?dev`.
consoleTail()A copy of the tapped warnings and errors: the report's console section unless the caller passes its own.§15
rps.consoleTail

A copy of the tapped warnings and errors: the report's console section unless the caller passes its own.

safeJson(v)A logged value as JSON cut to 300 characters, or `String(v)` when it will not stringify.
rps.safeJson

A logged value as JSON cut to 300 characters, or `String(v)` when it will not stringify.

scrubIdentity(text, secrets)Takes who the user is out of the report text: each secret the caller passes, and anything shaped like an email, a JWT or a Google API key.§15
rps.scrubIdentity

Secrets under four characters are ignored. Each pattern runs only where its anchor occurs (`@`, `eyJ`, `AIza`): the email pattern has no literal prefix and would otherwise walk every digit run of the geometry.

encodeText(s)A string as UTF-8 bytes: `TextEncoder` where there is one, else a hand-written encoder sized by `byteLen`.
rps.encodeText

A string as UTF-8 bytes: `TextEncoder` where there is one, else a hand-written encoder sized by `byteLen`.

reportId()A report id: the ISO time with `:` and `.` as `-`, and six random base-36 characters.
rps.reportId

A report id: the ISO time with `:` and `.` as `-`, and six random base-36 characters.

baseUrl(host, base)The report server's origin: `base` when given, else port 3001 on `host` or on the host that served the page.
rps.baseUrl

So a phone on the LAN posts to the machine it loaded the app from.

post(url, body, fetchFn)One POST of bytes to the report server with a 60 s timeout, answered as `{ ok, j }` or `{ ok: false, why }` in words.
rps.post

Never throws: a refusal carries the status and the server's `error`, an abort says the server did not answer in 60 s, anything else that the server is not reachable.

sendDevReport(E, opts)The Report button's path: build, one stringify with identity scrubbed, gzip off the main thread, POSTed in parts, then the whole drawing when asked.§15
rps.sendDevReport

In order: `buildReport` (with this module's console tail), a `drawing` summary when the opt-in plans parts (`drawingPlan`), one `JSON.stringify` through `scrubIdentity`, the raster section's `"reportBytes":null` hole filled with the body's byte size, UTF-8 bytes, `compression().gzip` (the raw bytes if that throws), then POSTs of at most 8 MB each (`PART_BYTES`) as `kind=json`. Returns what happened with each stage's ms; `onStage` gets the button's label.

  • A send that fails saves the gzip as a file (`saveFile`) unless `download` is false. The whole drawing (`sendDrawing`) goes only after the report has landed.
  • `tools/report-server.js` refuses a part over 32 MB.
sendDrawing(plan, { ... })Sends the whole drawing's planned parts, one task each: encode as a kobin-2 chunk, gzip, POST as `kind=drawing`.§15
rps.sendDrawing

Yields before each part and releases its natives once encoded; the first part that fails to encode or post stops the rest and says why. Records the encode time in total and the longest, and the bytes before and after gzip.

saveFile(u8, name)Saves bytes as a download through a temporary object URL; returns the name, or null where there is no page to save from.
rps.saveFile

Saves bytes as a download through a temporary object URL; returns the name, or null where there is no page to save from.

replayReport(E, opts)The harness's loader: fetches a report from the report server (by name, or the newest) and loads it into `E`, with its whole drawing when it has one.§15
rps.replayReport

The drawing's part files are found through the server's `/list` entry for the report and gunzipped by name (`.gz`) before `loadReport`. Exposed as `window.__kobinReport.replayReport` for the second-engine harness.

storage/db.js 660 lines

The browser-side store on IndexedDB: one header per canvas, the kobin-2 frame snapshots and op log (and the v1 frame records an old canvas still opens from), thumbnails as JPEG bytes under a 12 MiB LRU budget, bin payloads and pre-pull backups, all structured data with no JSON text and no compression. It knows nothing of the engine; `localCanvases.js` is its only importer (DESIGN.md §13).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
idbAvailable()Whether this environment has IndexedDB: false where the global is missing or reading it throws.
db.idbAvailable

Whether this environment has IndexedDB: false where the global is missing or reading it throws.

openDb()The one IndexedDB connection, opened and upgraded on first use; resolves null where the database is missing or refused.§13
db.openDb

Caches one promise. The upgrade creates whichever stores are missing: `canvases` (headers), `frames` (v1), `thumbs` (indexed by canvas and by `usedAt`), `trash`, `backups`, and version 2's `frames2` and `log`; every per-canvas store has a `byCanvas` index.

  • On `versionchange` (a newer build upgrading in another tab) it closes and forgets the connection, so the next call opens afresh. A null connection makes `tx` resolve null and do nothing.
_resetDbForTests()Tests only: closes and forgets the cached connection, since fake-indexeddb is reset between tests.
db._resetDbForTests

Tests only: closes and forgets the cached connection, since fake-indexeddb is reset between tests.

reqp(r)An IndexedDB request as a promise of its result.
db.reqp

An IndexedDB request as a promise of its result.

tx(names, mode, fn)Runs `fn` over the named stores inside one transaction and resolves with its value once the transaction commits.§13
db.tx

Resolves only on `complete`, so an awaited write is on disk; rejects on abort, and aborts the transaction when `fn` throws or its promise rejects. Resolves null, doing nothing, where there is no database.

  • `fn` may be async, but a request issued after an `await` must follow directly from one that just completed: a transaction auto-commits the moment it has nothing in flight.
only(v)`IDBKeyRange.only(v)`, for the per-canvas index lookups.
db.only

`IDBKeyRange.only(v)`, for the per-canvas index lookups.

putCanvas(id, { ... })Writes a canvas in the v1 store: its header and one record of kobin-1 natives per frame, in one transaction.§13
db.putCanvas

`frames` holds the frames to write and `frameIds` the full set. An incremental write deletes the frames that left the set since the last one; `full` makes the stored set match exactly.

  • Resolves false, writing nothing, for an incremental write of a canvas with no header: the header would list frames the store does not hold.
  • Callers: the localStorage migration and `localCanvases.writeCanvas`. The saver writes kobin-2 through `putCanvas2`.
headerToDoc(h, natives)Builds the kobin-1 envelope from a stored header and a natives map, leaving the listing fields behind.§13
db.headerToDoc

Keeps `format`, `version`, `meta`, `camera` and `crossings`; the header's name, stats, frame list, seqs and sync fields are not part of the document.

getCanvasHeader(id)One canvas's stored header (listing fields, meta, frame seqs, sync fields) without reading a frame.§13
db.getCanvasHeader

One canvas's stored header (listing fields, meta, frame seqs, sync fields) without reading a frame.

listCanvasHeaders()Every stored canvas header, for the storage sweep; an empty list where there is no database.§13
db.listCanvasHeaders

Every stored canvas header, for the storage sweep; an empty list where there is no database.

patchCanvasHeader(id, fn, writer)Rewrites one stored header through `fn`, touching no frame; false when the canvas has none, 'fenced' when another tab holds the store.§13
db.patchCanvasHeader

With a `writer` token the patch is refused as 'fenced' when the header names a different writer (SYNC-PLAN R2); without one (the gallery's rename, `claimStore`) it always applies. The id is re-applied after `fn`, so `fn` cannot move the record.

deleteCanvas(id)Deletes a canvas's header and all its records in the v1 frames, `frames2` and log stores, in one transaction.§13
db.deleteCanvas

Thumbnails, the bin payload and the backup are left: a binned canvas keeps its covers, and `sweepStorage` drops thumbnails nothing lists.

deleteOrphanFrames()Deletes frame and log records whose canvas header is gone (a torn delete); returns how many went.§13
db.deleteOrphanFrames

Walks every key of the three stores against the set of header ids. Run by `sweepStorage`.

bufferOf(geo)The ArrayBuffer to store for a Float64Array: its own buffer when the view spans all of it, else a copy of the view's bytes.
db.bufferOf

A structured clone of a buffer copies all of it, so a view into a larger buffer is sliced to its own bytes first.

putCanvas2(id, { ... })Writes a canvas in the kobin-2 store in one transaction: the header, the frame snapshots given, the new log entries and the compaction.§13
db.putCanvas2

`snapshots` maps frame id to `{ objects, geo, seq }` and `frameIds` is the full set; the header's `frameSeq` keeps each frame's snapshot seq and loses frames that left. `full` makes the stored frame set match exactly and deletes the canvas's v1 frame records; `resetLog` empties the log first; `dropBelow` deletes the entries with a seq under it.

  • Writes nothing and resolves: false for an incremental write of a canvas with no header on disk (the saver retries in full); 'fenced' when `writer` is given and the stored header names another writer (SYNC-PLAN R2); 'stale' when the new header's seq is behind the stored kobin-2 one and `rewind` is not set, so a document the store was pulled in under cannot overwrite the pull. Only a whole-document write and a full pull rewind.
  • The sync fields (`base`, `intent`, `pending`, `writer`) are carried over from the stored header unless the new header names them, because the saver's header never does; a given `writer` is stamped on the header.
getCanvas2(id)Reads a stored canvas: header, frame snapshots and log entries for kobin-2, `{ legacy }` for a v1 canvas, or null.§13
db.getCanvas2

Frame geometry comes back as a Float64Array over the stored buffer; entries are sorted by seq, one with no geometry given an empty Float64Array.

  • A v1 canvas is reassembled as a kobin-1 document; its next full write moves it into `frames2`.
  • One transaction for the whole canvas: `loadCanvasDoc` reads through it, and `getCanvas2Chunked` falls back to it; the editor's restore reads chunked.
copyCanvas2(fromId, toId, patch)Copies every record of a stored canvas to a new id in one transaction, the header through `patch`.§13
db.copyCanvas2

The v1 frames, the `frames2` snapshots and the log are copied as they are, so the copy keeps its undo history. Resolves true only when the source had a header.

  • Called by `copyCanvas2Chunked` for a v1 canvas and when the source changed during a chunked copy.
stamp(h)A header's fingerprint for the chunked read and copy: its seq, `savedAt`, frame seqs and frame ids, or '' for none.§13
db.stamp

A store write sets `savedAt`, so a write that lands between two reads of the header changes the stamp. A header patch that touches none of these fields (a rename, the sync fields) leaves it as it was.

getCanvas2Chunked(id, { ... })Reads a stored canvas as `getCanvas2` does, in short transactions: the header, one frame per transaction, the log, then the header again.§13
db.getCanvas2Chunked

If the stamp changed during the read (a write landed), it reads again, three tries, then falls back to `getCanvas2` in one transaction; a v1 canvas goes straight there. The frames are the ones the header lists; `onChunk` runs after each, for tests. Read by `loadCanvasStore`, the editor's restore and reload.

  • A transaction's scope is a whole store, so one that reads a whole canvas holds up every read-write on these stores across the origin. Measured 2026-09-22 in Chrome on a store the size of the Magnum Opus (60 frames, 42,856 objects, 60 MB of geometry): a one-transaction read 400–500 ms, a small write elsewhere waiting all of it; one frame per transaction, 25 ms at most, the small write waiting 1–3 ms.
copyCanvas2Chunked(fromId, toId, patch)Copies a stored canvas as `copyCanvas2` does, in short transactions: one frame per transaction, then the log, the header last.§13
db.copyCanvas2Chunked

The header, through `patch`, is written only if the source's stamp has not changed, so a copy torn midway has no header and the gallery's sweep deletes its records (`deleteOrphanFrames`). If the source did change, the partial copy is deleted and the copy made again in one transaction; a v1 canvas goes straight to `copyCanvas2`. True when the copy landed.

  • The source must not change meanwhile: its callers (`forkCanvas`, `stashCanvasStore`) run while the session holds the pen with the saver off. Measured on the same Magnum Opus-sized store: a one-transaction copy 1.4 s, a small write elsewhere waiting all of it.
putTrashDoc(id, doc, deletedAt)Stores a binned canvas's whole kobin-1 document in the `trash` store, stamped with when it was deleted.§13
db.putTrashDoc

Stores a binned canvas's whole kobin-1 document in the `trash` store, stamped with when it was deleted.

getTrashDoc(id)A binned canvas's stored document, or null.§13
db.getTrashDoc

A binned canvas's stored document, or null.

deleteTrashDoc(id)Deletes a binned canvas's stored document.§13
db.deleteTrashDoc

Deletes a binned canvas's stored document.

listTrashIds()The ids the `trash` store holds, for the sweep that drops payloads with no bin row.§13
db.listTrashIds

The ids the `trash` store holds, for the sweep that drops payloads with no bin row.

putBackup(id, doc, at)Stores a backup of a canvas's document, one per canvas, the newest replacing the last.§13
db.putBackup

Stores a backup of a canvas's document, one per canvas, the newest replacing the last.

getBackup(id)A canvas's backup document, or null.§13
db.getBackup

Only the tests read it; the app has no restore-from-backup action.

sweepBackups(maxAgeMs)Deletes backups older than `maxAgeMs`, and any whose date will not parse; returns how many went.§13
db.sweepBackups

`sweepStorage` runs it with a week (`BACKUP_TTL_MS`).

dataUrlToBytes(dataUrl)Parses a data URL into its media type and an ArrayBuffer of its bytes, or null.
db.dataUrlToBytes

Reads base64 and percent-encoded bodies. Thumbnails are stored as bytes because base64 is a third bigger.

bytesToDataUrl(type, bytes)Encodes stored bytes back into a base64 data URL.
db.bytesToDataUrl

Builds the binary string 32 KiB at a time: `String.fromCharCode.apply` takes the bytes as arguments, and a whole image would exceed the argument limit.

putThumbs(canvasId, map)Stores scene thumbnails as JPEG bytes with their content hashes, then trims the store to its budget, in one transaction.§13
db.putThumbs

`map` is `{ sceneId: { hash, data } }`; an entry whose data is not a data URL is skipped. Each record carries its size and `usedAt`, which the trim reads.

  • One transaction: a failure loses the whole batch, and `localCanvases.saveThumbs` swallows it.
trimThumbs(thumbs, budget)Evicts least-recently-used thumbnails until the store holds at most `budget` bytes; returns how many went.§13
db.trimThumbs

Runs inside the caller's transaction (`putThumbs`, `sweepThumbs`). The budget is `THUMB_BUDGET_BYTES`, 12 MiB.

getThumbs(canvasId, sceneIds)The stored thumbnails for some scenes of one canvas, as data URLs, marking each one found as just used.§13
db.getThumbs

A read-write transaction because a hit rewrites `usedAt`: being read is what keeps a thumbnail from LRU eviction. Missing scenes are simply absent.

deleteThumbs(canvasId)Deletes every thumbnail of one canvas; returns how many went.§13
db.deleteThumbs

Called when a bin entry expires or is purged.

sweepThumbs(keepIds, budget)Deletes the thumbnails of every canvas not in `keepIds`, then trims to the budget; returns how many went.§13
db.sweepThumbs

`sweepStorage` passes the gallery's and the bin's ids, so a binned canvas keeps its covers.

thumbBytesTotal()The bytes the thumbnail store holds.§13
db.thumbBytesTotal

Only the tests read it.

packSlot(json)Writes a document string in the old localStorage slot form: `lz1:` then lz-string's UTF-16 compression.§13
db.packSlot

Nothing in the app writes slots; the tests seed old slots with it for the migration. `localCanvases` re-exports it.

unpackSlot(raw)Reads an old localStorage slot: an `lz1:` slot decompressed, a plain-JSON one returned as it is, null for null.§13
db.unpackSlot

The one-time migration's reader. `localCanvases` re-exports it.

migrateLocalStorage(docToRecord)Moves every document, bin payload and thumbnail out of localStorage into IndexedDB and deletes the keys, once per browser.§13
db.migrateLocalStorage

Skipped when the `kobin.idb.migrated` flag is set, localStorage throws, or there is no database. Each `kobin.canvas.*` slot goes into the v1 store through `putCanvas` (full), each `kobin.trash.*` into `trash`, the `kobin.thumb.*` keys into `thumbs` a canvas at a time; `.bak` copies, `boundlessDrawing*` and `kobinSnapshot` are deleted unread.

  • A key that fails is left in place and named in the console, and the flag is still set, so it is not tried again; only a flag that will not write makes the next load retry.
  • `docToRecord` is passed in because it lives in `localCanvases`, this module's only importer.
storageEstimate()The browser's `{ usage, quota }` for this origin in bytes, or null where it will not say.
db.storageEstimate

The browser's `{ usage, quota }` for this origin in bytes, or null where it will not say.

requestPersistentStorage()Asks the browser not to evict this origin's storage under pressure; true when it is, or already was, persisted.§13
db.requestPersistentStorage

The gallery asks on mount. Chrome grants it silently by engagement, Firefox prompts, Safari ignores it; a signed-out user's drawings exist nowhere else.

readPushState(id, cloudFrameSeq, fromSeq)What a cloud push sends, read in one transaction so the three agree: the header, the frames the cloud lacks, and the entries after `fromSeq`.§13
db.readPushState

A frame is read when the cloud has no seq for it or a different one; the entries are those in (`fromSeq`, header seq], ascending, one with no geometry given an empty Float64Array. Null for a canvas not in the kobin-2 store.

  • Read through `cloudPushSource`'s `read`.

storage/localCanvases.js 702 lines

The local store's public face: whole-document and saver writes, the editor's restore read, the recycle bin, thumbnails, the one-time migrations, the gallery's sweep, and the sync's reads and writes of the kobin-2 store (pushes, pulls, stashes, conflict copies, one tab's writer claim). The gallery index, the bin index and the device id and name stay in localStorage, read synchronously (DESIGN.md §13).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
slotKey(id)The old localStorage key of one canvas's slot, `kobin.canvas.<id>`; nothing writes it now.§13
loc.slotKey

Exported for the tests of the one-time migration, which seed old slots with it; the migration itself (`db.migrateLocalStorage`) matches the prefix directly. Documents live in IndexedDB (DESIGN.md §13).

thumbKey(canvasId, sceneId)The old localStorage key of one scene thumbnail, `kobin.thumb.<canvas>.<scene>`; nothing writes it now.§13
loc.thumbKey

Exported for the migration's tests. Thumbnails are records in IndexedDB keyed `[canvasId, sceneId]`, under a 12 MiB LRU budget (`db.putThumbs`).

newCanvasId()A fresh canvas id.§13
loc.newCanvasId

Time in base 36 plus eight random base-36 characters: sortable and short. Four collided when two ids were minted in one millisecond (measured: 199 distinct ids from 200 in the uniqueness test).

  • Also mints the device id.
getDeviceId()A stable id for this browser.§13
loc.getDeviceId

`kobin.device` in localStorage, minted once with `newCanvasId`; 'unknown' where localStorage throws. The cloud lease and a push's manifest carry it, so a device recognises its own lease and, for a cloud copy from before versions, its own push (DESIGN.md §13).

getDeviceName()This device's name as other devices see it: the stored one, else the browser and OS read from the user agent.§13
loc.getDeviceName

Kept in localStorage (`kobin.deviceName`). The cloud lease carries it, so a read-only device shows 'editing on <name>', and a conflict's copy is named after it.

setDeviceName(name)Stores this device's name, trimmed and cut to 40 characters; a blank name is ignored.§13
loc.setDeviceName

Stores this device's name, trimmed and cut to 40 characters; a blank name is ignored.

readIndex()The gallery index, defensively.§13
loc.readIndex

Returns an empty list rather than throwing on anything malformed, and drops rows without a string id. The index is a convenience over the stored documents, which are the real data (`sweepStorage` adopts any it misses), so it must never be the thing that stops the app starting.

writeIndex(list)Writes the index, reporting quota failure.§13
loc.writeIndex

Returns false rather than throwing, because a full quota is an expected state here and every caller has something better to do than unwind.

statsFromNatives(natives)Stroke count and level span of a natives map, for the gallery badge and the stored header.§13
loc.statsFromNatives

Strokes counts every object in every frame. The span is taken only over frame ids that are plain numbers, which in the lattice are the spine frames (their id is their depth), so ink only in an off-spine frame such as `3/1,2` adds strokes and no levels.

  • The saver writes the result into every header it stores; the gallery's `depthLabel` shows the levels.
statsFromDoc(doc)Stroke and depth counts for a gallery badge.§13
loc.statsFromDoc

`statsFromNatives` over the document's natives: strokes in every frame, the level span over numeric frame ids only (the spine frames). It is also how the editor decides whether an unlisted canvas is worth keeping as a draft - a canvas with no strokes is not.

upsertIndexEntry(entry)Adds or refreshes one index row.§13
loc.upsertIndexEntry

Newest first, sorted on write, so the signed-out gallery shows the index as it stands; a signed-in gallery re-sorts its merge with the cloud listing.

docName(doc, fallback)A document's display name: `meta.name` unless it is missing or the engine's default `untitled`, else the fallback.§13
loc.docName

A document's display name: `meta.name` unless it is missing or the engine's default `untitled`, else the fallback.

docToRecord(doc)Turns a kobin-1 document into the `{ header, frames, frameIds }` a whole write stores, listing fields added.§13
loc.docToRecord

The header is the envelope without natives plus `name`, `strokes`, `levels` and, when `meta.modifiedAt` parses, `savedAt` from it, so a migrated or adopted drawing keeps its real edit date. Used by `saveCanvasDoc`, and passed to the localStorage migration.

saveCanvasDoc(id, doc)Writes a whole kobin-1 document into the kobin-2 store: every frame a fresh snapshot, an empty log, seq 0.§13
loc.saveCanvasDoc

Each frame is encoded with `format2.encodeRecords`; `full`, `resetLog` and `rewind` replace whatever was stored, even a store whose seq is ahead, and with no writer token it is never fenced. `base` and `intent` are written null: a document written whole has no cloud lineage, which the next open decides (SYNC-PLAN R4).

  • Resolves true when stored and false on any failure; never throws. Used by restore, duplicate, the legacy-autosave migration, the gallery's import, the hook's `keepUnsaved` (work that could not be written here, kept as a new canvas) and both sides of an old lz1 cloud copy's pull.
writeCanvas2(id, args)The saver's write: this tick's log entries, the frames it snapshotted, the full frame set and the compaction floor, passed to `putCanvas2`.§13
loc.writeCanvas2

Rejects on failure, so the saver can tell a full store from anything else. Resolves false when there is no stored header and `full` was not set, and 'fenced' or 'stale' when `putCanvas2` refuses (the store is another tab's, or ahead of this document); the saver then stops writing and hands either to the session (`onRefused`), which keeps the work in memory as a new canvas.

loadCanvasStore(id)What the editor restores from: the stored header, frame snapshots by id and log entries; `{ legacy }` for a v1 canvas; or null.§13
loc.loadCanvasStore

Reads through `getCanvas2Chunked`, one frame per transaction, so restoring a large canvas does not hold up writes elsewhere in the origin. Null on a read failure as well as for no canvas.

  • The editor's restore and its reload after another tab or a pull wrote the store both read it, and replay the entries past each frame's seq (DESIGN.md §13).
writeCanvas(id, { ... })An incremental or full write of kobin-1 frames into the v1 store, through `putCanvas`.§13
loc.writeCanvas

No caller in the app; the tests drive the v1 store through it. The saver writes kobin-2 through `writeCanvas2`.

loadCanvasDoc(id)A stored canvas as ONE kobin-1 document with plain arrays: its frames with the log tail folded in (`docFromStore`), or null.§13
loc.loadCanvasDoc

Null for no canvas and on any read or fold failure.

  • Callers: the gallery's download and its cloud catch-up for a canvas still in the v1 store, and `trashCanvas`, `duplicateCanvas` and `backupCanvasDoc` for a v1 canvas (a kobin-2 one is kept or copied whole).
hasCanvasDoc(id)Whether a canvas has a stored header.§13
loc.hasCanvasDoc

Only the tests call it.

removeCanvas(id)Deletes a canvas with no bin row: its gallery row, and its stored records unless the bin holds it as a whole store.§13
loc.removeCanvas

Its index row goes, and every stored record (header, frames, log) unless the bin lists the id as a whole store (`isBinnedStore`: binned by another tab or a cloud tombstone while this one had it open), which is the bin's to keep. Its thumbnails are left for `sweepStorage`.

  • Called for a canvas the gallery never listed: the editor's delete of an empty scratch canvas, and Discard when leaving an unsaved one.
isBinnedStore(id)Whether the bin lists `id` as a whole store (`store: true`), read synchronously from the bin index.§13
loc.isBinnedStore

The editor's leave prompt asks it: a canvas binned by another tab or a cloud tombstone while this one had it open is not offered as a draft, since the bin has it, edits included. `removeCanvas` leaves such a store to the bin.

renameCanvasLocal(id, name, savedAt)Renames without opening the editor.§13
loc.renameCanvasLocal

Writes both the index row and the name embedded in the document, so the next cloud save or pull carries the new name rather than reverting it.

backupCanvasDoc(id)Keeps a copy of a stored canvas that failed to open, before an autosave may write over it; best-effort.§13
loc.backupCanvasDoc

A kobin-2 canvas is copied whole into the bin as '<name> (could not be opened)' (`binCopy`, every record, since reading it is what failed; F86), once per stored seq: a bin row with the same `backupOf` and `seq` means the copy is already there.

  • A v1 canvas's `loadCanvasDoc` document goes to the `backups` store, one per canvas, the newest replacing the last; `sweepStorage` drops it after a week. Called when the editor's restore cannot decode the stored copy.
readTrashIndex()The bin's index from localStorage: an empty list on anything malformed, rows without a string id dropped.§13
loc.readTrashIndex

The bin's index from localStorage: an empty list on anything malformed, rows without a string id dropped.

writeTrash(list)Writes the bin index.§13
loc.writeTrash

Swallows a quota failure: failing to record a deletion must not fail the deletion.

readTrash(...)The bin, newest first, purging what has expired.§13
loc.readTrash

Expiry happens on read rather than on a timer. There is no timer in a browser that can be relied on to run, and the bin is only interesting at the moment somebody looks at it.

  • An expired entry, older than 30 days (`TRASH_TTL_MS`), takes its stored document and its thumbnails with it, and for a whole-store row (`store`: a binned kobin-2 canvas, a stash or a backup) the store's records too, unless the gallery lists that id again (`isIndexed`).
isIndexed(id)Whether the gallery index lists `id`.§13
loc.isIndexed

A whole-store bin row whose id is listed again (a tombstone undone elsewhere) never deletes that store on expiry or purge (`readTrash`, `purgeTrashEntry`).

trashCanvas(id, fallbackEntry)Moves a canvas to the recycle bin: a kobin-2 canvas stays stored and only its row moves; a v1 canvas's document goes to the `trash` store and its records are deleted.§13
loc.trashCanvas

A kobin-2 canvas keeps every record, op log and undo history included. Its bin row carries `store: true` and the header's stroke and level counts, so a restore only lists it again and an expiry or purge deletes the records.

  • A v1 canvas's document is `loadCanvasDoc`'s (plain arrays), written anew on a restore. If that bin write fails the stored canvas is still deleted and the row still listed; a cloud copy, where there is one, holds the data.
  • An older bin row for the same id is dropped first, so it cannot expire over this one. The fallback entry covers a canvas with no index row - a never-saved scratch, or a cloud-only listing - so the bin still shows a row for it.
restoreCanvas(id)Brings a binned canvas back.§13
loc.restoreCanvas

A whole-store row (`store`: a binned kobin-2 canvas, a stash or a backup) still has its records, so it is only listed again, without its bin fields. Otherwise the bin's document goes back through `saveCanvasDoc`: a fresh kobin-2 store with an empty log and no cloud lineage. The index row is rebuilt only when the bin held a stored document; a cloud-only row comes back through the cloud listing instead, which is the one path that has the data.

  • If the write fails (quota) the entry stays in the bin rather than being lost between the two.
stashOverwrittenVersion(doc, name)Files the losing side of a cross-device overwrite in the bin.§13
loc.stashOverwrittenVersion

Given a FRESH id and a '(overwritten)' name, so restoring it becomes its own canvas rather than fighting the live one for the same id. `doc` may be a document or its JSON.

  • No caller in the app; only the tests call it. The session keeps a store it is about to pull over with `stashCanvasStore` (the whole store, op log included) and a conflict's copy with `forkCanvas`.
purgeTrashEntry(id)Deletes a binned canvas for good.§13
loc.purgeTrashEntry

Bin row, stored document, thumbnails and, for a whole-store row (`store`), the store's records unless the gallery lists that id again (`isIndexed`); nothing local keeps a copy. The module's other outright deletes are `removeCanvas`, the bin's expiry in `readTrash` and `sweepStorage`'s removal of empty unlisted documents.

duplicateCanvas(id, fallbackDoc, fallbackName)Copies a canvas to a new id and gallery row named '<name> copy': a kobin-2 canvas through `forkCanvas`, anything else written whole from its kobin-1 document.§13
loc.duplicateCanvas

A kobin-2 canvas is copied record for record (`forkCanvas`: op log, undo history and cover thumbnail kept, no cloud lineage); null when the copy fails. A v1 canvas's document is `loadCanvasDoc`'s, written by `saveCanvasDoc` as a fresh store with no undo history, and its cover thumbnail is carried across.

  • Takes a fallback document, or its JSON, for a cloud-only canvas whose data was fetched separately (the gallery's `cloudLoadCanvas`).
migrateLegacyAutosave()Adopts the pre-multi-canvas drawing into the gallery, once.§13
loc.migrateLegacyAutosave

The pre-multi-canvas app kept one drawing in `kobinAutosave`. On the first gallery visit a drawing with strokes is written as a canvas (`saveCanvasDoc`) with its own index row; an empty one is not.

  • The legacy key is left in place as a safety net; nothing else reads it. A flag stops the migration running twice, and is not set when the write fails, so the next visit retries.
loadThumbs(canvasId, sceneIds)The stored thumbnails for a set of scenes.§13
loc.loadThumbs

Missing ones are simply absent rather than an error; the caller regenerates what it did not get.

saveThumbs(canvasId, map)Stores thumbnails, quota permitting.§13
loc.saveThumbs

One transaction through `db.putThumbs`, which also trims the store to its LRU budget: a failure loses the batch, and is swallowed because thumbnails are derived data, made again next time.

loadCoverThumb(canvasId)The gallery card's image.§13
loc.loadCoverThumb

The primary scene's thumbnail, aliased under a 'cover' key so the gallery does not have to know which scene is primary.

migrateStorage()Runs the one-time move out of localStorage with this module's `docToRecord`; safe to call on every gallery load.§13
loc.migrateStorage

Runs the one-time move out of localStorage with this module's `docToRecord`; safe to call on every gallery load.

sweepStorage()The gallery's housekeeping: adopts or deletes unlisted documents, then drops orphaned records, old backups, unreachable bin payloads and unlisted thumbnails.§13
loc.sweepStorage

A stored canvas that neither the gallery index nor the bin lists is adopted into the index when its header counts strokes (a crash or a killed tab kept it from being filed) and deleted when it counts none. Then: orphaned frame and log records, backups over a week old, bin payloads with no bin row, thumbnails of canvases in neither list, and the LRU budget. Expired bin entries go on the way past (`readTrash`).

  • Returns the counts, for the console and the tests. The gallery runs it after the migration and before the legacy-autosave adoption.
storageUsage()'Using 12 MB of browser storage', with the browser's usage and quota, or null where it will not say.
loc.storageUsage

'Using 12 MB of browser storage', with the browser's usage and quota, or null where it will not say.

formatMB(bytes)A byte count as MB or GB for the storage line, 'under 0.1 MB' below that.
loc.formatMB

A byte count as MB or GB for the storage line, 'under 0.1 MB' below that.

agoLabel(verb, iso, fallback)'Edited 3 hours ago'.§13
loc.agoLabel

One implementation for both the edited and the deleted labels, so they cannot phrase the same interval differently.

editedLabel(savedAt)When a canvas was last edited.§13
loc.editedLabel

When a canvas was last edited.

deletedLabel(deletedAt)When a canvas was binned.§13
loc.deletedLabel

When a canvas was binned.

depthLabel(levels)'3 levels deep', for the gallery badge.§13
loc.depthLabel

The one place the engine's level count is turned into something a reader is meant to feel rather than measure.

cloudPushSource(id, writer)What the cloud push reads from the local store: the stored header, `read` for what the cloud lacks, a setter for the sync bookkeeping, and `alive`.§13
loc.cloudPushSource

`read(cloudFrameSeq, fromSeq)` goes to `readPushState`, one transaction, so the header, frames and entries agree; `setSync` goes to `setSyncState` under the given `writer`. The editor's hook passes the tab's token; the gallery's catch-up passes none, so its bookkeeping is never fenced.

  • `alive()` reads the header again and is false once another tab's token holds the store (always true without a writer); the push checks it before each part and stops, leaving its parts pending for a later push to sweep.
  • Null for a canvas not yet in the kobin-2 store, which the gallery's catch-up then pushes as its kobin-1 document.
getStoreHeader(id)A canvas's stored header (listing fields, seqs, sync fields), or null; never throws.§13
loc.getStoreHeader

The session reads the local `base` from it at open (SYNC-PLAN R4).

setSyncState(id, patch, writer)Patches a stored canvas's sync fields without touching its frames; `addPending` and `dropPending` edit the pending chunk list in the same transaction.§13
loc.setSyncState

The rest of `patch` is spread over the header. `addPending` adds chunks not already listed and `dropPending` removes the named ones, inside the transaction, so two patches at once both land. Resolves true, false for no canvas, or 'fenced' when `writer` is given and another tab holds the store.

claimStore(id, token)Stamps a tab's writer token on a stored canvas's header, so from then on only that tab's writes land (SYNC-PLAN R2).§13
loc.claimStore

Unfenced, being the claim itself; `putCanvas2` and `patchCanvasHeader` then refuse any other token as 'fenced'. The session calls it at each lock grant with a fresh token (the tab id and the grant's generation), which the saver then writes under.

replaceCanvasStore(id, { ... }, writer)Writes a pulled kobin-2 canvas whole: its frames as the snapshots, its log replacing the local one.§13
loc.replaceCanvasStore

`full`, `resetLog` and `rewind`, with the frame set from the pulled header, under the given `writer`. Used by `applyPulledStore` for a full pull and by the dev panel's Copy real.

applyPulledStore(id, pulled, base, writer)Writes a cloud pull into the local store with `base` the cloud head it came from: whole for a full pull, else a fast-forward.§13
loc.applyPulledStore

A full pull goes through `replaceCanvasStore`, rewound. A fast-forward writes only the frames it downloaded and the entries past the local seq, with the cloud's frame set and header, and is not rewound, so `putCanvas2` refuses it as 'stale' if the stored seq is ahead. `intent` is cleared either way (SYNC-PLAN R4).

  • Resolves false for a fast-forward onto a canvas with no stored header, and 'fenced' when another tab holds the store. The session pulls in full after a refused fast-forward, and after 'fenced' or a refused full pull stops, blocked.
copyHeader(h, name)A copied canvas's header: the new name in the header and the meta, a fresh `savedAt`, no cloud lineage and no writer.§13
loc.copyHeader

Drops `base`, `intent`, `pending` and `writer`, so the copy is a canvas the cloud has never seen and no tab holds. Used by `forkCanvas` and `stashCanvasStore`.

stashCanvasStore(id, name)The bin's safety net for a store a pull is about to replace: the whole store copied to a new id named '<name> (overwritten)' and listed in the bin.§13
loc.stashCanvasStore

Through `binCopy`, so the copy keeps its op log and restores as it is. Returns the bin entry, or null when no copy landed, and then the pull does not happen (SYNC-PLAN R4).

  • The session calls it before pulling over a local copy of unknown ancestry, and before a newer lz1 cloud copy replaces this one.
binCopy(id, label, extra)Copies a stored canvas whole to a new id named `label` and lists it in the bin as a whole-store row (`store: true`), with `extra` on the row; the bin entry, or null when no copy landed.§13
loc.binCopy

Through `copyCanvas2Chunked` with `copyHeader` (one frame per transaction, the header last), so the copy keeps its op log and has no cloud lineage or writer; the row takes the header's stroke and level counts. A restore lists it again as it is; an expiry or purge deletes its records. Used by `stashCanvasStore` and `backupCanvasDoc`.

forkCanvas(id, name)A conflict's copy: every record of the stored canvas copied to a new id named `name`, without its cloud lineage, and listed in the gallery.§13
loc.forkCanvas

Through `copyCanvas2Chunked` with `copyHeader`: one frame per transaction and the header last, so a large copy does not hold up other writes. The copy keeps its op log and undo history, and has no `base`, `intent`, `pending` or `writer`: the cloud has never seen it. The cover thumbnail is copied too. Returns the new index entry, or null when no copy landed (SYNC-PLAN R5).

  • The session calls it when both this device and the cloud moved, before pulling the cloud's copy into this canvas; null blocks the pull.

storage/foldStore.js 50 lines

A stored or pulled kobin-2 canvas as one kobin-1 document: its frame snapshots, with the log entries they do not hold yet replayed through a detached engine (F86). The gallery's download, the v1 paths of the bin and backup, and `cloudLoadCanvas` read through it (DESIGN.md §13).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
logTail(entries, frameSeq)The log entries the frame snapshots do not hold yet: all but those whose every touched frame has a snapshot at or past the entry's seq.§13
fld.logTail

`OpLog.replay`'s rule inverted; an entry that touches no frame is always kept. `docFromStore` makes an engine only when it is non-empty.

plainRecords(objects, geo)A kobin-2 frame decoded to kobin-1 records whose loops are plain arrays.§13
fld.plainRecords

A decoded loop is a view into the frame's geometry buffer; a document bound for JSON, the bin or a backup must not carry one.

docFromStore(res)A stored or pulled kobin-2 canvas as ONE kobin-1 document: its frame snapshots, plus its log tail replayed through a detached engine; a v1 canvas's `legacy` as it is; null for nothing (F86).§13
fld.docFromStore

Without a log tail the frames are the document: decoded with plain arrays under the header's format, version, meta, camera and crossings, and no engine is made. With one, the frames go into a detached `KobinEngine` (1024 × 768, scenes off) loaded with `render: false`, since nothing is shown and a cold render is seconds (F87); `OpLog.replay` applies the entries past each frame's seq as the editor's restore does, and `serializeDrawing` is the result. The engine is destroyed either way.

  • A log that will not replay gives the snapshots alone, with a console warning: the download is the way out for such a canvas.
  • Takes `loadCanvasStore`'s result or `cloudPullCanvas2`'s. Callers: `loadCanvasDoc`, and `cloudLoadCanvas` for a kobin-2 cloud copy.

storage/thumbnails.js 153 lines

Scene thumbnails as 320×240 JPEG data URLs, cached by each scene's content hash: from the live raster engine's snapshots by default, or from a one-off SVG engine (`withSvgEngine`), which also makes the SVG export in raster mode (DESIGN.md §9).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
aspectRect(rect)Grows a scene rect to the thumbnail's shape.§13
thm.aspectRect

Centred, so the thumbnail shows the scene plus margin rather than a crop of it.

rasterize(svgEl)Turns the one-off SVG engine's `<svg>` into a 320×240 JPEG data URL.§13
thm.rasterize

Serialises the SVG, loads it as an image, draws it into a canvas over white.

  • Every failure path resolves to null rather than rejecting. A thumbnail is a nicety and must never be able to fail a save.
withSvgEngine(doc, w, h, fn)Runs `fn(engine, host)` on a one-off SVG engine over a copy of the document, off screen, and destroys it after.§9
thm.withSvgEngine

Always the SVG engine (raster off, scenes off, outlines built at once), because a thumbnail or an export is made by serialising its `<svg>` and the raster path's ink is on a canvas no serialiser sees (DESIGN.md §9). The document is deep-copied through JSON and loaded, so the camera is the file's.

  • Once `fn` settles the engine is destroyed (its renderer detaches the `<svg>` and clears its scene) and the host removed; what `fn` returns outlives them. Used by `renderThumbs` and by the SVG export in raster mode.
renderThumbsLive(engine, scenes, existing, opts)Scene thumbnails from the live raster engine: one `snapshotView` per scene whose hash changed, a few at a time, each landing as it is made.§14
thm.renderThumbsLive

Scenes whose stored hash still matches are skipped. Up to `opts.limit` lanes (4) run; each job waits for an idle callback, snapshots the scene's rect at 320×240 and encodes it with `scaleToDataUrl`. `opts.onThumb` fires per thumbnail so the panel fills progressively; `opts.signal` stops what has not started.

  • Returns `{ out, missed }`: a scene the engine could not snapshot (raster off, an unreachable frame, no canvas context) is in `missed`. The editor renders those with `renderThumbs` only when raster is off; with raster on a miss keeps the scene's last picture.
  • A cold frame's tile bake still runs inside `snapshotView` on the main thread (F59); the idle spacing keeps the panel responsive between jobs.
scaleToDataUrl(bitmap, w, h)Copies the top-left `w`×`h` of a snapshot bitmap onto white and encodes it as a JPEG data URL; null without a 2D context.
thm.scaleToDataUrl

The top-left is where `fitView` put the scene's rect in the plate (P3).

renderThumbs(doc, scenes, existing)Renders thumbnails for the scenes whose content changed.§13
thm.renderThumbs

It builds a WHOLE SECOND ENGINE (`withSvgEngine`, the SVG one), loads the drawing into it and jumps it to each scene in turn, rasterising each view.

  • The editor calls it only with raster off (`?svg`); on the raster default thumbnails come from the live engine (`renderThumbsLive`), because a second engine on the Magnum Opus drawing is an out-of-memory reload.
  • Only scenes whose content hash has changed are re-rendered. Returns only the new entries.

cloud/canvasSession.js 883 lines

One open editor's part in one editor at a time: the device lock (Web Locks, or storageLocks.js without them) and the cloud lease decide which tab edits, and the others are read-only and follow the holder. Each grant claims the local store with a writer token, so a tab that lost the lock cannot write. It reconciles versions at open and whenever the pen changes hands, pushes, hands the pen over on request, and keeps work that cannot be written as a new canvas (DESIGN.md §13).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
editorFromHook(get)Adapts the editor hook's API to the session's `editor` interface, reading the hook afresh on every call.§13
css.editorFromHook

`get()` returns the hook's latest object, a new one each render. The methods map to the hook's `setReadOnly`, `setSaving`, `setWriter`, `flushSave`, `idle`, `reloadFromStore`, `refreshMetaFromStore` (as `refreshMeta`), `hasUnsaved`, `keepUnsaved`, `knownSeq`, `cloudPushSource` and `stats`, each a no-op or a resolved default when the hook lacks it.

withTimeout(p, ms, why)Rejects with a `Timeout` error after `ms` unless the promise (or plain value) settles first; the work itself runs on.
css.withTimeout

Rejects with a `Timeout` error after `ms` unless the promise (or plain value) settles first; the work itself runs on.

perfNow()A millisecond clock for the session's perf log: `performance.now()`, or `Date.now()` where there is none.
css.perfNow

A millisecond clock for the session's perf log: `performance.now()`, or `Date.now()` where there is none.

who(s)The session's identity as a lease holder: device id, tab id and the device's display name.§13
css.who

The session's identity as a lease holder: device id, tab id and the device's display name.

shownName(entry, local)A canvas's name for notices and kept copies: the gallery's, then the stored header's, never the engine's default "untitled".§13
css.shownName

A canvas's name for notices and kept copies: the gallery's, then the stored header's, never the engine's default "untitled".

isNetwork(err)Whether an error means the cloud is out of reach (a timeout, unavailable, offline, a failed fetch) rather than something wrong.§13
css.isNetwork

An open or a catch-up that fails this way goes on editing offline and retries; any other failure blocks it (`_blocked`).

CanvasSessionOne open editor's part in one editor at a time: holds or follows the device lock and the cloud lease, reconciles versions, pushes.§13
css.CanvasSession

On the device the pen is the lock `boundless:canvas:<id>` (Web Locks, or `storageLocks.js` without them); in the cloud it is the manifest's lease. A tab or device without it is read-only and follows the holder: a same-device tab reloads the store when the holder posts "saved" (only the header when the write moved no data), another device pulls when the manifest's head moves (DESIGN.md §13).

  • The fence. Every grant bumps a generation and claims the local store with a writer token (`claimStore`); every store write carries the token and is refused once another tab has claimed; every flow checks its generation after each `await` (`_live`); a lost lock is dropped synchronously (`_drop`). The saver stays off from the grant until `_edit`.
  • Work that cannot be written here is kept as a new canvas (`_keepUnsaved`); a local copy that cannot be kept blocks the pull that would replace it. `CanvasEditor` creates the session once the document is restored and sign-in has resolved; `env` injects `locks`, `Channel`, `now` and `visible` for the two-tab and two-device tests.
CanvasSession.constructor(opts)Stores the canvas, device and tab ids, the editor adapter and the environment, and starts in mode `starting` at generation 0.§13
css.CanvasSession.constructor

`env.locks` defaults to `navigator.locks`, else `makeStorageLocks()` over localStorage. `opts` overrides `SESSION_DEFAULTS`: beat 20 s, lease 90 s, skew margin 5 min, background push 30 s, "Edit here" forced after 6 min, tab steal after 5 s, open timeout 4 s, open retry 20 s doubling to 10 min, push deadline 5 min (also the push lane's no-progress limit), a follow at most every 2 s or ten times the last reload. It also sets up the follow bookkeeping: whether a same-device write moved data since the last reload, and a follow asked for while one runs.

start()Opens the channel and asks for the device lock without waiting: with it the tab holds the device, without it follows.§13
css.start

Opens the channel and asks for the device lock without waiting: with it the tab holds the device, without it follows.

stop()Leaving the editor: a last flush while the tab still holds the store, a last push, the lease let go, then the device lock.§13
css.stop

In order: an editing (or handing-over) lock holder flushes (10 s at most) and keeps the document as a new canvas if the flush reports failure; timers, the manifest watch and a queued lock request are cleared; the last push runs for dirty edits (never for a discarded canvas) and the lease is released after it, which `stop` does not wait for; the hook's whole write chain is awaited (`idle`, 10 s at most); the lock is let go.

  • The lock goes last because a new holder reading the store earlier would continue the log at seqs the old holder's last write then overwrites.
markDirty()Notes that the document changed, so the cloud copy is behind.§13
css.markDirty

Notes that the document changed, so the cloud copy is behind.

onLocalSaved(seq, opts)The saver wrote the store: marks the cloud behind and posts "saved" so same-device read-only tabs follow.§13
css.onLocalSaved

`data: false` (a camera, a name) tells the followers to read only the header rather than reload the drawing.

onRefused(kind)The saver's write was refused: the work in memory is kept as a new canvas, then the tab follows or reloads.§13
css.onRefused

`fenced` (another tab has claimed the store): after keeping the work, a tab that still thinks it holds the lock drops it (`_lockLost`) and follows. `stale` (the store is ahead of this document): the saver goes off, the store is reloaded keeping the camera, and the saver comes back on if the tab is still editing.

onVisibility(visible)Tab shown: runs a follow owed while hidden and beats at once. Tab hidden: pushes an editing tab's unpushed edits.§13
css.onVisibility

Tab shown: runs a follow owed while hidden and beats at once. Tab hidden: pushes an editing tab's unpushed edits.

pushNow(opts)An explicit Save: a forced push with the thumbnails; refused signed out, read-only, or with a push in flight.§13
css.pushNow

Returns `{ ok: false }` with `local`, `readOnly` or `busy` in those cases. Forced, it ignores the failure backoff.

takeOver()"Edit here": asks whoever has the pen to save and let go, and takes it anyway after a wait.§13
css.takeOver

Refused while starting, editing or already taking; clears the chip's error. A tab follower posts `want` on the channel and steals the lock after 5 s of silence. A device follower calls `cloudAskLease`: a free lease is taken at once and the session promoted; otherwise it waits in mode `taking`, watching the manifest, while the holder keeps renewing as it saves, pushes and lets go to it.

  • The wait ends when `_maybeTake` sees the lease let go to this device, or unchanged for a TTL (a holder gone silent; the beat polls the manifest for that), or with a forced take after 6 min. A failure to reach the cloud leaves it read-only with an error.
_openChannel()Opens the BroadcastChannel named after the lock: the same-device tabs' line for "want", "saved" and "released".§13
css._openChannel

Opens the BroadcastChannel named after the lock: the same-device tabs' line for "want", "saved" and "released".

_post(msg)Posts a message on the channel stamped with this tab's id; nothing when there is no channel.§13
css._post

Posts a message on the channel stamped with this tab's id; nothing when there is no channel.

_onMessage(msg)Answers another tab: "want" makes the lock holder hand over at once; "saved" schedules a follower's `_reloadFollow`.§13
css._onMessage

A "saved" that moved data marks a whole reload owed until one runs, whatever header-only writes come after. The hand-over does not wait behind the serial chain.

_requestLock({ ... })Requests the device lock: now or not at all, queued until the holder lets go, or stolen; resolves whether it was granted.§13
css._requestLock

Each request has an id; a queued one also carries an AbortController and a `done` promise that settles `granted`, `none` or `aborted`. A granted lock is held by a promise `_letGoOfLock` resolves. A grant that lands after `stop()`, or while this tab already holds the lock through another request, is let go at once (seen in Chrome after a Fast Refresh).

  • When the held request rejects, the lock was stolen: `_lockLost` runs at once, not behind the serial chain.
_drop()Drops the lock and everything that rode on it at once: generation bumped, token cleared, saver off, read-only, cloud work stopped.§13
css._drop

Synchronous, so a flow still inside an `await` finds its generation stale (`_live`) and stops, and nothing it does afterwards writes.

_letGoOfLock()Drops everything held on the lock, then releases it by resolving the promise that holds it.§13
css._letGoOfLock

Drops everything held on the lock, then releases it by resolving the promise that holds it.

_lockLost(why)The lock went to another tab (stolen, or the store fenced): everything dropped at once, a notice, unsaved work kept, then follow.§13
css._lockLost

Whether there is unsaved work is read before the drop; that work is kept as a new canvas before the tab becomes a follower.

_stealLock()Takes the device lock from a holder that did not answer "want" within 5 s, then holds the device.§13
css._stealLock

Aborts this tab's own queued request first and waits for its outcome: if that request was granted meanwhile, nothing is stolen. The tab it is taken from drops everything (`_lockLost`) and writes nothing more.

_tabFollower()A tab without the device lock: read-only, saver off, following the holder through the store, queued for the lock.§13
css._tabFollower

When the queued lock is granted (the holder closed or handed over) the tab holds the device, reloading the store first.

_live(g)Whether a flow started at generation `g` may go on: not stopped, still holding the lock, the generation unchanged.§13
css._live

Checked after every `await` in the flows that write.

_holdDevice({ ... })This tab holds the device lock: claims the store with a new token, catches up with it, then lets the cloud decide whether it edits.§13
css._holdDevice

Bumps the generation, sets the token `<tab>.<generation>` on the hook (`setWriter`) and on the stored header (`claimStore`), with the saver off and the editor read-only. Reloads from the store when the lock came from another tab or the stored seq differs from the editor's. Signed out it edits at once; signed in it starts the lease beat, the 30 s background push while dirty and the manifest watch, then `_openCloud`.

_handToTab()Another tab asked for the pen: read-only, flush, let go of the lock, post "released", follow.§13
css._handToTab

Runs at once, one at a time. A failed flush keeps the document as a new canvas first; a tab that lost the lock meanwhile stops there. The cloud lease is not released: it is this device's, and the device lock decides which of its tabs holds it.

_stopCloud()Clears the session's timers and the manifest watch, and forgets a scheduled follow whose timer went with them.§13
css._stopCloud

Clears the session's timers and the manifest watch, and forgets a scheduled follow whose timer went with them.

_openCloud(g)At open: reads the manifest, takes the lease if it can, reconciles versions, then edits or follows another device.§13
css._openCloud

The manifest read has 4 s; any failure of it counts as offline, and the tab edits with `needOpen` set so a later beat reopens. With no kobin-2 copy (none, or an lz1 one) it mints `createLease`, which the first push writes. A lease taken by a flow that went stale meanwhile is released again.

  • Any other failure, or a reconcile that could not keep the local copy, blocks the open (`_blocked`). A live lease on another device leaves the tab read-only after reconciling, naming the holder.
_blocked(message)The cloud open cannot finish (an error, or a local copy that could not be kept): read-only, saver off, shown, retried.§13
css._blocked

Sets `needOpen` and the next try 20 s later, doubling per failure up to 10 min; the beat reopens then.

_reconcile(g, opts)Compares the local base with the cloud head through `decideOpen` and acts; answers `ok`, `blocked` or `gone`.§13
css._reconcile

A base `decideOpen` recovers is written to the local header first, under the token. `push` only marks the session dirty; `pull` is incremental unless `full`; `stash` and `conflict` keep the local store (`_keepStore`) and then pull the cloud's whole, and are `blocked` when it could not be kept; `legacy` takes the lz1 path. The camera is kept except at open.

_pull(g, { ... })Downloads the cloud head into the local store and reloads the editor from it; incremental unless `full`.§13
css._pull

An incremental pull passes the local frame seqs and seq as `have`; a refused incremental apply is repeated whole, and a fenced store or a refused whole apply blocks. Records the cloud head as the new `base`, saves the thumbnails, updates the gallery row (the cloud's name unless it is "untitled"), reloads, and posts "saved" so same-device tabs follow.

_keepStore(g, kind, local)Before a pull replaces the local store, keeps it whole: in the recycle bin (`stash`) or as a new canvas (`conflict`).§13
css._keepStore

Flushes first (a failed flush keeps the document in memory as a new canvas). `stash` copies the store to "<name> (overwritten)" in the bin; `conflict` forks it as "<name> — edits from <device>, <date>" without its cloud lineage. Answers true, false when nothing landed (the open is blocked and the pull must not happen), or `gone`.

_pullLz1(g, local, m)An lz1 cloud copy: the newer of it and the local copy wins by `savedAt`, and the other is kept as a canvas of its own.§13
css._pullLz1

Local newer: the older cloud copy, if it has strokes, is kept as "<name> — the older cloud copy, <date>", and the session is marked dirty so the first push replaces the lz1 copy. Cloud newer: an empty cloud copy never replaces a local one; otherwise the local store goes to the recycle bin (`_keepStore`), then the lz1 drawing is written with its gallery name and the editor reloaded without keeping the camera. A copy that could not be kept blocks.

_keepUnsaved()The document in memory as a new canvas, "<name> — unsaved edits from <device>, <date>", when it could not be written here.§13
css._keepUnsaved

Nothing when there is nothing unsaved. When even that copy fails, the notice points at downloading from the ⋮ menu. Returns the new index entry or null.

_edit(g)Lets the tab edit: saver on, read-only off, mode `editing`, with the chip's cloud state; nothing for a stale generation.§13
css._edit

The cloud state is `off` signed out, `offline` while the open is owed (its error kept), `local` for a canvas not yet in the gallery, otherwise `saving` or `saved`.

discard()The canvas was deleted: nothing more goes up, not even the last push on leaving.§13
css.discard

The canvas was deleted: nothing more goes up, not even the last push on leaving.

_readOnlyDevice(holder)Another device has the pen: read-only, saver off, the epoch dropped, the chip naming the holder.§13
css._readOnlyDevice

Another device has the pen: read-only, saver off, the epoch dropped, the chip naming the holder.

_offline(err)Marks the cloud unreachable on the chip, with the error's first 120 characters.§13
css._offline

Marks the cloud unreachable on the chip, with the error's first 120 characters.

_beat()The visible lock holder's periodic cloud step: watch an asked-for lease, reopen, follow, or renew the lease and answer a `want`.§13
css._beat

Runs every 20 s and when the tab is shown; skipped hidden, signed out or without the lock. While "Edit here" waits it reads the manifest for `_maybeTake`. An owed open waits for its retry time, flushes an editing tab (keeping unsaved work if that fails) and reopens. A read-only device schedules a follow. An editor renews: a refusal means the pen was taken (`_lose`), a vanished copy mints a new `createLease`, a renewal clears the offline state, and another device's `want` starts `_handToDevice`.

_watch()Subscribes to the manifest once, sending each change to `_onManifest`.§13
css._watch

Subscribes to the manifest once, sending each change to `_onManifest`.

_onManifest(m)Reacts to a manifest change: the editor loses the pen or hands it over; a read-only device may take it, or follows the new head.§13
css._onManifest

Only the lock holder listens. Editing, a lease with another epoch means the pen was taken (`_lose`), and another device's `want` on a live lease starts the hand-over at once. A device follower (not mid-hand-over) tries `_maybeTake`, updates the holder's name, and schedules a follow when the head moved.

_maybeTake(L)A visible device follower takes the pen unasked when `leaseState` calls the lease free, or it sat unchanged for a TTL of this device's clock.§13

Free covers a lease let go to this device or to nobody, and one past `until` by the skew margin. The TTL is timed from when this device first saw that epoch, `until` and `to`, so a skewed clock elsewhere cannot make a live lease look dead; a lease let go to another device is taken after a TTL too.

_lose(holder)The pen was taken (a refused push, a beat or the manifest said so): read-only, flush locally, a notice, follow the cloud.§13
css._lose

A failed flush keeps the document as a new canvas. Unpushed edits stay in the local store; once the new holder's head moves, the follow's reconcile keeps them as a conflict copy (DESIGN.md §13).

_handToDevice(want)Another device asked for the pen: flush, push what is left, let go of the lease to the asker, follow.§13
css._handToDevice

One at a time. A failed flush keeps the document as a new canvas; the saver goes off; a push in flight is awaited, then what is still dirty is pushed (forced) and awaited. The beat keeps renewing meanwhile, so the asker waits. The release names the asker (`to`), which reserves the pen for it.

_takeLease(force, ifLease)Takes the cloud lease (forced after "Edit here" has waited 6 min, or `ifLease` for a watched stale one) and promotes the session.§13
css._takeLease

One take at a time; the promote runs on the serial chain; a failure marks the cloud offline.

_promote()The pen taken from another device: reconciles to catch up with what it left, then edits and watches the manifest.§13
css._promote

Saver off and read-only until the reconcile answers `ok`. A network failure edits offline with the open owed; any other failure blocks.

_followCloud()A read-only device catches up: reads the manifest, reconciles (pulling the new head), and checks whether it may take the pen.§13
css._followCloud

The take is considered only after a reconcile that answered `ok`.

_reloadFollow()A read-only tab catches up with what the holder saved: the whole store when data moved, otherwise the header alone.§13
css._reloadFollow

A whole reload keeps the camera; one that throws leaves the reload owed for the next follow. Answers false when nothing was reloaded. The code records the reason: a whole reload is 5-7 s of main thread on the Magnum Opus (measured 2026-09-23).

_scheduleFollow(fn)Runs a follow while visible, at most every 2 s or ten times the last reload's cost, whichever is longer.§13
css._scheduleFollow

A hidden tab owes the latest follow until it is shown. One follow is pending at a time, run on the serial chain; one asked for while a follow runs waits and is scheduled when that one ends, gap included. The gap is timed from the end of the last follow, except one that answers false (a header-only refresh).

_push({ ... })One push at a time of the local store to the cloud, with the failure backoff and the refused-push path.§13
css._push

Refused signed out, while a push is in flight, when not editing or handing over, and in backoff unless forced. A canvas not in the gallery index stays local; one not in the kobin-2 store is skipped. Otherwise it clears `dirty` and calls `cloudPushCanvas2` with the held epoch (or `createLease` when the push creates the copy), passing its 5 min deadline as the lane's limit.

  • The deadline runs from when the push leaves the page's push lane, not while it queues, and only reports the failure: `busy` settles when the push itself settles, so a timed-out push is never doubled. A push that lands, even after its deadline was reported, makes the created copy's lease this tab's and records the head, or the next push would read its own lease as another's.
  • `SyncConflict` or `LeaseLost` gives up the pen (`_lose`); any other failure keeps the edits dirty and backs off 1, 2, 4 ... min up to 30 min, shown on the chip.
_set(patch)Merges a patch into the session state and reports it to the UI.
css._set

Merges a patch into the session state and reports it to the UI.

_serial(fn)Runs losses, promotions and follows one at a time on a promise chain; skipped after stop.
css._serial

Hand-overs and a stolen lock do not wait here. A failure does not break the chain.

_after(ms, fn)A tracked timeout, cleared with the session's timers and skipped after stop.
css._after

A tracked timeout, cleared with the session's timers and skipped after stop.

_every(ms, fn)A tracked interval, cleared with the session's timers and skipped after stop.
