cloud/syncCore.js 136 lines

The pure rules of one canvas on several tabs and devices: the head `{ epoch, seq }`, the lease's state, and the open decision, which compares versions, not clocks. No Firestore, no IndexedDB (DESIGN.md §13).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
newEpoch()A fresh epoch id: five base-36 digits of the clock and five random ones, safe in a Firestore document id.§13
syn.newEpoch

Minted for every lease take and as a tab's id; a manifest from before versions reads as epoch 0.

headOf(manifest)A cloud manifest's head `{ epoch, seq }`; one from before versions reads as epoch 0 at its seq.§13
syn.headOf

A cloud manifest's head `{ epoch, seq }`; one from before versions reads as epoch 0 at its seq.

sameHead(a, b)Whether two heads name the same point of history: both present, the same epoch and the same seq.§13
syn.sameHead

Epochs compare as strings.

leaseState(lease, { ... })Who may take the pen unasked, from a manifest's lease at `now` on this device's clock: `{ free, mine, holder }`.§13
syn.leaseState

A lease let go (`until` 0) is free, unless it was let go `to` another device: then it answers `reserved` to every device but that one, the device that let it go included. Otherwise free: no lease; this device's own live lease (the device lock arbitrates its tabs, so another tab's lease here is ours to take); another device's live lease only `skewMs` (`LEASE_SKEW_MS`, 5 min) past its `until`.

  • `until` is the holder's clock, so the margin keeps a clock running ahead from taking a live lease. A follower that watched a lease sit unchanged for a TTL of its own clock takes it sooner (`CanvasSession._maybeTake`).
chunkNames(m)The set of chunk ids a manifest names, frame snapshots and log runs, for `intentLanded`.§13
syn.chunkNames

The set of chunk ids a manifest names, frame snapshots and log runs, for `intentLanded`.

intentLanded(intent, manifest, col)Whether a push this device recorded as its `intent` landed, though its tab closed before recording it.§13
syn.intentLanded

True when the intent is for this collection and the cloud head is the intent's, or the manifest still names one of the intent's chunks (another device has pushed on top since). The recovered base is the intent's head, at the next push (`cloudPushCanvas2`) and at the next open (`decideOpen`).

decideOpen({ ... })The open decision: compares the local base with the cloud head and answers none, legacy, sync, push, pull, stash or conflict.§13
syn.decideOpen

Versions, never clocks: local ops past the base with the head unmoved is a fast-forward push, the head moved with nothing unpushed a fast-forward pull, both a conflict. A base from another collection counts as none; a local `intent` that landed (`intentLanded`: a push whose manifest was written after its tab closed) is the base.

  • With no base: an empty local copy pulls whole; a legacy manifest this device pushed, or the same frames at the same seqs (`sameFrames`), gives one. Otherwise the ancestry is unknown and `savedAt` decides, the one time a clock does: the cloud newer (or a local copy not in the kobin-2 store) is `stash`, this copy newer is `conflict`. Both keep both copies (DESIGN.md §13).
sameFrames(local, cloud)Whether a local copy holds exactly the manifest's frames at the same snapshot seqs: a copy pulled from it.§13
syn.sameFrames

Whether a local copy holds exactly the manifest's frames at the same snapshot seqs: a copy pulled from it.

conflictName(name, deviceName, at)The name of a conflict's copy: "<name> — edits from <device>, <month day>".§13
syn.conflictName

The name of a conflict's copy: "<name> — edits from <device>, <month day>".

defaultDeviceName(ua)The default device name other devices see: "<browser> on <OS>", read from the user agent.§13
syn.defaultDeviceName

Used until the device is named from the sync chip (`localStorage["kobin.deviceName"]`).

cloud/storageLocks.js 70 lines

A stand-in for the part of `navigator.locks` the session uses, over localStorage, for a browser without Web Locks (the dev server reached over http by LAN address, Safari before 15.4): the last writer of a lock key holds it, renewed every second, and a key left unrenewed for 10 s is free.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
abortError()An Error named `AbortError`, as Web Locks rejects an aborted or stolen request.
slk.abortError

An Error named `AbortError`, as Web Locks rejects an aborted or stolen request.

sleep(ms)A promise that resolves after `ms`.
slk.sleep

A promise that resolves after `ms`.

makeStorageLocks(opts)The part of `navigator.locks` the session uses (exclusive; `ifAvailable`, `steal`, `signal`) over localStorage, for a browser without Web Locks.§13
slk.makeStorageLocks

A lock is the key `boundless.lock.<name>` holding `{ owner, at }`, renewed every heartbeat (1 s) while held; a key not renewed for 10 s is free (a closed tab). With no compare-and-set, a taker writes its owner, waits 60 ms and reads it back: the last writer holds it, the others poll every 250 ms. A holder that finds another owner in its key rejects with `AbortError` (stolen).

  • `ifAvailable` calls back with null when the lock is taken; `steal` writes over the holder; an abort before the grant rejects. The lock is held until the callback's promise settles, then its key is removed if still its own.

cloud/canvasSync.js 638 lines

Firestore persistence for canvases: the kobin-2 mirror (gzipped frame and log chunks, then the manifest in a transaction that checks the head and the lease), pushed one at a time per page through one push lane; the lease transactions, the gallery's listing, trash and rename, and the old lz1 copy. A development build uses `dev-canvases`, never the deployed app's `canvases` (DESIGN.md §13).

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
isDevBuild(env, host)Whether this is a development build, which reads and writes `dev-canvases` instead of the deployed app's `canvases`.§13
cld.isDevBuild

Real only for a `production` build served from the deployed app's own hosts (`REAL_HOSTS`: bound-less-kk.web.app, bound-less-kk.firebaseapp.com); every other build or host (the dev server, a test, localhost, a LAN address, a Hosting preview channel) is development. Evaluated once at load to fix `CANVAS_COLLECTION`, which every manifest, part and collection builder uses (DESIGN.md §13).

  • The dev server and the deployed app share one Firebase project, so this is what keeps a development build out of the real collection. The gallery skips its bulk catch-up when it is true, and the editor's dev panel offers Copy real.
canvasesCol(uid)The user's canvas collection for this build: `canvases`, or `dev-canvases` in a development build.§13
cld.canvasesCol

Every path is built from the signed-in uid, which is what the security rules match on: a user owns exactly their own subtree and nothing is public.

  • The collection is `CANVAS_COLLECTION`, fixed at load by `isDevBuild`: the dev server and the deployed app share one Firebase project, and a development build never writes the real collection (DESIGN.md §13).

cld.canvasDoc

One canvas's parent record.

partDoc(uid, id, i)One numbered part of a canvas's old lz1 copy (`parts/<i>`).§13
cld.partDoc

-

cld.realCanvasDoc

The one manifest builder that names `canvases` whatever the build. Only `cloudPullCanvas2` with `real` reads through it; nothing writes through it (DESIGN.md §13).

realPartDoc2(uid, id, chunkId, i)One kobin-2 chunk part in the REAL collection, read by Copy real in a development build.§13
cld.realPartDoc2

One kobin-2 chunk part in the REAL collection, read by Copy real in a development build.

chunk(u8)Cuts lz1-compressed bytes into 700 KiB parts for the old lz1 copy, always at least one.§13
cld.chunk

Returns `{ codec: "lz1", chunks }`, each chunk a `subarray` view of the input: the shared tail of `encodeCanvasPayload` and `encodeCanvasPayloadAsync`.

encodeCanvasPayload(json)Compresses a document and splits it into chunks.§13
cld.encodeCanvasPayload

A Firestore document caps at one mebibyte, so the drawing cannot live on the parent. It is compressed to bytes and cut into 700 KiB parts.

  • Pure, and unit-tested without Firestore - which is why the chunking has its own test file rather than being reachable only through the network.
encodeCanvasPayloadAsync(json)The lz1 encoder with the lz-string compression in a worker where one loads; what `saveCanvasLz1` writes.§13
cld.encodeCanvasPayloadAsync

Compresses through `lzWorker.compressToUint8Array`, then cuts with `chunk`. The code records the reason: on the phone the compressor was 97% of a multi-second save freeze (F33).

  • A job the worker ran and failed is not retried on the main thread (OPEN-FLAGS F64); only a missing worker falls back.
decodeCanvasPayload(parts, codec)Reassembles chunks into a document.§13
cld.decodeCanvasPayload

Legacy string parts still decode. The codec is read from the parent record rather than guessed, so an old canvas and a new one are told apart by data rather than by sniffing.

decodeCanvasPayloadAsync(parts, codec)Turns an lz1 copy's parts back into kobin-1 JSON, decompressing in the worker; legacy string parts are joined as text.§13
cld.decodeCanvasPayloadAsync

`codec` comes from the parent doc: `lz1` joins the byte parts and decompresses them through `lzWorker`; anything else takes the parts as plain strings, a non-string part reading as empty. `cloudLoadCanvas` calls it.

boundedThumbs(thumbs)Caps the thumbnails that ride on the parent record.§13
cld.boundedThumbs

They share the parent's one-mebibyte limit with the metadata, so the cover goes first and the rest fill the remaining budget in insertion order.

  • Without the cap a canvas with many scenes would silently fail to save at all.
perfNow()A millisecond clock for the save timings: `performance.now()`, or `Date.now()` where there is none.

A millisecond clock for the save timings: `performance.now()`, or `Date.now()` where there is none.

Queues `saveCanvasLz1` in `inLane` with the lane's deadline (`laneMs`), so it never runs beside a kobin-2 push. Its one caller is the production gallery's catch-up, for a local canvas the account does not know and that is not in the kobin-2 store; the first kobin-2 push replaces the lz1 copy (DESIGN.md §13).

saveCanvasLz1(uid, entry, json, thumbs, run)The lz1 whole-copy write: lz-string parts one a commit, then the parent in a transaction that refuses a kobin-2 copy.§13
cld.saveCanvasLz1

Parts first, the parent LAST. Readers key off the parent's part count and codec, so a torn save never looks complete: it looks like the previous save. `SyncConflict` when the copy is kobin-2, checked before the parts go up and again in the parent's transaction, which also deletes parts beyond the new count. The thumbnails are merged over the stored set within the parent's budget.

  • Each part commit marks progress on its lane run (`run.tick`); once the lane has let it go past its deadline it throws `PushDead` and writes nothing more.

cld.cloudListCanvases

Metadata only - listing the gallery downloads no drawings, which is the whole reason metadata lives on the parent.

  • Deleted canvases are included on purpose. A device that filtered them out would re-upload a canvas deleted elsewhere, because to that device it would look like a canvas the account had never seen.
cloudGetCanvasMeta(uid, id)One canvas's metadata, one read.§13
cld.cloudGetCanvasMeta

The manifest (or an lz1 copy's parent) alone, no drawing. The session reads it at open (with a 4 s timeout), to reconcile, when a read-only device follows, and each beat while "Edit here" waits: the head and lease `decideOpen` and `_maybeTake` compare.

cloudLoadCanvas(uid, id)A cloud canvas's drawing as kobin-1 JSON, with its thumbnails and metadata: an lz1 copy's parts decoded, a kobin-2 copy pulled whole and folded.§13

A kobin-2 manifest goes through `cloudPullCanvas2` and `docFromStore`, so edits only in the log are in the result; null when the pull finds nothing. An lz1 copy's parts are read in parallel and decoded in the lz worker. The parent's name outranks the one embedded in the drawing, because a gallery rename only touches the parent.

cloudTrashCanvas(uid, id)Soft-deletes: a tombstone on the parent.§13
cld.cloudTrashCanvas

The parts are left in place, so restoring is a one-field write and no data moves.

cloudRestoreCanvas(uid, id)Clears the tombstone.§13
cld.cloudRestoreCanvas

A full save clears it too, which means editing a canvas anywhere resurrects it - the behaviour a person expects without being told.

cloudRenameCanvas(uid, id, name, savedAt)Renames without re-uploading the drawing.§13
cld.cloudRenameCanvas

A parent-only merge. The timestamp is passed in so it matches the local index bump exactly, which keeps freshest-wins comparisons symmetric between the two stores.

cloudDeleteCanvas(uid, id)Permanent deletion, parts and all.§13
cld.cloudDeleteCanvas

Deletes every part (each chunk's parts for a kobin-2 manifest, the numbered parts for an lz1 copy) in commits of 400, then the parent last, so a failure part-way leaves the canvas listed in the bin, where the purge can be run again.

partDoc2(uid, id, chunkId, i)One part of a kobin-2 chunk: `parts/<chunkId>~<i>` under the canvas's manifest, in this build's collection.§13

`/` becomes `.`, `,` becomes `_`, and any other character outside `A-Za-z0-9_-` becomes `-`, so a frame id such as `0/3,-1#1` names a part document without a path separator.

cld.SyncConflict

Carries the cloud's `head`. `pushCanvas2` checks before any part is written and again inside the manifest's transaction, so a refused push has touched nothing a manifest names. `saveCanvasLz1` throws it rather than write an lz1 copy over a kobin-2 one.

SyncConflict.constructor(why, head)Names the error and keeps the cloud head it was refused against (null when none).§13
cld.SyncConflict.constructor

Names the error and keeps the cloud head it was refused against (null when none).

LeaseLostThe error a push throws when the manifest's lease is not the epoch this device holds: another device or tab has the pen.§13
cld.LeaseLost

Carries the lease it found (`holder`), which the session names on the chip when it goes read-only. `pushCanvas2` also throws it with no holder when the local store refuses the push's bookkeeping as another tab's (`"fenced"`), or when `source.alive()` says another tab claimed the store mid-push.

LeaseLost.constructor(holder)Names the error and keeps the lease that holds the pen (null when none).§13
cld.LeaseLost.constructor

Names the error and keeps the lease that holds the pen (null when none).

commitAll(items, per, fn, before)Applies one write per item in sequential batches of `per`, each committed before the next starts.§13
cld.commitAll

`before`, when given, runs ahead of each commit and may throw to stop the rest: the push uses it to mark lane progress and to stop once the store is another tab's or the lane has let it go.

  • Parts go up one a commit (`PARTS_PER_COMMIT`), deletes 400 a commit. Measured 2026-09-08 on the 12,849-object canvas: six parts a batch had Firestore's write stream answering `resource-exhausted` on every batch (DESIGN.md §13).
inLane(fn, opts)Runs a cloud write in the page's one push lane: one at a time, from any session or canvas, each queued behind the last.§13
cld.inLane

Firestore's write stream refuses overlapping uploads (DESIGN.md §13), and a session restarted mid-push (Fast Refresh, a remount) queues behind the old one. `fn(run)` gets a `run` whose `tick()` marks progress; after `ms` (5 min) without one the run is marked `dead` and the next write goes, so a slow push that keeps committing keeps the lane and a stuck one does not. `onStart` is called as the write leaves the queue. Resolves or rejects as `fn` does.

pushDead()The error (named `PushDead`) a push throws once the lane has let it go, so a commit that answers late writes nothing more.§13

The error (named `PushDead`) a push throws once the lane has let it go, so a commit that answers late writes nothing more.

cld.partsOf

The document reference of every part of the given chunks, for a batched delete.

cloudPushCanvas2(uid, entry, source, opts)Mirrors the local kobin-2 store into the cloud: queues `pushCanvas2` in the page's one push lane.§13
cld.cloudPushCanvas2

`opts.laneMs` is the lane's no-progress limit (5 min by default; the session passes its push deadline) and `opts.onStart` is called when the push leaves the queue; the other options go to `pushCanvas2`. Resolves or throws as it does. Callers: the session's `_push` and the production gallery's catch-up.

pushCanvas2(uid, entry, source, opts, run)One push of the local kobin-2 store: changed frames and new log entries as gzipped chunks, then the manifest in a checked transaction.§13
cld.pushCanvas2

In order: reads the manifest; reads from the local store, in one transaction (`source.read`), the header, the frames whose snapshot seq differs from the cloud's and the entries past the cloud's seq; checks the manifest (the cloud head must be the local `base`, else `SyncConflict`; the lease must be `epoch`, else `LeaseLost`; no copy or an lz1 copy is not checked); gzips each frame and the run of entries, one chunk each, split into 700 KiB parts; adds the chunks to `pending` and records the `intent`; writes the parts one a commit; writes the manifest in a transaction that repeats the check; records the new `base`; deletes the parts of the chunks it replaced, and an lz1 copy's parts, then drops them from `pending`.

  • A push never overwrites (DESIGN.md §13). Every chunk id is this push's alone, its epoch and a random nonce (`f_<frame>_<seq>_<epoch>_<nonce>`, `l_<from>_<to>_<epoch>_<nonce>`), so a refused push leaves only parts no manifest names, which the next push sweeps from `pending`. An intent that landed (`intentLanded`: a push whose manifest was written after its tab closed) counts as the base.
  • Before each part commit it ticks the lane and stops with `LeaseLost` when `source.alive()` says another tab claimed the store, or with `PushDead` once the lane has let it go; a store fenced at the bookkeeping step stops it before any part. A push let go after its manifest landed skips the deletes, leaving them pending for the next push's sweep.
  • The head is kept only when nothing went up and the seq has not moved (a rename, a camera); chunks uploaded at an unchanged seq get a head of their own (epoch `<epoch>.<nonce>`). The manifest keeps the cloud's lease; `lease` is written only when this push creates the copy or replaces an lz1 one. A transaction that throws re-reads the manifest: when its head is this push's the commit landed and the push goes on, otherwise it sweeps its parts and rethrows. Log chunks wholly below `dropBelow` (the saver's compaction floor) leave the manifest. The older source shape (`header`, `readFrames`, `readLog`) is still accepted.
sweep(uid, id, pending, manifest, setSync)Deletes a refused push's pending chunks that the current manifest does not name, and drops them from `pending`.§13
cld.sweep

The chunks the manifest names stay pending. A failed delete leaves every one in `pending` for the next push to try again.

cloudPullCanvas2(uid, id, opts)Reads the kobin-2 cloud copy in the local store's shape; with `have`, only the changed frames and the entries past its seq.§13
cld.cloudPullCanvas2

Reads the manifest (null when there is none or it is not kobin-2), then each frame chunk whose snapshot seq differs from `have.frameSeq`, then the log chunks in seq order, keeping the entries past `have.seq`. A chunk's parts are read in parallel, joined, decompressed by the manifest's codec (`gunzipAs`) and unpacked. Returns `{ header, frames, entries, head, full, thumbs, meta }`; `full` is true without `have`.

  • A missing part throws, naming it. `real` reads the real collection from a development build (Copy real); nothing is written there.
cloudLoadCanvas2(uid, id, opts)The whole kobin-2 cloud copy, every frame and entry: `cloudPullCanvas2` without a local copy.§13
cld.cloudLoadCanvas2

The dev panel's Copy real calls it with `real` to bring a canvas from the deployed app's collection in as a new local canvas.

leaseFor({ ... }, now, ttl)A new lease for a device and tab: a fresh epoch and an expiry `ttl` past this device's clock.§13
cld.leaseFor

Every take mints a new epoch; the holder's pushes name it, which is what tells two histories at the same seq apart (DESIGN.md §13).

cloudTakeLease(uid, id, who, opts)Takes the pen in a transaction when `leaseState` calls the lease free, when forced, or when it is still the stale one a follower watched.§13
cld.cloudTakeLease

No cloud copy answers `{ ok: true, absent }` and an lz1 copy `{ ok: true, legacy }`, with no lease written. Otherwise it writes a new lease (`leaseFor`) and returns it with the head, or `{ ok: false, holder, head }` while another device holds it. Another device's live lease is free only `skewMs` (5 min) past its `until`, which is the holder's clock.

  • `ifLease` is a lease a read-only follower saw unchanged for a whole TTL of its own clock; it is taken only if the same epoch and `until` are still there, so a renewal that landed meanwhile wins. A lease let go to an asker (`to`) who never took it falls back the same way (SYNC-PLAN §6).
cloudRenewLease(uid, id, epoch, opts)The holder's beat: extends its lease `ttl` past now in a transaction and reports another device's `want`.§13
cld.cloudRenewLease

Refuses (`{ ok: false, lost, holder }`) when the lease is no longer `epoch` or was let go (`until` 0), and answers `absent` when the copy is gone. The session calls it every 20 s while visible; each renewal sets `until` 90 s past the holder's clock (`LEASE_TTL_MS`), and another device treats the lease as dead unasked only 5 min past that (`leaseState`) or after watching it unchanged for 90 s of its own clock (`CanvasSession._maybeTake`).

cloudReleaseLease(uid, id, epoch, opts)Lets go of the pen by setting the lease's `until` to 0, if the lease is still `epoch`; `to` reserves it for the device that asked.§13
cld.cloudReleaseLease

The lease record stays, `want` included, so the device that asked sees the release on its manifest watch. The session's hand-over (`_handToDevice`) passes the asker as `to`, and `leaseState` then answers `reserved` (not free) to every other device, the releasing one included. Returns whether it wrote.

cloudAskLease(uid, id, who, opts)"Edit here" from another device: takes the pen at once when free, otherwise writes `want` onto the holder's lease.§13
cld.cloudAskLease

Free is `leaseState`'s: another device's live lease counts as free only 5 min past its `until`. The holder sees `want` on its manifest watch or its next beat, pushes and lets go; the asker takes the lease anyway after a wait (`CanvasSession.takeOver`). Returns `{ ok, lease, head }` or `{ ok: false, asked, holder, head }`.

cloudWatchManifest(uid, id, onChange, onError)Subscribes to one canvas's manifest, calling `onChange` with it (or null) on every change; returns the unsubscribe.§13
cld.cloudWatchManifest

How the holder sees a `want` or a lost lease, and a read-only device sees the head move, between beats.

cloud/store2.js · gzip.js · lzWorker.js 62 + 39 + 90 lines

The kobin-2 store as cloud chunks and back: one chunk per frame snapshot or run of log entries, split into 700 KiB parts. Pure and lossless (DESIGN.md §13). The cloud chunks' compression: the browser's own gzip stream, raw where it is missing, never lz-string (OPEN-FLAGS F64). The diagnostic report uses it too. lz-string in a Web Worker, for the old lz1 cloud copy that a canvas still in the v1 local store writes and old copies are read from; the main thread only where there is no worker.

Throws on a chunk of another kind, or on an entry whose span falls outside the array.

Cuts a gzipped chunk into parts of at most 700 KiB for Firestore's 1 MiB document cap; always at least one.

Pages · App 5 files · 1,952 lines

The routes, the gallery, the editor. None of it holds geometry.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
App()The router: seven routes, four of them developer-only.§13
app.App

Hash routing, because the app is served as static files and a hash route needs no server rewrite for every depth of URL.

  • The canvas route is KEYED on the canvas id, so moving between canvases remounts the editor and with it the engine and its autosave slot. Without the key React reuses the element and the second canvas opens inside the first one's engine.
CanvasEditor()THE PRODUCT.§13
edt.CanvasEditor

The tool rail, the scenes panel, the scale HUD and the set-scale flow, the save, delete and keep-draft dialogs, the save bar, the sync status button in the title chip, the sync banner and the session's notices under the top bar (a notice about the pen moving is left to the banner, `showsNotice`), and the developer panel behind `?dev`. At a phone's width (`useNarrow`) the status button is an icon only and the title chip stops short of the top-right group.

  • The cloud side is one `CanvasSession` per open canvas, started once the document is restored and sign-in has resolved (after 3 s it starts signed out): the device lock and cloud lease, the decision at open (push, pull or keep both), one push at a time, following another tab or device while read-only, and the hand-over (DESIGN.md §13).
  • The engine is gated: read-only and not saving until the session holds the pen. Every tool but pan is disabled while read-only, which includes before the session starts. Leaving never offers to keep or discard a draft from a read-only tab, nor for a canvas the bin holds as a whole store (deleted elsewhere while open, `isBinnedStore`). A write the store refuses (another tab's, or ahead of this document) goes to the session (`onRefused`), which keeps the work in memory as a new canvas.
  • The parts worth knowing: the save path serialises independently of whether the local write succeeded, so a full browser storage cannot take the cloud down with it; the session's dirty flag is driven off DOCUMENT CHANGES rather than off a successful local save, for the same reason; and the save notice is dismissible per KIND, so waving away 'autosave is off' does not also silence a real failure later.
ScaleValueDialog({ ... })'This length equals...' - where a drag becomes a real-world scale.§14
edt.ScaleValueDialog

The one place a drawing is connected to physical units. Its unit grid walks the same rung machinery as the HUD picker, starting at the everyday span.

CanvasesV2()THE GALLERY.§13
gal.CanvasesV2

Sign-in, the local and cloud listings merged by freshest timestamp, a one-way catch-up upload of canvases the account has not seen, tombstone propagation so a deletion elsewhere reaches this browser (one canvas at a time: each move rewrites the bin's index, and two at once can drop a row), rename, duplicate, download, delete, the recycle bin, and file import.

  • The merge is the interesting part and it is deliberately asymmetric: a canvas this device has and the account does not is uploaded, but a canvas the account has TOMBSTONED is not - otherwise a stale device would resurrect everything anyone had deleted.
  • The merged list shows before the catch-up, which can take minutes on a big canvas: one canvas at a time, a kobin-2 store as its chunks (`cloudPushSource`, never its JSON: F64), a v1 canvas as its document. A development build skips the catch-up, since its collection starts empty and would receive every local canvas (DESIGN.md §13).

11 Not running

In the tree, imported by nothing that ships

Why this section exists

src/engine/__oracles__/ holds independent implementations the shipping code is checked against — the retired pre-lattice engine, the cubic perimeter, the rasteriser's coverage, the scene index by brute force — and two test-only residues, cede.js and erase.js, whose headers say so. Only test suites reach any of it, so webpack never bundles it. Production code must never import from here: an oracle the engine depends on has stopped being one (DESIGN.md §15).

KobinEngineV0.js 1,151 lines

oracle The retired pre-lattice engine, kept as the golden oracle the current one is compared against. Not on any route.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§
KobinEngineV0The retired god-class engine.§17
v0.KobinEngineV0

Everything the current engine splits across LevelMap, Document, Camera, TileStore and Renderer, in one file, with live projection instead of bidirectional tiles.

  • Kept as the golden oracle: `derive.test.js` requires `deriveStep` to equal `_deriveInto` on the same inputs, which is what makes the extraction provable rather than asserted. With the `legacyOffset` branch of `derive.bandRings` that comparison walks, it is what keeps `clipper-lib` in the dependency list (DESIGN.md §15).
KobinEngineV0.constructor(container, opts)Builds the retired engine: a Two.js scene of three groups, the camera, per-level natives, crossing records, tile caches and tool state.§17
v0.KobinEngineV0.constructor

Level 0 holds the originals; `levelObjects` is each level's render list; `crossings` pin each level's frame on first entry; `tiles` caches each level's derived content per grid cell. It also keeps a perf ring and a projection cache, and puts the Clipper and polyline helpers on `geom` for scripted tests.

The single tolerance that turned out to bind the whole cubic bake. Every point of an offset piece sits at exactly the pen radius from its own generator, so an exposed piece reads exactly r and a buried one dips below; a fragment between two close crossings dips only a little, and a coarse oracle reads it as exposed.

  • Measured: at r/512 the resolve left 122 open chains, at r/4096 twenty-five, at r/32768 none. That is not a tolerance wanting tuning, and it is why the arc pipeline's oracle is closed-form instead.

Each chord is filed in every cell within r of it, so a burial query reads one cell. It takes no cubics for the bakers that grow it one cubic at a time with `addCubic`.

Subdivision returns the centre of the last surviving box, and its two halves are centres of DIFFERENT boxes - one per curve. For a shallow crossing they land far apart; measured at 1.10 units on a ring, over the welding tolerance, so the two pieces cut there never joined.

  • This is F15's second defect, and the class of problem that does not exist once both curves are arcs.

cvp.cubicIntersections

Near-tangent pairs produce a cluster of boxes rather than one crossing; unmerged, they cut a piece into slivers whose midpoints all classify the same way.

Straight cubics are offset along their end tangents so they meet fitted neighbours without a step; a tangent break gets a round join on both sides, the inner one buried and culled later. A `live` mask skips cubics whose offsets cannot reach the boundary.

Each meets its side chain tangentially - a semicircle leaves the offset perpendicular to the centerline, which is exactly the direction the offset arrives in - so cap junctions are smooth rather than corners.

Both sides plus both caps, as one loop.

Where the centerline turns, the outer offsets leave a gap at the shared anchor and the boundary genuinely runs round it at the pen radius.

  • The arc pipeline has no equivalent: consecutive offsets there share an endpoint computed once per vertex, so there is no gap to fill.

A circular arc as kappa cubics, under 90 degrees each.

The clock for the resolve's phase timings: `performance.now()` where it exists.

marginOf(...)How strict burial has to be, given where the boundary might really be.§17

Two error terms: the fitted offset can sit a fit-tolerance inside the true one, and the oracle's chords read short by their own tolerance. With no margin a legitimate boundary point lands exactly on the threshold - F15's third defect.

Every baker that builds its own oracle has to agree with the one the resolve would have built, or it is measuring a different shape.

buildTolFor(...)The tolerance the perimeter is BUILT at, given the tolerance it must MEET.§17
cvp.buildTolFor

Divides by eight and floors at a fraction of the radius. The floor is what matters: at a crossing of angle theta a fitting error is displaced along the curve by one over sin theta, so the amplification is geometric rather than absolute.

  • Shared, because B computing its own was enough to make it disagree with A by 187 points out of 2,056 while A was exact.
repairTolFor(...)How far a junction may be welded shut.§17
cvp.repairTolFor

Empirical, and it has to be. The displacement to be closed is not predictable from the tolerances - which is itself the argument that the parity weld was load-bearing rather than tidying, and therefore that the representation was wrong.

The cubic pipeline's whole bake, and the direct ancestor of `bakeArcPerimeter`. Same three phases - build the boundary, cut it at its own crossings, keep what is not buried, restitch - with every step approximate rather than exact.

  • Measured against its replacement on the same strokes: 3.3 to 3.8 times slower, and where it left open chains the arc version leaves none.

cvp.dropHairlines

A doubled-back strip paints nothing, so dropping it changes no pixel. Exported so the batch and incremental schedules filter the same way; the perimeter is measured on four chords a cubic.

test only What is left of the superseded “a cut is a recipe every bake re-runs” model.

FunctionWhat it does in the design§

ers.cutVisible

The same gate the window machinery uses. Coarser than a fraction of a pixel and the ink around the cut is equally sub-pixel, so cut and uncut agree - which is what made zooming out across a crossing continuous with no re-baking.

eraserFootprint(E, cfg)The eraser's painted footprint, as curve loops local to its own centre.§17
ers.eraserFootprint

An eraser IS a stroke, so it is polygonised by the same rule ink strokes are: above the fat gate its outline is CURVES, which is what let the same cut be re-flattened at whatever fidelity the consuming level needed.

  • Local coordinates were not a detail: Clipper caps its integer scale by the largest coordinate present, so building a 32-unit eraser at frame coordinate 1e5 quantised it to about 0.0025 units.

Naive on purpose: the rasteriser deposits a run's two ends and lets a running sum fill the interior, and the oracle must not share that step.

ringsArea(rings)The exact signed area of a set of rings, by the shoelace formula.§17
cov.ringsArea

Positive is clockwise on a y-down screen; a ring `strokeStripNear` emits comes out negative.

ringsFromLoops(loops, tol)Rings from loops in the stored grammar, arcs sampled from their own centre and angles within `tol`, for the two functions above.§17
cov.ringsFromLoops

Reads the raw numbers (a `Loop`'s `buf` or an array), all four piece codes. Sampling from the centre is allowed here and forbidden to the rasteriser, which is why this is not the reference for a far-centre arc: the arc suite checks those against the exact contour.

frameMap(frames, from, to)The similarity between two frames, walked up from one to the common ancestor and down to the other; no Horner offsets, no cache.§17
sor.frameMap

The similarity between two frames, walked up from one to the common ancestor and down to the other; no Horner offsets, no cache.

SceneOracleThe scene index's rules by brute force, which `sceneIndex.test.js` runs beside SceneIndex on the same batches and compares after every one.§17
sor.SceneOracle

Every distance is an all-pairs scan in a frame the pair shares, every stray run is recomputed when read, every split is a full labelling; no grids, anchors, origins or caches. It covers frames (those that went included), items, closed loops, erase hints, re-joins, heirs, renames, names kept aside and the list's echo rows; not restores, parts, regions or the saved state.

  • Test-only: production never imports `__oracles__`.

_merge(A, B)Two scenes become one under the winner's identity, the loser's kept aside; with no anchors, nothing is re-filed.§17
sor._merge

Two scenes become one under the winner's identity, the loser's kept aside; with no anchors, nothing is re-filed.

_sceneOf(x)The scene holding an item, by scanning every scene.§17
sor._sceneOf

The scene holding an item, by scanning every scene.

_insert(x)The insert rule by brute force: every chunk against every chunk of each range-compatible scene; the group of touched chunks touching most decides, and its scenes merge while the range fits.§17
sor._insert

Touched chunks fewer than STRAY_CHUNKS apart are one group, around a closed loop's start too, built by union-find independently of SceneIndex's `chunkRuns`; a tie goes to the group holding the lowest chunk.

_split(S)The split check by full labelling over all member pairs: the heaviest component keeps the identity (tie: the smallest id), the others get new ids in order of their smallest id.§17
sor._split

The split check by full labelling over all member pairs: the heaviest component keeps the identity (tie: the smallest id), the others get new ids in order of their smallest id.

_rejoin(S, own)A scene moved whole merges with every range-compatible scene its moved ink (`own`, all its members by default) touches, valid chunk to valid chunk, oldest first.§17
sor._rejoin

A scene moved whole merges with every range-compatible scene its moved ink (`own`, all its members by default) touches, valid chunk to valid chunk, oldest first.

_root()The root frame's id: the first frame with no parent.§17
sor._root

The root frame's id: the first frame with no parent.

apply(batch)One batch by SceneIndex's rules and order: frames, placed items (rigid or re-inserted), removals with pieces filed back and split checks, inserts in id order, re-joins, heirs, renames, reclaimed names.§17
sor.apply

A frame that went carries the names kept aside in it, and scenes' last frames, up the old tree to a frame that stayed. `attr` records (z only) are skipped; a record's `loops` travel with its chunks, as in SceneIndex. A rigid move (every member that stays, moved by one displacement) is measured in the root frame against each item's position at the end of the last batch (`was`); each scene then holding that ink re-joins through it alone.

  • An emptied scene keeps its name aside with the frame and range it had then, unless members that moved away emptied it and gather in a scene born this batch, which takes its id and name. Returns `result()`.
_translated(a, b, wa, wb)Is `b` the chunks of `a` shifted by one displacement? The same test as SceneIndex's.§17
sor._translated

Is `b` the chunks of `a` shifted by one displacement? The same test as SceneIndex's.

_reclaim()Scenes born this batch take a kept-aside name whose frame they cover by MATCH_OVERLAP with a compatible range, best cover first.§17
sor._reclaim

Scenes born this batch take a kept-aside name whose frame they cover by MATCH_OVERLAP with a compatible range, best cover first.

result()What the test compares: per scene id, its name, whether it was renamed, its sorted member ids, its parent, and `row`, the id of the panel row it is listed under.§17
sor.result

The parent is the scene with the smallest Lmax above its own whose frame holds its centre. Rows are folded by the echo rule restated: top-down, the nearest ancestor's row (up to ECHO_UP) whose smallest frame and the scene's hold each other's centres within ECHO_ZOOM, the row spanning at most 16× and holding one renamed scene at most; a row's id is its renamed member's, else its first's.

  • Also records each scene's frame and range, for the names kept aside in the next batch.
